preText:
8.01pm The two umpires finally emerge. Deepak Chahar has the new ball in hand. Let there be swing. One slip in lace. Third is inside the circle

8pm Let the IPL 2024 begin. Virat Kohli and Faf du Plessis to open the innings for RCB. The fielders are ready and in position, but we don't have any umpires

7.50pm Now for the teams.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru F du Plessis*, V Kohli, RM Patidar, GJ Maxwell, C Green, KD Karthik†, Anuj Rawat, KV Sharma, AS Joseph, MJ Dagar, Mohammed Siraj

Impact: Dayal, Akash, Prabhudessai, Swapnil, Vyshak

Chennai Super Kings RD Gaikwad*, R Ravindra, AM Rahane, DJ Mitchell, RA Jadeja, Sameer Rizvi, MS Dhoni†, DL Chahar, M Theekshana, TU Deshpande, Mustafizur Rahman

Impact: Thakur, Dube, Rasheed, Sindhu, Moeen

7.40pm Faf du Plessis has won the toss, and RCB are batting first. "Generally it is always a bat-first wicket," says du Plessis, who knows the ground well as a former CSK player.

Gaikwad says he came to know he would be the captain a week ago. CSK's four overseas players are Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Maheesh Theekshana and Mustafizur Rahamn. He also says Sameer Rizvi is making his debut.

7.35pm Conditions report time. Brian Lara says there are a few cracks, and there is some looseness on the edges of the crack. Lara feels spin is going to play a part. I think they are playing on the centre strip because there is no one boundary that is bigger. Lara still feels you bowl first despite the expectation of spin because you want to protect them from the dew.

7.30pm The toss has been delayed to 7.40pm even though the captains have been out and ready. The start time stays at 8pm.

Deivarayan Mathu has seen Alzarri Joseph mark his run-up. Like Faf du Plessis, Joseph is also a Super Kings man, who unfortunately will play against them in the IPL. Deivarayan points out how du Plessis has liked to play Joseph both for St Lucia Kings and Joburg Super Kings.

7.25pm All eyes on two men who haven't played in a while. Virat Kohli more so because not just RCB fans but also India fans want to see how he responds to the latest demands the India team seems to have made of him in T20 cricket. And MS Dhoni of course, who has again found a way to surprise people after all these years.

7.20pm I am sure you have heard about it, but this is worth checking out again. Ask Star on ESPNcricinfo: Got a question for the Star Sports commentators about this match? Want to ask Navjot Sidhu, Ambati Rayudu or Harbhajan Singh about anything cricket? Go to the ESPNcricinfo homepage on the mobile site, click on the Ask Star button at the bottom of the screen, and send in your questions. They could get answered on TV.

7pm How ya doin'? Thanks Ashish. If I was in the Chennai crowd, I would carry a "Hinthi nahi ata saar" placard. Anyway, this too shall pass. A timely reminder that because of this ceremony, this match will start at 8pm. All other matches will sart at the usual time of 7.30pm. Toss in half an hour.

ShahSafeer: "People are here to see the start of another blockbuster season of IPL while I am here ro see Virat Kohli bat again. It seems like it's been ages since he last batted! "

Our hindi commentary is live as well, while Deiva has kicked off the live blog, too. And with that, please welcome Sidharth Monga in the comms seat.

Ask Star on ESPNcricinfo: Got a question for the Star Sports commentators about this match? Want to ask Navjot Sidhu, Ambati Rayudu or Harbhajan Singh about anything cricket? Go to the ESPNcricinfo homepage on the mobile site, click on the Ask Star button at the bottom of the screen, and send in your questions. They could get answered on TV.

Aaron: "RCB will be looking to groom Himanshu as their designated Leggie this season, would love to see him spin his magic wand in Chepauk!"

6.45pm The opening ceremony is underway. Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff making their way to the stage. Meanwhile, I have just spotted two RCB jerseys amid the sea of yellow! While the celebs do their thing how about some light reading from Alagappan Muthu: ChatIPL - An AI-powered peek at the league that defies logic. There is a also a pretty fascinating interview with Daryl Mitchell from Deivarayan and Alagappan where he opens up on what it was travelling around with his dad, John Mitchell - a world-class rugby coach.

Soumya: "Better to error towards caution. RCB can go with Dagar, Karn and Lormor as 3 spinners apart from Maxi on this pitch. They have the pacers and batting to breach casa Chepauk."

6.30pm If you want to know what's it like at Chepauk right now, Deiva sets it up beautifully from the venue. "He has handed over captaincy to Gaikwad, but he's still Chennai's Thala. The chants of "Dhoni!Dhoni!Dhoni!" and the whistles for him are getting louder and louder. It looks very much like these 14 matches - 16 or 17 if luck is once again on his side - are very much the beginning of the end. At the same time, the crowd is warming up to the new captain Gaikwad. Once, another Gaikwad with Maharashtrian roots, a certain Shivaji Rao, went on to become a household name in Chennai. That's some way away, but for now Gaikwad has the keys to the Chennai kingdom. A huge replica of the IPL trophy now makes its way into the middle. The LED lights are also being tested out ahead of the opening ceremony, which will include performances of AR Rahman and Prabhu Deva."

6.25pm The last time CSK and RCB played the opening game of an IPL season, RCB were rolled over for 70, and it took CSK 17.4 overs to chase the target down. RCB will want to right that wrong. But can they? CSK have three spin options in Maheesh Theekshana, Ravindra Jadeja and part-timer Rachin Ravindra on what could be another slow pitch. In contrast, RCB don't have a world-class spinner in their ranks. Here's Deivarayan Muthu with the match preview.

Pawas: "The first true transitional season of IPL is about to kick off" Really feels that way, isn't? The first time ever in the IPL that none of Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma or MS Dhoni will be leading a team.

6.10pm We are still close to two hours away from ball one, but Chepauk is already half full and it shouldn't take long for the stadium to be packed to the rafters. And make no mistake, it's going to be a sea of Yellow at the Chepauk. There will be an opening ceremony with all the glitz and glamour in full flow. Once the dust settles, RCB will try and get the better of CSK at a venue where they haven't had a lot of success. In fact, just once in nine attempts - that one coming way back in 2008. Can they change history?

Afeef: "And so begins another season of the IPL. Looking forward to a fantastic season. May or not be Dhoni's last, but we know he will get the loudest cheer everywhere he goes."

5.55pm There is a also a small matter of Virat Kohli returning to competitive cricket after close to two-and-a-half months having missed India's five-game Test series against England. His most recent game was a T20I against Afghanistan in mid-January. How he goes in Chennai will be interesting to see, especially with the T20 World Cup starting right after the IPL.

5.40pm Righto, where do we start. The latest captaincy change is a good place, I reckon. A day before the IPL begins, defending champions CSK have a new captain - Ruturaj Gaikwad. Yep. And as with most things with Dhoni: It happened quietly. A whisper into the ether. Just like it did in 2014. And then in 2020. The end of an era. MS Dhoni's last act as captain was lifting the IPL trophy. His most lasting act, subverting expectation. Here's Alagappan Muthu on how as a season begins, an era ends, but life goes on for Dhoni.

5.30pm IPL S17 E01. Ten months on since that crazy final in Ahmedabad which started on a Sunday and ended on a Tuesday, we are back it again. Ten venues. Ten teams. New captains. Comebacks. Fanwars. The carnival returns. Hello and welcome to the ball-by-ball commentary of match No. 1 of IPL 2024 - MS Dhoni Ruturaj Gaikwad-led CSK vs Faf du Plessis-led RCB. I am Ashish Pant nice and early and will soon be joined by Sidharth Monga with all that unfolds in Chennai. Join in, it's going to be a fun ride.

postText:
IPL 2024 gets off to a rousing start with CSK getting the better of RCB at Chepauk yet again. If you missed any of the action, Deiva's report will be in soon. That's it from us tonight. Thanks everyone for tuning in. It's a double-header tomorrow and we will be live nice and early to bring all the action. Till then, this is me Ashish signing off on behalf of Sidharth, Thilak and Chandan. Ciao!

Mustafizur Rahman is the player of the match for his 4 for 29.

CSK captain, Ruturaj Gaikwad: Total control right from the start. 2-3 overs here and there but once the spinners came on, we were in control. 10-15 runs lesser would have been great but they came back well. [Turning point?] To get Maxwell and even Faf out, the quick wickets were the turning point. Helps to control the next five-six overs. That was the main point. [Captaincy debut] I have always enjoyed it. Haven't felt the additional pressure, right from the state side. Not even a single time I felt pressurized by anything. Obviously had Mahi bhai with me. [On the chase] Everyone is a stroke-player in our side, even Jinx. There is role clarity in the batting unit. Helps a lot. Lots of positives, but two-three things to work on. The batting, everyone chipped in. If we had a few batters from the top-order batting through, the chase would have been easier.

Presentation time.

Some stat nuggets from Sampath:

- This is the 8th consecutive win for CSK vs RCB at Chepauk, the longest winning streak for any team against an opponent at a venue in IPL. Next best streak is for MI, who have won their last seven matches vs KKR at Wankhede.

- Ravindra Jadeja unbeaten in a successful IPL chase for the 27th time, joint-most by any batter, alongside MS Dhoni.

Amey: "Credit to Jadeja for playing only 2 dot balls and keeping the scoreboard moving, especially when Dube was struggling."

Afeef: "RCB needed a better plan than just bowling short balls. Alzarri could've been used better, I feel."

Rachin Ravindra: Pretty complete performance by us. We held our nerves. Batting with Jinx [Rahane] and Rutu, very calm heads. Lucky we had 4-5 days of good training. I find it easier going from red ball to white ball because I think the positions are the same, [Form] It's been good. The wickets were a bit different in training but I backed myself in the game. The experience of the amazing crowd was great. Helps a lot.

Faf du Plessis: You have to get ahead in the first six overs. Chennai squeeze you with their spinners. We lost too many wickets in the first six overs. We were 15-20 runs short on a pitch that wasn't as bad as we played in the first ten overs We were always a little bit behind trying to get ahead of the game. They were always ahead of the game. [Short ball plan] Dube wasn't comfortable with the short ball, we were trying to get a few wickets in the middle overs. But didn't happen. [Batting first] If you look at the stats, it is very in favour of batting first. It looked a bit on the drier side. The spinners, in the second innings, the ball started to grip a bit. We backed our seamers against Dube. But batting first was the right decision. [On DK and Rawat] Really good for Dinesh setting up the season for someone who hasn't really played a lot of cricket in the last year. Really important knock for himself. Rawat showed some really promise even last year. He showed composure.

11.55pmAnd the wait continues. That is eight wins on the bounce for CSK against RCB at Chepauk. And a clinical win it was to kick-off IPL 2024. It was Rachin Ravindra, on IPL debut, who gave the chase a flying start with a 15-ball 37. Rahane also did his bit scoring a quick 27. RCB did come back into the game with a few quick wickets as they adopted the short ball plan. But I felt they over-did it. Dube was clearly struggling initially, but once he survived, run-scoring was easy. Jadeja did his bit in rotating the strike, and eventually CSK got home with eight balls to spare. While RCB's middle order collapsed, CSK had all their batters contributing. And that was the difference between the two teams.

postText:
Pant's return game was fun. He didn't get a big score but looked happy and healthy, which has been the theme leading up to now. Hope that continues and that Ishant's fine. Updates will be in about that soon and you'll be able to check it out here. If Kings manage to get most from their resources, they'll have a good season. For now, the second game's started. KKR are struggling against SRH. Do follow that, and take care.

Sujit: "So Porel's innings ensures that Delhi don't take a big NRR hit. But they really need to spruce their bowling. I mean Khaleel and Marsh as front line bowlers is an invitation to the opposition to indulge themselves."

Sam Curran, POTM: Really pleased, didn't know how the ground would play. Amazing way to start. Nothing better than starting with a win at home. [Chat when Axar, Kuldeep were bowling] Those two are world-class bowlers and play a lot of cricket for India, thought we could take it deep with them being a bowler down. We were in a good position, and then to be with my great mate Liam, was pretty special. [Surviving the dropped chance] At that stage, you gotta take those risks, thankfully luck was on my side there. I knew after surviving it, one of us had to take it to the end Thought the wicket got better under lights, was a good pitch. Ground was big but the ball was travelling well, not much spin and ball was coming on nicely from the pacers. [Did you ask Dhawan for more overs] We got some great options, nice additions too, maybe it'll be different in Bangalore. Most importantly, we won.

Shikhar Dhawan, Kings captain: Feels great, happy to be on the ground. I've been preparing for this tournament, this is the first time I'm playing at this high a level since the last IPL. I was a bit nervous as well but yeah, came through. No chat in the innings break after the 25-run over because I was preparing to bat. Also, bowlers will be going through their own emotions. So I would rather give them space and chat after things calm down. I felt we leaked a few extra runs, of course extra nerves are there in the first match. It's normal. Felt the wicket got better under lights, we got a good start and Sam played an amazing innings. Livingstone finished it nicely. [Decision to bowl first] I didn't know the records here, it's a new ground. So didn't focus on it too much, we practiced during day and at night. Thought we'd let the other team use their brains first and then we'll assess it. It worked for us, so we're happy and content.

Machakaari : "DC didn't win the crucial moments. But for Kuldeep and Axar,Their bowling looks seriously weak. Fielding below par to say the least" I still can't get over Warner dropping a catch.

Rishabh Pant, DC captain: Ishant's injury was clearly evident because we were anyway one player short because we lagged with the batting a bit. Abhishek came in and chipped in with a few runs which were crucial. We were short on extra bowling. We actually pulled it back in the end [but couldn't complete the job], part and parcel of the game. [Batting] Personally I was pretty nervous but you have to go through this when you enter the field. This isn't the first time being nervous, but happy about that [return overall]. I think we had a par score but because we were one bowler short, because of an injury, can't do much about it. Wicket played as we expected to play, can't make excuses. We will learn from it but having one bowler short is never good. End of the day, well played to them [Kings] I guess. Porel's finish helped us finish on a high. It was an amazing innings, congrats to him. I think it's just his third or fourth game but the kind of impact he made was huge. Really looking forward [to seeing him] this season.

7:19pm It was a seesaw battle but Kings were often in front. For Capitals, Ishant twisting an ankle in the field was a big blow. Especially since it was in the sixth over. The bowlers, Marsh and Khaleel in particular, not coming good cost them. Curran, pushed up to No. 4, was spectacular. Bairstow and Dhawan gave Kings a decent start but fell quickly, so Curran held the innings together amid Kuldeep looking threatening as ever. Axar was trying his best to play a holding role. Sumit, who had to be brought in, was expensive. Curran and Livingstone used the short boundary to their advantage, especially when it was behind them and the bowlers went short. Capitals pulled it back a bit late in the innings, Khaleel got Curran but it wasn't enough with Livingstone and his clean hitting taking the hosts home, in their new home.

Afeef: "Last season Livingstone played one of his best T20 knocks against DC but PBKS failed to get over the line. I'm glad he could finish off this chase against DC today."

Kolkata Knight Riders: 1 Venkatesh Iyer, 2 Phil Salt (wk), 3 Shreyas Iyer (capt), 4 Rinku Singh, 5 Nitish Rana, 6 Sunil Narine, 7 Andre Russell, 8 Ramandeep Singh, 9 Mitchell Starc, 10 Harshit Rana, 11 Varun Chakravarthy. The impact-sub options are Suyash, Pandey, Arora, Raghuvanshi and Gurbaz.

Sunrisers Hyderabad: 1 Mayank Agarwal, 2 Rahul Tripathi, 3 Aiden Markram, 4 Heinrich Klaasen (wk), 5 Abdul Samad, 6 Shahbaz Ahmed, 7 Marco Jansen, 8 Pat Cummins (capt), 9 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 10 Mayank Markande, 11 T Natarajan. The impact-sub options are Reddy, Washington, Malik, Phillips and Abhishek.

7pm It is windy at Eden, as we get set for the toss. SRH win the toss and bowl first. Pat Cummins says T20 "is pretty quick", and so he'll have to think on his feet when it comes to captaincy in this format. His other three overseas players are Markram, Klassen and Jansen. Meanwhile, home captain Shreyas Iyer is greeted by a roar, and says his back "feels fantastic". He refers to the team sheet, and says his overseas quartet is Salt, Narine, Russell and Starc.

6.45pm Steven Smith - yes, him! - who is one of the experts at ESPNcricinfo for this IPL, gets his prediction meter ticking. He forecasts Starc's wicket tally, IPL 2024's MVP and much more. And if you're wondering what made Smith guess that number for Starc, here's Sid Monga's analysis on the constant and universal appeal of Starc.

There are some subplots which will be taking shape at Eden Gardens tonight, with Shreyas Iyer's return, and Cummins vs Starc being two of them, as Hemant Brar's preview reminds us. As for the two most expensive buys in IPL history, Cummins, who is Starc's captain at Australia, says it will be "weird seeing him in the other dugout".

6.30pm They come very rapidly in the IPL - like sharp, rising waves in the sea. Only last night we were in Chennai, the southern part of the country; and even before the action in Mullanpur, the northern corner, is wrapped, we are all but readying ourselves for a game in Kolkata in the east. This is Himanshu saying hello ahead of the third game this season, with Alan, who is busy munching lunch, set to join me soon.

preText: Cummins
postText:
A game which could have gone anywhere. In what was typical modern hitting, Russell hammered 64* off 25 balls, and Klaasen hit back with 63 from 29. KKR were 51 for 4 at one stage, before going on to post 208; SRH required 60 in the last three overs, but fell just four short. Exceptional T20 batting from both sides! And with this thriller, we wrap the double-header Saturday up. Join us for another two games tomorrow, as this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Raghav and Alan. Good night!

Andre Russell is the Player of the Match: "Sometimes I realise how I'm striking the ball... I just try to react to whatever comes my way. Over the last year or two, bowlers have been exceptionally good to me. I'm still figuring out how to score. I realise everyone is coming to me with a plan. I've been a permanent fixture in the XI [since making it there]. What I did tonight is just to say 'keep supporting'. I am happy to contribute with this jersey on. Harshit's body language was on point in the last over; he wanted the ball. If he was shying away from it, it could have gone their way. With the first ball gone for six, he still got the job done."

Shreyas Iyer, KKR captain: "Right from the 17th over I had butterflies in the stomach! To be honest, I thought anything can happen in the last over. Harshit was a bit nervous when he was coming to bowl [the last over]. I told him, 'Even if we lose, it's fine'. I tried to calm him down as much as possible. Narine and Russell have got such experience. Elated to see how Russell performed with bat and ball. Sunny executed well. It is a luxury to have them in the team. Whenever you start with a win, it gives you motivation. There are areas we need to improve on as a team - fielding is one of them!"

Time for the presentations

Afeef: "This game boiled down to Russell vs Klaasen, the two most destructive batsmen from both the squads today"

Ramandeep Singh: "I was really enjoying my time in the middle. Trying to play with intent. All thanks to Gauti paaji and Abhishek Nayar sir. I was striking pretty well in domestic cricket. The way these guys have backed me is tremendous. I really want to play like that (like Russell!). Maybe one day I will play like that! The plan was that Klaasen was really hitting the pace ball. So the message was to take pace off. I really loved the atmosphere at the ground."

Pat Cummins, SRH captain: "Close game in the end. Wonderful game of cricket; unfortunately didn't go our way. Dre Russ did what he does best. You do your planning, and you try to execute your plans. But he's a pretty tough guy to bowl to. Tough job in cricket to bowl to someone like him. It's one of those ones which goes one way or the other. Who would have thought we would have got that close? Unfortunately, a bit too much. Lots to be encouraged by. A couple of points to work on also."

Joel Mick: "There's something that even Cummins can't do!"

Karthik: "Jailbreak :)"

11.25pm The heart rates rose and fell in the final over, which started with SRH requiring 13. The first ball went for six, and thereafter, it was all KKR, as Harshit got Shahbaz, who was playing second fiddle, and Klaasen, who threatened to do the impossible. Before the last over began, Klaasen and Shahbaz had pumped 63 off the three overs just before that. It seemed like KKR were running out of ideas, but just then, Harshit came out with his magical slower balls to deny a rampaging Klaasen, who continues his dream run in this part of the world. Hang around for the presentations.

The first game of the double-header Sunday is wrapped up, as RR beat LSG by 20 runs. But the action shifts to Ahmedabad, where Pandya's GT host Pandya's MI. That is it from us from Jaipur this evening, as this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Raghav, Thilak and Ekanth! Good night!

Sanju Samson is the Player of the Match for his 82*: "It's always great fun to spend time in the middle. This time I have been a different role, with a slightly different combination. Sanga has given me suggestions... I have been playing IPL for ten years, so there's experience coming in. Good start, but let's see how it goes. In our view, we were ten short. It was a good pitch; it tends to get better here. I went for 12 off the first ball I bowled! I bowl in different stages of the game. The body is ageing. Requires different mindset. I came from a Test series. I went for 15 in the first over - that was inside the powerplay. The moment that phase of the game is done, I try to shell it away. The next three overs of mine went for 20, and I got a wicket... Most importantly, [it is about] preparing for every single batter in the opposition. The game is built by perception. Sandeep has been an unsung hero. He stepped up for Prasidh last year. He is a character; it's about the fight they have. A bowler for a fight is way more valuable than a bowler with a skill. There are two bouncers to be used, and that's the only fillip the bowlers have got in this competition. Boulty's very aggressive up front, and so is Nandre."

KL Rahul, LSG captain: "I don't think the target was a lot; it was just ten over-par. We bowled well in patches. Not making too much out of it. Just made a few mistakes. Mohsin was our powerplay bowler in the first season, but he wasn't fully fit last season. Good to see him back. Naveen has been crucial for us since he has come in. Powerplay is crucial for every team, and I don't think any team has cracked it yet. We'll made from the small mistakes we made. When we are three [down] for nothing, and we give ourselves a chance of chasing 194 speaks of our line-up... We need to find ways to win games of cricket. We'll try to build from here, and see where we can get stronger. Langer's brought a lot of calmness to the group. I stole his line when I said we need to find ways to win games of cricket. We enjoy having him around. All of us have watched him coach Australia to a T20 World Cup and an Ashes victory. When you get runs, you always feel good. But it's important for us to end up on the winning side. That gives more satisfaction. Missing a season was really painful."

7.23pm LSG needed another 49 from the last 24 balls, with Rahul and Pooran well set and ready to smash. That is when Sandeep Sharma struck, and pushed LSG back against the wall. His first over had gone for only five, and he started the death overs with Rahul's wicket. Rahul took his time to score 58, and eventually, it was too much to do for even Pooran, who was much brighter with 64* in 41 balls. RR seemed to have lost their way after they had LSG at 11 for 3 and then 60 for 4, but Sandeep, who finished with 1 for 22 in three overs, was spot on when required. Hang around for the presentations.

6.30pm Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of today's blockbuster clash between Gujarat Titans and Mumbai Indians - or as I am going to refer to it this season (at least), the 'Hardik Pandya derby'. For the uninitiated, Hardik Pandya's career was launched by Mumbai Indians, following which he has gone on to earn a superstar status. Then, released by Mumbai Indians, he joined Gujarat Titans as their captain for the franchise's first year. He led them to the title in their maiden season and to the final again last year. Now he has returned to Mumbai Indians in an all-cash trade, and has replaced Rohit Sharma as their captain.

The last time Rohit Sharma played for Mumbai Indians as a non-captain, they had never won the IPL. Now they jointly hold the record for most title wins. How will Rohit fare this year, freed up from his responsibilities? How will Hardik go, leading the team where he started his career?

The focus will be on them, but also on Shubman Gill, who has his first season as captain? His franchise may only be two years old, but have gotten used to success already so expectations will be high. I am Abhimanyu Bose, and I'll be joined soon by Sreshth Shah as we bring you all the action from the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.

9.15pm Titans bat through 20 overs without ever changing gears, finishing on 168. Credit for that, though, must go to Jasprit Bumrah, who didn't open the bowling but split his four overs into two beautiful spells to finish with 3-14 in four overs. He conceded just the lone boundary and bowled 14 dots.

Bumrah was ably supported by Gerald Coetzee, who was the seventh bowler introduced but ended up bowling his full quota to finish with 2-27. Hardik, Luke Wood and Chawla were a tad expensive, but Mumbai would take that in Ahmedabad, known to be batting friendly.

Back to the Titans, and they'll be disappointed that they couldn't change gears through the innings. Both Saha and Gill started positively, but once they fell, nobody else could really keep the tempo up. Sai Sudharsan with 45 did try to offer some resistance, but with his strike-rate of 115, you could say the bowlers enjoyed that more.

postText:
11.45pm There were some great performances from Mumbai Indians. Jasprit Bumrah, back and fit and firing for MI, bowled a brilliant spell, finishing with three for 14. Rohit Sharma and Dewald Brevis got to the forties. But it's a complete team effort from Gujarat Titans that eventually comes out trumps. It was another closely-fought contest with the home team coming out on top, which has been the trend for all five games this season. That will be all from us. On behalf of Sreshth, Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, it's Abhimanyu signing off.

11.3pm Stay tuned for the presentation ceremony.

Gujarat Titans captain Shubman Gill: "I think the way the boys held their nerves, and the way we bowled in the death overs, especially with the dew coming in, I thought it was special. With the dew, how the spinners bowled, they made sure we stayed in the game. It was all about putting on the pressure [on the batters]. [Mohit] has been a revelation for us since he joined us last year and hopefully he can continue his form. We just wanted them to feel under pressure. The plan was to keep building the pressure and wait for them to make a mistake. [On their total] I thought 170 was a good score but we definitely left 10-15 runs out there. Even with them, they were scoring above par but with the old ball and the pitch being slow, it's difficult to hit."

Player of the match, Sai Sudharsan: "Even in the first innings it was a little bit difficult. Dew helped them go after the bowlers but I think we pulled off a great game today. I'm not taking it as pressure, I'm just taking it as an opportunity to express myself and help my team win. After a few balls I felt it's not that kind of a wicket where you go after the ball every over. So i felt building the game was more important. I was actually a bit shocked for getting the player of the match because there were many great contributions [from the bowlers]. [On bowling plans] Taking the pace off was the plan. Even I found it difficult."

Hardik Pandya: "Obviously we back ourselves to chase those 42 runs [in the last five overs] but it was one of those days where we see the score quite less in those last five overs, we lost a bit of momentum there. It feels good to be back because this is one stadium where you can enjoy and feel the atmosphere quite lively and obviously the crowd was full and they got a good game as well. [On Tilak turning down the single to David] I think Tilak felt that was a better idea at that point of time. I completely back him. Not an issue, 13 games to go."

Debutant Spencer Johnson: "Absolutely incredible [experience]. Full house here. To get the win is very special. [On the 19th over] I think to stay calm. I had Ash [Nehra] telling me you're going to win the game. To have the backing from him and everyone else, even after going for runs in my first over, it's pretty cool. For me what works well is bowling hard lengths and keeping calm and not panicking and sticking to doing what I do well. This is easily the biggest crowd I've played in front of. I've always wanted to play cricket in india and here I am. I hope we can keep winning. Shubman is unbelievable. He sat next to me on the bus trip. He was calming me. We talked through the game. As a young captain, he's unbelievable."

Roopang : "Difference between two team is Nehraji"

Rajesh: "While everybody plays cricket, Nehra plays football. Always outside the line, passing tips ball by ball! Have not seen other coaching staff do this. Kudos!"

Ahmed: "The whole GT bowling unit is POTM in my opinion!" Indeed! it was a fantastic team effort to choke Mumbai Indians the moment they slowed down a little. Saw an opportunity and grabbed it.

11.25pm What a brilliant comeback from the Titans after Mumbai Indians looked like they were cruising to victory! Sai Kishore bowled beautifully, Rashid Khan was wicketless but economical. But Mohit Sharma with a two-wicket over changed things around before Spencer Johnson responded to an expensive first over in the IPL with two big wickets in the 19th over. The stage was set for Hardik Pandya to take his new team to victory over his old and he started the final over with a six and a four but the experienced Umesh Yadav came out on top eventually. Shubman Gill starts off his first captaincy assignment with a win over his old captain!

Afeef: "Got to commend the GT bowlers and new captain Gill for how they choked MI."

6.37pm RCB's numbers at home are not impressive. This season question marks persist over their death-overs skills and their spin options - and the Chinnaswamy will not allow slips on either front. Here's what Hemant has to say on why Bengaluru brings few home comforts for RCB.

6.30pm Royal Challengers Bangalore Bengaluru are back at the Chinnaswamy after losing their first game of the season in Chennai. The home crowd, who got to celebrate some success recently in the Women's Premier League, will be expected to be vociferous, cheering on their favourites in Virat Kohli, Glenn Maxwell, Mohammed Siraj and co. RCB will be up against Punjab Kings, who clinched victory in their first game of the season and will look to make it two in two. Can they silence the home crowd or will RCB open their tally today? 9.15pm A good finish provided by Shashank Singh, but RCB will likely feel the happier side after this innings. They bowled well, and Punjab Kings never really looked like they got going. There was a critical partnership between Sam Curran and Jitesh Sharma and then Shashank provided the spark at the end. Yash Dayal was excellent, so was Siraj. Alzarri was good but conceded runs at the end. But overall, RCB will be happy with how the bowlers went. The score may not be what you are used to at the Chinnaswamy, but as Curran said, there's something in the wicket for the bowlers, so the chase may not be as straightforward for RCB. Join Ekanth in a bit to see how Kohli and Co. go!

Sam Curran: "I think it's probably slightly under-par but there's a bit in it for the bowlers. I think simple stuff. There's a bit in the wicket. With the new ball they bowled well and there's something for the spinners as well. We are going to go out there with a plan to defend 176."

postText:
That was fun. There were unforced errors, teams not capitalising after getting close to taking home the advantage. Kohli's intent™️ chat won't be too loud given how he exploded at the start. But both teams got a lot of things right tactically and skill-wise, which made it a great game for the neutrals too. Hope that trend continues as the tournament progresses and that you follow it along with us, here on Cricinfo.

Harit Gautam: ""We had to pay the price for dropping Kohli" hope the selectors don't have to repeat Dhawan's words after the World Cup "

Kozhakks: "Loved the post match presentation from Kohli! The camaraderie between Harsha and Kohli was evident in that. "

[Dancing down and hitting over cover to pacers] I had to, bowlers know I play the cover drive pretty well. So they won't allow me to hit gaps. Guys like KG and Arshdeep, if they are hitting length, you have to create momentum, once you're closer to the ball you negate the bounce. You have to come up with a game plan and try to keep improving. I know my name is often used to just promote the T20 game across the world these days but still got it I guess. [Last two months] We were not in the country. We were at a place where people weren't recognizing us. Just to feel normal for two months was a surreal experience. Of course, things become totally different with two kids from a family perspective. Just being together, the connection with the older kid too is amazing. I couldn't have been more grateful to God for the opportunity that I got to spend time with the family. I was telling the guys that the voices got that much louder as it wasn't the case for the last two months. It was amazing to be another person on the road. I don't play for caps, it's just another opportunity. (2/2)

Virat Kohli, POTM: [To the crowd] Don't get overexcited, it's just two games. I know what this (orange cap) means. [Love story with the crowd] It's been going on for years. People talk a lot about playing the sport. At the end of the day you don't talk about the achievements, stats or numbers but the memories. It's what Rahul Dravid says. The friendship, love, appreciation, backing has been amazing and is what you'll miss and never forget. In T20, I'm opening, I try to give the team a blazing start. But when wickets start falling, you have to understand the conditions as well. The wicket wasn't as placid as normal here. It was a bit two-paced. Had to play correct cricketing shots, couldn't hit balls across the line. Tried a few, felt like I needed big hits at the other end, which didn't happen as Maxi and Anuj got out quickly. Disappointed not having finished it off. It was a slot ball that I sliced straight to deep point. Not a bad bad though playing after two months and getting into the tournament. (1/2)

Faf du Plessis, RCB captain: [Was he cool] Only on the outside, not as much on the inside. Gotta make sure you get over the line early in the tournament. Great to see the composure at the end. Don't think game was gone after Kohli went, because of the Impact Player and Mahipal in. In previous years we used to feel 12 runs in the last overs would be tough but now even 15s seem gettable in the last two. Really pleased for DK getting his game going. It sets us up for the rest of the tournament. Games get won at lost at the No. 7 and 8 position with the Impact subs, so he's key. Our plan at the auction was to find the DNA of the team. It's tough on this unique ground. The pitch was a bit different. Kohli's is still the same person, has had a nice break. It helps keep fresh in the back end of the career.

Dinesh Karthik Getting there [past the rust] I wasn't completely in control but it started to feel good. We needed the partnership with Lomror, he took the pressure off me with that six. It was critical, he batted well. Harshal is a wily customer. If you miss the dipping slower ball, you're done, so I had to time the scoop well. Lomror looked calm, didn't tell him anything at first. Told him to put that behind after he hit that six, then keep his head still and the rest will follow through. He's been batting well in the nets too.

Shikhar Dhawan, Punjab Kings captain: Good game, we brought it back. Think we were 10-15 less. Should have encashed in the first six overs. We had to pay the price for dropping Kohli. We lost momentum there, it was crucial. It looked a good wicket but wasn't true. It was stopping, bit of double-bounce and turned. 70% it was coming good. I was happy with my runs but think could've played faster in the first six. We lost two wickets which put pressure too. That total we thought was par. Match went till last over, at the end we could have bowled better. Harpreet is bowling really well, that too to left-handers on a small ground. He soaked in pressure and got breakthroughs. His celebration, the Kabaddi thing, is big in Punjab. People connect with the thigh-five, happy to see him doing it

11:14pm It was a twist-y turn-y chase. Kings were in it despite the unforced error. But Kohli gave RCB liftoff and DK landed the plane safely. All games this season have been won by the home team. RCB's record hasn't been great but that wasn't an issue tonight. The biggest event seemed to have taken place at the start of the chase, when Bairstow dropped Kohli. It unleashed one of the best players, and indeed flayers, in cricket. Him charging pacers and clubbing them through extra is what we've imagined doing as kids. The overseas stars failed. Promoting Green to No. 3 and Patidar over Maxwell didn't work. Harpreet was sensational, Rabada was good too. The constant wickets almost derailed the chase, especially Kohli fell due to some smart field placement. But DK came in with ice in the veins, got Lomror for support and the duo cleared the game with great skill and calmness.

7pm Toss: Gujarat Titans have won the toss and will bowl first. Titans are going in unchanged, but CSK have one change. They have Pathirana coming in for Theekshana.

Gill: That [first] match was very physically and mentally exhausting. Quick turnaround, but we are are used to it. It was a tremendous feeling to be able to be down in the game and then come back. It showed the character of our team. We are going with the same team.

Huge applause for Gaikwad: We were looking to bowl first. Wicket is similar to what we had in the first game. Batting first here is not much difference. I would say, slightly rusty start but we came back well. And once we came back we did not allow them to be back. Everyone showed good intent. In place of Theeskahana, we have our Malinga, Pathirana.

Pitch report from Anjum Chopra and Mathew Hayden: Lovely to be back. Really good wicket. There was quite a lot of bounce in the first game. There is a lot of grass on the surface. Very unusual for Chepauk to have grass. The way Chahar bowled in the first game, it was carrying really nicely through. There are patches where it is a little uneven with the grass surface. Very much inside the first four or five overs to do the damage and then the spin comes into its own and it gets tough. That is where CSK come to their own. It is a bat first wicket.

6.55pm Another interesting subplot in this game is the Chennai boys vs Chennai Super Kings. Titans have as many as five Tamil Nadu players in their side - Sai Sudharsan, Sai Kishore, Vijay Shankar, Shahrukh Khan and Sandeep Warrier. Among the quintet, Sudharsan, Kishore and Vijay are set to slot into Titans' XI or XII (accounting for the Impact Player). Sudharsan, Kishore and Vijay all have been part of CSK or Junior Super Kings, their grassroots programme. And back in the day, Shahrukh used to be a ball boy at Chepauk for IPL matches. In contrast, CSK don't have a single local player in their main squad.

CricDude: "GT needs to relook at their middle order. Except Tewatia, all others take time to settle. They need to bring in Abhinav Manohar who can keep the run rate up."

6.50pm New captains Gill and Gaikwad have already grabbed the headlines with their captaincy. After Titans snatched victory from Mumbai debutant Spencer Johnson talked up Gill's leadership, saying the captain sat alongside him on the bus to help calm his nerves in the lead-up to the game. As for Gaikwad, he rifled through fielding changes in his first game as IPL captain, and one such change, which involved extra-cover moving to sweeper cover, brought CSK their first wicket. The two new captains will once again be in the spotlight. Here's Deivarayan Muthu with the preview.

Joy: "If Pathirana is good to go, I would bring him in for Theekshana. If the pitch proves to be assisting spinners a bit, there will be the option of using Rachin."

6.40pm Remember the last time CSK and Titans came face-to-face? It was the final of IPL 2023 which began on a Sunday and ended on a Tuesday. In between there was a clash which ebbed and flowed like you won't believe. And in the end, with CSK requiring 10 off 2, Ravindra Jadeja struck a six and a four to help CSK secure a fifth IPL final. If the two teams can recreate even half of the drama from that game, we're in for some fun.

6.30pm Hello and welcome to match number 7 of IPL 2024 as Chennai Super Kings get all set to host Gujarat Titans. Both teams made a winning start to their season. While CSK got the better of RCB in a high-octane clash on the opening day of the tournament, Titans scored a sensational come-from-behind win against Mumbai Indians on home territory. Six games so far this season, six wins for home teams. Can Titans buck the trend and breach Fortress Chepauk or will CSK continue their winning run at home? I am Ashish Pant, and will soon be joined by Sreshth Shah as we try and answer all your questions from what should be a pulsating clash.

Question for Irfan Pathan: All young batters have seen a dip in their strike rate the season they have been named captain. Why is this trend there and will we see the same with Gill and Gaikwad?

Answer: With Gill especially, we don't associate a big strike rate with him. Last year he had a fantastic strike rate. But before that season his strike rate in T20s was 127. So he has always been a guy who takes his time, thinks about batting long. So I don't think that's the case with him. Ruturaj Gaikwad is the kind of player who looks for a big strike rate, score quick runs. Today, Rachin was taking an aggressive approach. But I think Ruturaj was also waiting for Rashid Khan, who has played very well. So I don't think it will affect these guys.

7pm Murali Karthik is out for the toss with the captains - Sanju Samson and Rishab Pant. Pant calls heads, he's right. Delhi Capitals will bowl

With five minutes to go to the toss, Rishabh Pant gets a jersey with 100 written behind. This will Pant's his 100th IPL game. Delhi Capitals, Daredevils previously, is the only team he's represented in the tournament.

Mohit Arya: "I feel if today Samson scores a fifty this could be breakthrough season for him 600 season, well we all hope so!"

Vince: "Is a rock hard pitch high or low scoring?" I think (and hope) high.

Pitch report: Equidistant square of the wicket with 67 metres. 76 metres down the ground. Simon Katich says RR have done their homework after a poor home showing last season. Pitch 5 was used twice, they made 237 and got bundled for 60. They'll hope to change that trend. It's a rock-hard pitch. When the cracks are pressed, there is a bit of movement which indicates there could be low bounce with the new ball, which was the case in the first game too. Going into the pitch with cutters, going high with the bouncers - something Sandeep did well - is expected to work. Both teams have had issues chasing. RR did well batting first last game, so they might prefer that.

Mukesh Kumar going full throttle, says Shashank, from the ground. Likely to come in for one of Ishant or Khaleel Ahmed

Nandre Burger interview with Shashank Kishore: 'I didn't want to be a cricketer, it was a free way to study'

6:40pm Kumar Sangakkara is currently addressing RR's players in the huddle. Samson smiles before they break jauntily. Theirs is a five-head 5D chess group that's looking to recreate home dominance which was lost in the last season. Jaiswal's still blazing, Parag's hit the ground running and will get a good run at No. 4, Jurel's coming on a high too. Buttler needs to hit form and Samson needs to find a way to carry his form deep into the season. Chahal and Ashwin are their big-name spinners. Sandeep is can be a specialist wherever you want him to be. Their Impact Sub selections are smart too. Expect them to be formidable.

Match Preview: Shaky Capitals look to raise their game at high-flying Royals' den

Similar thing is happening with Parag too !!"

6:30pm It's pink city, it's home-team advantage, it's run fests. The trends at the 17th edition of the IPL have been strong and Rajasthan Royals will hope to continue it against Delhi Capitals. Rishabh Pant's comeback last week was amazing, more for his return than his performance. His keeping was solid and his range-hitting - including some competition with Jake Fraser-McGurk in the lead-up to this game, has been good. Ishant Sharma, who got injured while fielding last game, is available. Anrich Nortje is expected to play, Prithvi Shaw might be out. Capitals need their middle order to fire.

postText:
And so, the streak of home teams winning matches continues in IPL 2024. Nine in a row, and it is the longest such streak at any point in the IPL, says Sampath. That's all we have for you all tonight. Do join us for another cracker - RCB take on KKR in Bengaluru - tomorrow. Till then, take care, ciao!

11:41pm Time for the presentation

Sanju Samson, Royals captain: "The way we started, the first ten overs, we were like Rovman, be ready you might have to bat! The IPL is changing and we all have to be flexible. Earlier it was about 11 players, now it is about all 15 players. Me and Sanga had a lot of chat between 15th and 17th over before deciding the Impact Player. It's all about gauging in which zone they are. You have to look at that and take your decision. I saw Sandy was calm and Avesh was also looking good, so i went with that. Riyan Parag has been a big name in the last few years. Wherever I go, people ask me about him. There is something very special he can give to Indian cricket."

Riyan Parag, Player of the Match: "Emotions are settled, mum's here as well. She's seen the struggles, this feels special. I know what my ability is and I never let that change - irrespective of whether I perform or not. A lot to do with the domestic season, where I scored a lot of runs. Someone in the top four has to take it deep. First match, Sanju bhaiya did it, today I did it. I had to work very hard. I was on bed in the last three days. I could manage it today."

11:25pm High fives all around in the Royals camp. Ninth successive win by a home team this season. The bowling changes from Samson were spot on. Never let the batters settle and some excellent death bowling saw them eke out a 12-run win. This was after a Riyan Parag special enthralled one and all in Jaipur. That was clean-hitting of a different class, capitalising on his superb form. Axar was thrifty with the ball for Capitals, but barring Warner, none of the batters could get going.

Rishabh Pant, Capitals captain: "Definitely disappointed. The best thing to do from here to learn from it. The bowlers did well through the 15-16 overs. But the batters did well at the death, hopefully we do better in the next game. The platform that Warner-Marsh gave was very nice. We had to save wickets. We had to consolidate but at the end we had a lot to cover up. [On not bowling Nortje to Parag earlier] There is always one or the other option, but we wanted to finish Nortje in the death overs. Sometimes you are going to go for runs. Didn't go well for us today."

Avesh Khan, Royals bowler: "[On the death-over yorkers] My plan is always clear. One side was longer, so my plan was to bowl wide yorkers. I was giving myself five seconds and only thought about executing them. My focus is always on the execution and back my yorkers. Enjoying myself here because we have Sandeep, Boult, Burger, all of whom have different skills. Samson gives me freedom to execute and only steps in if he sees I am struggling. I try to improve myself everytime. In T20s I try to reinvent myself. I never think about selection and only practice what I want to bowl."

postText:
Big win for KKR tonight and they are now 2-0 in this IPL 2024 season. It is also the first win for an away team, so plenty of other sides will be pleased with how this result panned out. See you tomorrow for more IPL cricket. Till then, on behalf of everyone at ESPNcricinfo, bye bye!

Jai Kedia: "I want to credit y'all over at Cricinfo for the excellent "MVP" tool you've built. It's very difficult to convert traditional cricket stats into match impact in T20s but you have done a sensational job. Harshit Rana today is an example. On the surface his stats don't impress but he played a crucial role in KKR's win."

11.05pm On his 500th appearance in T20s, it is Sunil Narine who is the Player of the Match for his overs and batting blitz. Here he is: "(500th T20 match) It is a nice milestone. Hopefully there are 500 more to come. Great to perform like this. Relief also to get it after a while. (Batting success today) Just self belief and support staff giving encouragement. Little bit of hard work and it is helping. (Bowling, how he pulled things back) Powerplay is always the hardest over to bowl so you have to forget that. When you come back later, you have to capitalise and pull things back. (KKR camp) It helps when you win. Self belief and confidence is coming from the support staff."

10.57pm We'll have the presentation shortly. And here's the winning captain Shreyas Iyer: "(rest between games) Absolutely. Coming here, we were in good shape between games. Coming here and hitting few balls made us feel comfortable. (Bowling innings) Russell showed slower ones are good here and the way he executed them were easy to see. From there on, rest of the bowlers picked up on that and made that their plans. Communication was brilliant. (Narine as opener) See Narine when he comes in, he has one job that is to clear the outfield and get maximum runs. Today was a phenomenal example. We were contemplating today whether to open with him or not, but this was great. (Nature of surface between innings) From one end, it was pretty good to bat on. From the other end, it was two-paced. It was bouncing extra. That was the communication we were having and passing it on to the batter coming next. (Break between now and next game in Visakhapatnam) We are spending a day here tomorrow and then going to Vizag. Have to see the nature of the pitch there. (Only one playoffs last four seasons - what expectations?) Not expecting much. Season has just started and we have just two wins so far. We need to embrace this and enjoy each others' successes."

Humaid Salman : "Only off-pace bowlers can succeed at Chinnaswamy. Fizz would have been a good buy but RCB never learn from mistakes. Bowlers like Starc also goes for runs here.I would definitely retain Vyshak before Siraj"

Venkatesh Iyer, who hit a fifty: "Let's see how my back is. Will know after a scan. The ball was coming on really well in the evening. Credit goes to Sunil Narine whose runs took the pressure off us. We just had to finish formalities. (Venkatesh's mindset) With a platform like that, you have to maximise. With a left-hand spinner bowling, I walked in in front of Angkrish, so I knew I had to take 'em on. Also my fiance was here today so it was a special day. (Facing Vyshak) Pace-off in totality was tough but if fast bowlers bowled pace-on, it was easy to take them to the cleaners. Happened with us in our bowling innings too."

Bruce Wayne: "Any one who played more than 6 deliveries in this match had a higher SR than Kohli - and that is the reason RCB lost - not ground or dimensions or pitch. If Rizwan or KL Rahul or Steve Smith or Williamson etc played this innings - that would be the only conversation point."

Hari: "Gambhir comes in - asks Narine to open, picked Salt and plays him over Gurbaz (who was benched by DC last season), doesn't care to sub Varun, injects aggression to bowling department (especially Harshit). Championship mindset!"

10.48pm Losing captain du Plessis: It was two-paced in the first innings but the pitch became better in the chase. It was not easy batting in the first innings, and you could see that with Virat also struggling a little. (Looking back) We could've tried one or two things, but the way Salt-Narine batted, they pretty much took the game away. They were excellent and broke the game in the first six overs. (Did you miss spin options?) We've tried Maxwell and fingerspinners are effective here but today there wasn't much spin. And with them having a left-right combination, spinners can find it tricky. We needed a wristspinner who could turn it both ways. (Vyshak) Very good. He hasn't had a lot of opportunity. We thought of getting legspinner Karn as an Impact Sub but brought him in for his cutters. We saw Dre Russ bowled 80% of his balls as cutters, so knew that would work. Good mix-ups from Vyshak, in terms of skillset.

10.45pm And an away team finally wins a game in IPL 2024. This game turned out to be a non-contest with KKR cruising to victory with 3.1 overs remaining. Every batter who turned up in purple and gold had a field day out today on a batting-friendly surface, and this par target was razed down easily.

KKR fans would once again love to see Narine get among the runs, who nearly got a fifty in his 500th T20 appearance. Salt, the two Iyers and an unbeaten Rinku ensured all their boxes were ticked as a batting side.

For RCB, only Vyshak's spell was promising. Otherwise, they all went for runs, even the spearheads Siraj and Alzarri Joseph. The only question that remains is whether they lost the match with the ball or with the bat when they scored only 182. We'll know more about what they think when we hear from Faf du Plessis.

Dhawan leads his team out and they get in a huddle as the umpires walk out. Rahul and QDK stride out. Sam Curran has the new ball in hand. Over the wicket to Quinton de Kock. One slip in place.

Praveen: "So if LSG were fielding first then KL would not have been in the eleven for the first innings ? Is that what this is about ? Thank you for explaining" Bingo!

7.25pm It's almost time for the match to start off. M Siddharth is in for his first appearance of the season and Mayank Yadav is making is debut for LSG. And as a reminder, KL Rahul will only play as a batter today, with Nicholas Pooran leading LSG. How will the LSG batters go against Rabada, Arshdeep, Brar and company?

Satish : "If overseas player can't substitute another overseas player, then what is reason behind the teams for keeping them in impact sub list" They can come on as sub fielders. Also, if a team has started with three overseas players, they can still come on as an Impact Player.

Pradeep: "Strange that LSG chose KL to be impact player, they could have chosen Padikkal!" It's been done keeping Rahul's workload in mind.

Gajesh: "What kind of workload management KL is under? He kept wickets earlier even though QDK was there and now he is playing as impact sub. Is there something I'm missing?" Maybe him keeping in the first game aggravated something. With fitness issues, you never know when something flares up.

Bini Sivan: "Impact player in Playing XI??" So effectively, Rahul will only bat, and go off for whoever comes in as the Impact Sub, and hence Pooran is the captain.

Jasdev: "Can teams swap an overseas player for another overseas player? This way, effectively utilizing 5 overseas players in a match!" Nope, the only way an overseas player comes on as an Impact Player is if the team starts with just three of them.

7pm It's toss time, and it looks like Nicholas Pooran is out there for LSG! We'll know soon enough what is up with KL Rahul. Yup, Pooran out there with Dhawan. LSG win the toss and bat. "KL Rahul is playing as an impact player," Pooran says. They are easing him in as he is returning from an injury. Says they want to put up a good total and defend it. Dhawan says Punjab Kings would have bowled first anyway because of the dew they saw last night. Wants his bowlers to get their lines more tight and also for batters to not lose back-to-back wickets. Punjab Kings are unchanged.

LSG XI: Quinton de Kock (wk), Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, Marcus Stoinis, Nicholas Pooran (capt), Ayush Badoni, Krunal Pandya, Ravi Bishnoi, Mohsin Khan, Mayank Yadav, M Siddharth

Subs: Ashton Turner, Naveen-ul-Haq, Amit Mishra, Deepak Hooda, K Gowtham

Punjab Kings XI: Shikhar Dhawan (capt), Jonny Bairstow, Sam Curran, Liam Livingstone, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Shashank Singh, Harpreet Brar, Harshal Patel, Kagiso Rabada, Rahul Chahar, Arshdeep Singh

Subs: Prabhsimran Singh, Rilee Roussouw, Tanay Thagarajan, Vidwath Kaverappa, Harpreet Bhatia

6.55pm Here is Brian Lara with the pitch report from the ground: The pitch has a little more grass, it's a little thicker. Something in it for the fast bowlers. It's a red soil pitch. No visible cracks, a level surface so should be a good contest between bat and ball. Lara reckons the pitch will hold for the 40 overs, so he thinks the team winning the toss should chase.

6.50pm While you'll get all the ball-by-ball action right here, for a more detailed coverage with stat nuggets and more analysis as the game goes by, don't forget to keep checking in on Sid Monga's live report.

6.47pm It looks like Delhi based right-arm medium-fast bowler Mayank Yadav has received his first cap for Lucknow Super Giants.

Ami: "Where can I find information regarding which teams will play each other twice, and which teams will face each other only once?" You'll find it all on our fixtures page.

Junaid Anwar: "Both these team remain away from media glare,fanfare,hype and all that normally associated with an IPL team,that also has an advantage as it allows players to remain free of pressures thereby playing to their full potential." Well, KL Rahul's strike rate will not escape scrutiny from media or fans, I can tell you that!

6.40pm Have any questions about today's match for the Star Sports Hindi commentators? Do you want to ask Sanjay Manjrekar, Mohammad Kaif or Harbhajan Singh anything cricket? Go to the ESPNcricinfo mobile site, click on the AskStar button and fire away your questions and you may just have your doubts answered on TV!

Also, don't forget that you can follow our commentary in Hindi as well!

Mustafa Moudi : "When before LSG is hosting their first match today, the home side winning streak got broken. So no assurance for LSG to win this. Feeling little sad for them !!" Yup, that streak got broken so that KKR could maintain their streak at the Chinnaswamy last night!

Bong Boy Ashish: "Lucknow is definately going to win their first match of the season. Ravi Bishnoi leads the IPL wicket-taking charts at the Ekana stadium. He is going to be the key player today." He had a quiet first game of the season, but back at his home ground, he will be hoping to make more of an impact.

Afeef: "I wish Rossouw could play but there's no place in the playing XI. That being said, I want Livingstone to come good in this tournament. He's been having a rough time for the past few months in terms of consistency."

6.30pm With ten games already done, IPL 2024 is well and truly underway. Today, for Match No. 11, we have Lucknow Super Giants, led by KL Rahul, up against his former team, Punjab Kings. LSG need to get off the mark, and will hope that home advantage will help them do just that. Kings, meanwhile, started the season with a win, but then lost in Bengaluru, so they will want to get momentum back on their side. The last time the two teams met was a high-scoring affair, but if the pitches at the Ekana stadium last season are anything to go by, today should be a much trickier affair for the batters. Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of today's game. I'm Abhimanyu and, along with Ekanth, we'll be bringing you all the action from Lucknow.

If you want to do some homework on the match, look no further than Vishal Dikshit's match preview. Meanwhile, in some team news, LSG have signed Matt Henry as a replacement for David Willey, although the New Zealand quick is not going to be available for today's game.

9.20pm Right then. A half-century from Quinton de Kock and some rapid 40s from today's captain Nicholas Pooran and Krunal Pandya have helped LSG set Punjab Kings a target of 200. Sam Curran was excellent with the ball, taking three wickets, while Arshdeep took two. Rabada and Chahar chipped in as well, while Brar was economical despite not getting on the wickets column. Join Ekanth soon to see how the chase will pan out.

Krunal Pandya: I've always prepared that way that I'll be flexible as a batter. I just want to go out and contribute to the team, regardless of what position I bat. I like to prepare well. I take it like an exam where if you study well, your paper will go good. I treat cricket the same way. [On the total] Pretty happy. One side is bigger, one side is shorter. If we bowl smartly we can defend this. The surface has been changed and it's much better than last year."

The family moved to Chennai to help Siddarth become a professional cricketer. Siddharth is a bit of a super-specialist in the TNPL: he bowls with the new ball and swings it. In the most recent TNPL, he spun Shahrukh Khan's Lyca Kovai Kings to the title. In IPL 2023, he was a net bowler for Chennai Super Kings and in the past, he has also had a stint with India as a net bowler. Siddharth has spent much of his career in the shadows of R Sai Kishore, TN's premier spinner and captain. This is his chance to emerge from the shadows of Sai.

postText:
It's a new pacer, a new performer, a new story. What's better than that, eh? Mayank's spell was an experience in itself, how cool was it to be a part of it?! Hope this is one of many coming in the league. Thanks for joining in tonight. Take care.

Mayank Yadav, POTM I've always heard from others there's nervousness in debuts but that goes away after the first ball. Plan was to not be under too much pressure and to bowl at the stumps and use the pace as much as possible. There was the thought to mix up the pace initially but the wicket helped and the skipper told me to bowl gas. The debut wicket was the favourite. Coming off the injury last season was tough, I'd set my goal to debut at a young age but injuries were a setback.

Nicholas Pooran, LSG captain: Wonderful start in front a home crowd. (On the batting order) We had a start at the chat of the tournament. Use the left-right combo as needed. It's a big ground, one side big. It's tough as you have to go big while going at tens. Shikhar and YJB played well, but they didn't take the game away from us. Mayank's was the story of the night. It was an inspiring performance. Every person in the team is happy he got a chance and performed tonight. Was wonderful watching him from mid-off. It's a young bowling attack. The IPL has given local players opportunities to grow. We have youngsters, experienced players and coaching staff as well. Expect guys to get better. Groundsmen, everyone who contributed was amazing.

Jasdev: "Glad any LSG batsman didn't score big. Now the MoM can deservedly go to Mayank Yadav !!"

Farid: "So Delhi and Mumbai are the only winless teams after two rounds of matches."

Morne Morkel, LSG bowling coach: Happy with the win. Bowlers stuck to it. In the first timeout told the bowlers to stay in the game. Then young Mayank bowled serious heat and got the wickets. It was tough last year as he got injured after the first warm-up game. We're managing him better. He ran in and that was the pleasing thing. We asked the guys to do the basics well on a good wicket. Told him to stick to his lengths and use bouncers. Proud he ran in and bowled gas despite the humidity. How the wicket would play was an unknown, we had to sum up conditions and use them. We had five-six days after the first game, that could've worked against us too. It's harder sitting in the dugout than on comms. (laughs)

Shikhar Dhawan They played well, Livi got injured that impacted us. He'd have come in at 4. Mayank bowled really well. His pace outsmarted us. It was nice facing him, surprised me with that pace. Knew as an experienced player I'd use it. But he figured it out and bowled yorkers to keep me down to a dot and a single. I was mindful and told my partners to use the short side. He bowled at Prabh's body and got him out. Told Jitesh to leave Mayank and take on the other bowlers but they bowled well too and then used the pressure against us. We're gonna analyse the game. We gotta take catches, that takes the momentum away and gets the energy down. To come up with better plans and more importantly implement them is what we need to do. We're close but need to do 10% more.

11:20pm It's another home-team win on Mayank Yadav day. It was an innings of two halves. Bairstow and Dhawan owned the first and Mayank the next. It was singlehanded and shows that the beauty of pace extends beyond optics if accurate. Just for reference, Kings needed 102 off 60 with ten wickets in hand. By the time Mayank was done, they needed 60 off 24 with seven wickets in hand. It was oh so effective, he's all smiles while hugging his opponents. Doubt he'll be tired of the compliments. His fellow debutant, Siddharth, started well bowling like Akeal Hosein in the first over of the innings but was found out. The duo stayed deep in the crease, literally, and found the boundaries often. They nailed the chase for a while but Mayank's entry hurried batters, created dots. It led to Bairstow falling. The new guys tried working against it, unlike Dhawan and also fell. Mohsin was excellent on the other end too. It slowed Shikhar before dismissing him. Krunal bowled tight enough for the game to not drift. Naveen got some tap in the end but had more than enough to defend.

preText:
Unsurprisingly, no changes to the SRH opening combination. Travis Head is back at Motera for the first time since the greatest cricketing night of his life. He'll partner Mayank Agarwal. No change to the GT plan for now either. Azmatullah Omarzai will get first use of the new ball. Mayank will take strike.

Aashique : "I think GT have one of the best squad but they are not being able to figure out best 12." --- One feature of Nehra's GT has been their brave calls coming off, like Vijay Shankar in the middle order last season. They certainly haven't yet put a finger no their balance without Hardik Pandya, though.

I've got plenty of you asking me about Natarajan's fitness status. He missed the last game with an unspecified niggle, so we're assuming him missing out today is only a continuation of that.

Abhishek Shah: "GT make changes in bowling and not batting?? Baffling.. " --- That's one way to describe it. Sai Kishore certainly will consider himself unlucky to miss out.

Pat Cummins has won the toss, and SRH will bat first. He says it's a good wicket and it's pretty hot, so they want to put some runs on the board. Got some wonderful memories at this stadium, he says. He says the last game was a measure of how good they are. No changes for SRH.

Gill says they would've bowled first, with the thinking being that they would like to know what the target is in front of them. Noor Ahmad and Darshan Nalkande come into the Gujarat side today, Spencer Johnson and Sai Kishore make way

Playing XIs:

Sunrisers Hyderabad: 1. Travis Head 2. Mayank Agarwal 3. Abhishek Sharma 4. Aiden Markram 5. Heinrich Klaasen (wk) 6. Abdul Samad 7. Shahbaz Ahmed 8. Pat Cummins (capt) 9. Bhuvneshwar Kumar 10. Mayank Markande 11. Jaydev Unadkat

Impact Player options: Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Umran Malik, Upendra Yadav, Glenn Phillips

Gujarat Titans: 1. Shubman Gill (capt) 2. Wriddhiman Saha (wk) 3. Vijay Shankar 4. David Miller 5. Azmatullah Omarzai 6. Rahul Tewatia 7. Rashid Khan 8. Darshan Nalkande 9. Noor Ahmad 10. Umesh Yadav 11. Mohit Sharma

Impact Player options: Sai Sudharsan, Sai Kishore, BR Sharath, Abhinav Manohar, Manav Suthar

Suman: "How can Shahrukh not play after all the investment and effort to bring him in? " --- A certain Ben Stokes was the most expensive player for last year's champions and played only a couple of games, so the auction value certainly isn't the be all and end all.

Pitch Report: 66m and 63m square boundaries. 73m straight boundaries, pockets at extra cover and midwicket a bit longer. It's an absolute road, says Kevin Pietersen, who thinks it looks like a tremendous wicket. He says there's a breeze which will help the players as temperatures are expected to reach 38-40 degrees celsius. Sunrisers will come here, look at that wicket, and say maybe they can make 270 again, chuckles Pietersen, as he tells Ravi Shastri they are going to be calling sixes and fours galore. It's a black soil wicket, adds Shastri, so that is similar to the November 19, 2023. That wasn't as high-scoring, so a nice bit of intrigue surrounds that. .

Ashish: "Is robin minz available for selection?" BR Sharath has replaced him. I didn't know but Aaditya was onto it in a flash. Here he is for more insights.

2:40pm As for Sunrisers, they're 1-1 but were four runs away from making it 2-0. Their pacers need some oomph. Cummins was excellent during MI's 278-run chase but still isn't a T20 whiz. Very different from Tests. His inclusion comes at a cost of other players - like Glenn Phillips and Marco Jansen - missing out. Wanindu Hasaranga's still not in India but he's not too far from making it either. But Cummins is cricketing chess grandmaster and alpha at the same time. He, along with Travis Head, has what it takes to silence the crowd at the Narendra Modi Stadium. Their batting's crazy strong with six-machine Klaasen and in-form Abhishek Sharma.

Aditya: "Hey there Ekanth! I'm going to oppose you here. Though high scoring games do give you entertainment, it is crucial to have games where bowlers dominate once in a while. Too many high scoring games get really boring after a while and hey, bowlers need some of the limelight too come on!" I do agree. Bowlers should dominate once in a while. The point is so should batters. That's what creates balance. My point is for being wholehearted with compliments rather than noting the exception which arguably undermines. Be it with batting or bowling.

CricDude: "GT have an issue with both their middle order. And Umesh failing is an added concern. They have to bring Abhinav at any cost. Either Nalkande or Sushant has to be tried for Umesh, or go for 2 overseas pacers. Gill, Saha, Sai, Abhinav, Miller, Tewatia, Rashid, Kishore, Mohit, Little, Spencer - this would be my XI. Add an extra batter or bowler as the game goes - Shahrukh, Vijay Shankar, Nalkande, Sushant are my impact players."

Match Preview by Sreshth Shah Vulnerable Titans face Sunrisers acid test. Sreshth will also be on the live blog for snappy summaries and analysis during the game.

2:30pm Here's a hot-take to start double-header Sunday - batters bashing it everywhere in T20s is a good thing. Like when Sunrisers Hyderabad got 277 on a flatty, along with basking in power-hitting excellence there was an undertone of 'what about the bowlers'... there was contrarianism in the concern. But you know what, bowlers will win tournaments, they will play a key part especially as the tournament goes on. So even if they don't get the social cache, they'd get many a chance to line up wins for their teams. That's actually what Gujarat Titans would want in the absence of Mohammed Shami. Rashid Khan has blown hot and cold, so they'll want him to turn up. Lest we forget, he's coming back from a surgery and has played just five T20 games since returning, including two IPL games. It's a day game, whoever bowls first will have their task cut out.

postText:
5:08pm: SRH were 58/1 at the end of the powerplay, with Travis Head going great guns. But he fell trying to attack Noor, then Mohit picked up Abhishek just when he looked set to go big, then Rashid removed the dangerous Klaasen. The Titans were very effective taking the pace off the ball towards the back end of that innings. Have SRH learned from that? Their captain specialises in that kind of bowling in white ball cricket, to be fair, so he'll certainly be encouraged by what he's seen from the wicket. They've got the extra spin option into their side, in the form of Washington, can he make use of the spin available on this track? 162 is not a huge total, but certainly is defendable.

Abdul Samad: This is a decent score. It's a day game, there's some help for the spinners as well, so this is a decent score. I was striking the ball well, so I thought I should've got more strike in the last over. Looking at our start, we thought we could get around 180, but around 160 is a decent score as well.

postText:
That's the 11th win for the home team in 12 games. Will that trend continue in Delhi or can super-strong CSK change that? Find out Live here. Thanks for tuning in to this match. I'm Ekanth, signing off on behalf of my co-commentator Aaditya Narayan, and our scorers, Thilak Rama and M Venkat Raghav.

Mohit Sharma, POTM: Thanks for telling me I'm aging. I practice what I do generally. What's important is knowing when to use them and being ahead of the batter. Everyone has them on slow wickets but knowing how to use it against whom is key. (Importance of tweaking the field when bowling slow) If you and the batter knows what you'll deliver, then you need to play with one fielder's position to deceive the batter. If he's ready for a slower bouncer but I go slow and wide, he won't be ready. (Bowling slow balls in night games) We practice with a wet ball to contend with dew. But it's an uncontrollable, mindset matters more there. (On his role) As long as I do well I enjoy. When you don't it hurts a bit but you have to go back and review things after the game. But it's better if the mistakes are due to failing in execution rather than not following the plan. Spinners were excellent after SRH started well. It helped us chase a smaller target.

Shubman Gill, GT captain: Winning two matches at home is great, two more to go and then we go on the road. Hope to bring the momentum back. Our bowlers, esp Noor, Rashid bhai is world-class. But Noor and Darshan bowled excellently. Mohit is such an experienced bowler, esp on wickets like this. Not easy to bowl three or four overs back to back. He mixes up yorkers, slower ones so well. In this heat, it's easier to bat early in day games. So we wanted to make them hit to the bigger boundary off slower balls. Ball hit the bottom of my bat on my wicket ball. In T20s if you see the ball in your slot you have to go for it. We thought 160-170 would be a good score. Credit to the bowlers to restrict them. Everyone knows their roles in terms of batting or bowling. Sai has played well, Wriddhi bhai does what he does well. Miller's gotten in form too. He has just a cramp I think.

Shadow-Shell: "Wow! Highest impact is Mohit with 58.38. Shows how no one dominated the game more than other"

Ananthanarayana: "Men in blue beat pat Cummins led side in Ahmedabad ! "

Sai Sudharsan: Happy with my contribution as it helped the team to win. On this wicket it was tough to play pacers bowling slower ones. So we thought of targeting spinners and maximising there. Great contribution from Mohit and Rashid, they saved 10-15 runs which was key. To be playing in front of home crowd is a plus point which is playing in our favour. [Being out in the 40s] Everyone wants to score more every game, I'm just thinking of contributing and helping the team win. Milestones will come.

Pat Cummins, SRH captain: Good match but we got 10-15 less. They bowled well. Losing a couple of wickets meant we couldn't get a batter not making fifty plus. It happens, it was probably the difference. [Him coming in late to bowl] Today it was a case because we thought the wicket would slow up a little bit and offcutters would become more effective, which they were. [Would he have changed the toss decision] No, I thought the wicket played the same in both innings. It's T20 cricket, batters have had fantastic couple of games. The boys looked good but were stifled by the wickets.

6:54pm It was a clean finish. Titans took it deep, had wickets in hand and the experienced Miller took them over the line. SRH were probably unders after being stifled in the powerplay. Four batters made 20s and three between 15 and 20. In contrast, all four of Titans' top order got more than 25. Saha attacked Shahbaz, got boundaries off Unadkat and Bhuvi too. Gill carried on with Sai Sudharsan with the asking rate not mounting. SRH were trying to get a good chunk of their spinners' overs out but it led to only two wickets in the first ten. Gill's wicket didn't open up the game as Miller joined Sudharsan. Cummins' entry slowed the rate, Miller was hobbling at times but the 24-run 16th over off Markande meant there were no death-overs worries. Vijay Shankar too chipped in with a cameo in the end.

nickH: "GT's 20th over and SRH's 16th over decided the game."
