7.30pm Here we go. Shaw to face, Chahar has got the ball. A first slip and a third slip in place.

Azweer : "Moeen Ali deserves a chance in Playing XI." -- The question is in place of whom.

Shaw's inclusion means he will be facing Chahar, a match-up the seamer has enjoyed: 6 dismissals in 68 balls for 85 runs in the IPL.

Here are the XIs:

Delhi Capitals: 1 Shaw, 2 Warner, 3 Marsh, 4 Pant (capt, wk), 5 Stubbs, 6 Porel, 7 Axar, 8 Nortje, 9 Mukesh, 10 Ishant, 11 Khaleel
Impact Players Sumit, Kushagra, Salam, Dubey, Jake Fraser-McGurk

Chennai Super Kings: 1 Gaikwad (capt), 2 Ravindra, 3 Rahane, 4 Mitchell, 5 Jadeja, 6 Rizvi, 7 Dhoni (wk), 8 Chahar, 9 Pathirana, 10 Deshpande, 11 Mustafizur
Impact Players: Dube, Shardul, Rasheed, Moeen, Santner

"We were looking to field first," Ruturaj Gaikwad says, "as it is a fresh wicket and the first game here and there's not much information about the pitch. Definitely a home game today [lots of yellow shirts in the stands]. We are going with an unchanged side."

7pm Delhi Capitals have won the toss and opted to bat. "The wicket looks good," says Pant. "We came early here and have practised a lot, which gives us a pretty good idea." Kuldeep Yadav has a niggle and Ricky Bhui has been left out. Prithvi Shaw and Ishant Sharma come in.

6.50pmWhile we wait to see if Shaw gets a game, Varun Aaron has a suggestion for Capitals: Play Kumar Kushagra at No. 3.

Sukrit: "Why is the game not being held in Delhi?" --- They wanted to allow the Delhi pitches some time to recover after the WPL games, so shifted the first two matches to Vizag.

6.40pm More from Deiva: There's a tinge of grass on the pitch, which suggests CSK will play both Pathirana and Mustafizur. Prithvi Shaw batted at the nets for about 20 minutes on Saturday, but wasn't at his fluent best. Capitals coach Ponting has acknowledged the work he's put in behind the scenes, but it remains to be seen whether he's done enough to break into the team.

Mustafa Moudi: "I know CSK is already a settled side and needs no changes, I feel they must give Shardul Thakur chance. Not only a wicket taking bowler but he is a great batsman too. Moreover, he is in great form as he played an important role in Mumbai's recent Victory in the Ranji Trophy !!"

6.35pm Here's Deivarayan Muthu from the ground: Whose home game is this, really? This is supposed to be DC's adopted home - they even had their pre-season camp in Vizag - but now there are yellow jerseys all around the city. At my hotel, which is about 15 kms away from the ACA-VDCA ground. At Novotel along the Varun beach, where the teams are staying. At lassi and samosa stalls near the venue. Even around the threates, which are screening the brand-new Telugu movie Tillu Square. Hundreds had turned up outside the gate of the ACA-VDCA ground on the eve of the match to catch a glimpse of Dhoni, but he didn't train on Saturday. Vizag has turned up in huge numbers once again on Sunday as Dhoni returns to the scene of his first big innings.

6.30pm Hello and welcome to match 13 of IPL 2024. It's Chennai Super Kings taking on Delhi Capitals in the second game of the day. If you go by the points table, this match is a mismatch. CSK have won their both games and Capitals have lost their both.

Not just that, Capitals have a few injury concerns as well. Ishant Sharma got injured during their opening game. Shai Hope missed the second with back spasm. Anrich Nortje and Jhye Richardson, meanwhile, are on a comeback trail. While Capitals are playing at home, it's not Delhi but Visakhapatnam. They have lost three of the five IPL games they've played here. I am Hemant Brar and will soon be joined by Alan Gardner as we bring you all the action. While we wait for the toss, have a look at Deivarayan Muthu's match preview.

Here's a recap from about Akash Madhwal, who's in for MI today - How Akash Madhwal engineered his way into IPL record books

MI Impact subs - Nehal Wadhera, Shams Mulani, Romario Shepherd, Nuwan Thushara, Dewald Brevis

Mumbai Indians: 1 Rohit Sharma, 2 Ishan Kishan (wk), 3 Naman Dhir, 4 Tilak Varma, 5 Hardik Pandya (capt), 6 Tim David, 7 Gerald Coetzee 8 Piyush Chawla, 9 Akash Madhwal, 10 Jasprit Bumrah, 11 Kwena Maphaka

RR Impact Subs - Kuldeep Sen, Shubham Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Rovman Powell, Abid Mushtaq

Rajasthan Royals: 1 Yashasvi Jaiswal, 2 Jos Buttler, 3 Sanju Samson (capt & wk), 4 Riyan Parag, 5 Shimron Hetmyer, 6 Dhruv Jurel, 7 R Ashwin, 8 Trent Boult, 9 Avesh Khan, 10 Nandre Burger, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal.

Hardik Pandya does get booed for the length of his first sentence. Says he was wanted to bowl. Good toss to lose, we'll see what we can put up. (Mumbai's 250th game) This franchise holds a lot of value and a lot of love from the fans (boos go up again but he keeps loud and firm), exciting to be very honest. (It gets quieter again) We are quite lucky to be part of the 250th game. Slow start doesn't bother us. We hope to have clarity, keep the mood happy and light. This group is all about that. Looking forward to play a brand of cricket everyone enjoys and gets that two points.

Sanju Samson: Bowling first (gets a small cheer after that) says they are confident. This is the first game here, hope the seamers will use the conditions upfront. Confident from the wins but the tournament has not yet started so we need to keep going. Sandeep misses out, he's not 100% fit. Burger in the XI.

7pm Sanjay Manjrekar is out for the toss with Hardik Pandya and Sanju Samson. Sanjay asks for a big round of applause for Hardik but there is a boo. "Behave," he says. RR have won the toss and will bowl. Small cheer from the crowd

Pitch report: Pitch No. 7 being used. Not used in IPL 2023. Brian Lara says the red-soil surface looks great. It has a generous covering of grass and the team that's bowling first has to get new-ball wickets. We're gonna see a lot of runs. Not sure spinners are gonna come into the game because of the grass. What the team does on winning the toss will be crucial - RR have won batting first. MI have chased, they came short (although they made 246 in 278-run chase). The team batting first will have the advantage.

Sujatha : "Looking Hardik as a villain is totally uncalled for. It is sport , professional sport , a Franchise driven league. Employers need results and emotions need to be set aside. With Hardik and backing him" Think (and hope) his employers are supporting him. It's massive as Tom Moody said. The chat among the public and how things are from a cultural pov is fascinating. Agree that villanising him is uncalled for. R Ashwin's comments on it were interesting too.

Match Preview by Karthik Krishnaswany Can slow starters MI kick into gear on a batting paradise?

6:40pm RR have shown glimpses of being the shrewd franchise that they are by showing flexibility with their Impact Player choices and bowling selections. Sandeep Sharma has been amaze at the death, Avesh Khan can offer him support. Nandre Burger can chomp into top orders with the new ball. R Ashwin and Yuzi Chahal are skilful spinners but won't have helpful conditions. That's a challenge, as is Jos Buttler's poor form. But he'll have a local batter in Yashasvi Jaiswal familiar with the conditions. Their middle order was taken down in the last game but Ashwin came in and gave them an escape. 6:30pm MI are back at the Wankhede for the first time in IPL 2024 and Hardik Pandya will lead them for the first time, at home, as permanent captain. He's back to his roots as MI was the franchise that gave him his big break back in 2015. But coming back after leading Gujarat Titans to a title win and a final hasn't been seamless. Their season opener, in Gujarat, saw him get booed. But that continuing in Hyderabad was what's surprising. How the home crowd receives him will be a point of intrigue but his team needs to win. 9:20pm RR well set to get the second win for a travelling team in this IPL. The pitch was said to be a good one to bat on but Boult and Burger ensured that wasn't the case. The former got two in the first over. He didn't try to swing it as Rohit expected, to nick him off. Then did swing it to Naman to have him lbw. Brevis as impact sub didn't work. postText:
11.25pm So, that's three wins in three for Rajasthan Royals. But even a return to their home ground could not help Mumbai Indians avoid defeat for the third consecutive game. There were some boos for Hardik, several cheers for Rohit, but it was the Royals bowlers who stole the show. Trent Boult was sublime with the new ball, with two wickets in the first over. Mumbai lost three players for golden ducks thanks to the left-arm quick. Nandre Burger was also great with the new ball as Royals dominated the powerplay. Chahal helped take out the middle order and that left Royals chasing 126. Maphaka started with Jaiswal's wicket in the first over and Bumrah bowled a probing spell without luck, but Akash Madhwal's two strikes just around the end of the powerplay gave Mumbai Indians a sniff at an upset. But with Ashwin pushed up the order to arrest a potential collapse, Parag continued to impress as he played a calm, nerveless knock to eventually make sure Royals won without much fuss. Akash Madhwal's performance will be a rare positive for Mumbai Indians, but they know they have a lot of work to do. For Royals, they would want Buttler and Jaiswal - their gun openers - to start firing soon. While those teams ponder about what's next for them, we are going to wind down here. You can read Sreshth's report, meanwhile, for a recap of the game. Thank you for joining us. On behalf of Ekanth, Chandan and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, this is Abhimanyu signing off. Goodnight!

11.12pm Time for the presentation ceremony, then.

The player of the match is, as expected, Trent Boult: "[First over wickets] Never say it's a certainty in the format, but it was nice to get the wickets. We created early pressure, nice to take some wickets and glad the result went our way. [On the Rohit wicket] I've played against Rohit a lot over the years and it was just about trying to do something different. It rarely comes off, you try something different and it works, but great when it does. [On Burger] He has been a great find. Bowls with great skill and plays with his heart on his sleeves. Sandeep obviously missed out but he'll play a big role in the season. Excited to be part of this bowling attack."

Rajasthan Royals captain, Sanju Samson: "[The toss] I think that was the gamechanger. The toss was very crucial. I felt it was too sticky to start off and we had the experience of Trent Boult and Nandre Burger's speed. [Boult] has been playing international cricket for so long and we expected him to deliver. I didn't expect four or five wickets down, but it was great. We all do our roles and move on. Someone like R Ashwin knew we had a good powerplay so he didn't go for wickets, just kept it tight. So it's about teamwork."

10.56pm Riyan Parag's assured innings, along with handy contributions from R Ashwin and Shubham Dubey have helped Royals seal this chase with ease. A fired up early spell from Bumrah and Madhwal saw Royals lose three wickets early-ish, but Parag marshalled the chase expertly. Of course, it was Trent Boult and Nandre Burger and the rest of their bowlers who set up the win.

Riyan Parag: "Actually, I've simplified everything instead of trying to do a lot of things. Earlier when I wasn't getting runs I would try a lot of different things. This year, it's just seeing the ball and hitting the ball. When I play domestically this is the exact kind of situations I go into bat. When Jos bhai and Ash bhai got out, I thought to myself this is what I do in domestic cricket. So that's what I calculated/ [On difference between domestic level and IPL level] I have had three-four years of not performing at all. And you really go back to the hotel room and think when you know you can do it and the results are not coming, you go back to the drawing room. I realised I wasn't practicing at this kind of level so I went and did that. I practiced these kind of quick balls and these kind of scenarios a lot and hence the performances."

Hardik Pandya: "We didn't start the way we wanted to, tough night tonight. [On his innings] I think we were in a decent position to give us a chance to get to 150 or 160 but I think my wicket changed the game and brought them more in the game and I think I could have done better. [The pitch] It's good to have something for the bowlers as well. The game is quite cruel to the bowlers. But it was unexpected. It's all about doing the right things. Results, sometimes it happens sometimes it doesn't. I don't think much surprises me anymore. But as a group we believe we can pull off a lot of better things going forward and we just need to be more disciplined and show more courage."

Gaurav: "Does Parag get the Orange Cap, or it remains with Kohli?" Parag has it now, thanks to a better strike rate than Virat Kohli.

Mohan: "MI need to replace Maphaka and Coetzee with Nuvan Thusara and Nabi as their overseas players to make squad stronger."

Arjun: "Two things happened in the last ball of the innings. Coetzee bowled the fastest ball of this IPL at 157 kph and Riyan Parag got 4 runs to get the Orange Cap. " The latter is correct. The former was a glitch! That was at around 141kph, not 157, even though the TV did show it at 157!

6.45pm RCB's batting hasn't quite fired, and they will hope it finally does today. That is what Shashank Kishore's preview states. After all, the likes of du Plessis and Maxwell are yet to kick into gear for the hosts. LSG, meanwhile, have concerns around their captain KL Rahul, who they are looking to only ease back into action. Rahul didn't keep wicket for much of training on the eve of the game, and stand-in captain Nicholas Pooran only said "we'll see how he goes".

6.30pm Hello and welcome to the Chinnaswamy. Not quite a fortress yet for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, who sit at No. 9 in the points table. They have a tight win squeezed in between two losses where they fought before losing their way. That said, Lucknow Super Giants haven't started too well either. "To bat first is a brave call. Is dew not expected tonight? " --- Neither captain mentioned about it, Shrikant. Maybe it isn't expected, after all.

7pm We are set for the swing of the coin. KKR win the toss and bat. Iyer says the pitch looks like a "belter to bat on". He says it might not make a lot of difference even as he played for DC until a few seasons back. Raghuvanshi is back for KKR. Pant, meanwhile, would have batted first too, given he expects the pitch to slow down. He hit his first fifty last game after his comeback, and is happy to take it day by day. DC have one change: Sumit replaces an injured Mukesh.

Ishant Sharma leads the DC huddle, with all eyes on ears intently on him. We are less than five minutes away from the toss, so hang around while sipping some hot cold coffee.

6.45pm Both DC and KKR have some thinking to do ahead of today's contest. The hosts have still not had their opening batter Prithvi Shaw at his best. He has had a bit of a rollercoaster ride, as Deiva Muthu writes. Their other concern is about the fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who has returned from a long injury lay-off. Tom Moody, our expert, thinks "Nortje isn't quite back at his full pace" yet. As for KKR, they spent INR 24 crore on Mitchell Starc alone, but... is he running out of time already? Moody and Varun Aaron ponder.

In a quick recap of the points table, DC are at No. 7 at the moment, with KKR pretty high up at No. 2. A hat-trick of wins for KKR would mean they draw level on points with Rajasthan Royals, who are also unbeaten. That reminder, and much more in Ashish Pant's preview for today.

6.30pm A former DC captain comes back home, but instead as the leader of the opposition. Meanwhile, his replacement at DC has returned to full flow after missing out on plenty of cricket. KKR, the side Shreyas Iyer brings to Visakhapatnam tonight, face Rishabh Pant's team, who got off the mark three days back at the same ground. We are into Match No. 16 of Season 17 of the IPL, as this is Himanshu saying hello.

postText:
That's time for us to say goodbye. Congratulations to KKR fans, commiserations for our friends rooting for Delhi Capitals, and if you're a fan of Indian cricket, there were plenty of positives to take home irrespective of which side you support. See you tomorrow for more IPL action. This is Sreshth saying bye on behalf of Sudeep, Chandan and Himanshu.

Sunil Narine, the Player of the Match, for his highest T20 score (85 in 39) and a wicket: "(Happier with batting or bowling?) Cricket is all about batting so looking to contribute more as a batter. That said, I still enjoy by bowling. (On the team joke that he does not attend batting meetings) I have one role and the less I know the better it is for me. (Batting lower down in Abu Dhabi Knight Riders) We had sufficient batters there so I wasn't needed. At the end of the day it is what the team needs. If they need me to bat, i will bat. (Plan with Salt) He is aggressive and gets the scoring going so all the pressure isn't on me. (As well as you've bowled?) On a wicket like that we wanted to win by a bigger margin so it helps later on in the tournament."

Winning captain Shreyas Iyer: "(Did you think about crossing 277?) No no, the way we started we thought 210-220, but 270 was icing on the cake. (Going hard in the powerplay - pre-planned?) As I said in the toss interview, Sunny is there to take on the bowlers, and if he cannot the rest of us should. That's the plan. (Raghuvanshi) He was fearless from ball one. His work ethic is phenomenal. He analyses situations well. He is a smart batter, shots were pleasing to the eye. (Bowling - Starc, Varun with wickets) Good to see bowlers stepping up and taking responsibility. They supported each other in their successes. We've been observing that last few games. (Harshit Rana OK?) Don't know. He was holding the shoulder. I know how he is feeling with shoulders. Will find out. (Vaibhav) The way he came back after conceding two overs early to take wickets. That is the character we need. (Three wins in three) You always have to be down to earth, especially in the IPL."

NEW: All the stats highlights from the KKR batting innings

Mitchell Starc, two wickets tonight: (What worked tonight?) Not changing too much. In T20s, you get some dropped chances and some edges and they don't go your way. But we are 3-0 and that's what it is all about. (Biggest price tag. Struggled with wickets early on) Nothing really as I said before. Games come thick and fast. It is T20 cricket, it can get brutal. You take a bit of luck here and there. We are 3-0, been clinical with the bat, so personal things aside, the team is going fantastic. Nice to have Marsh and Warner in the pocket. Another way win. (Vaibhav Arora and the short ball) That is all him. He was fantastic, using the short ball really well. We talk more in training and in bowling meetings. Just talking about that side of things. They may have questions, we have little conversations, certainly not me telling them what to do."

Mustafa Moudi : "85 with the Bat, A Wicket and excellent Economy Rate with the ball and a Catch as a Fielder. Narine has contributed in every department tonight !!"

Rishabh Pant, losing captain: Our bowlers were all over the place. We just didn't turn up on the day. Today was one of those days. As a batting unit, we only wanted to keep going hard as a team. I would rather get all out as a team than not go for the target. (Some reviews not taken) I think it was quite loud here. At the same time, couldn't see the timer on the screen. There was some problem on the screen. But there are some things you can control, some things you can't. (Use of Axar, only one over) See the thought process was that we didn't want to use spinners but our fast bowlers were going through the motions. I think it is time for reflections as an individual. We need to learn from these mistakes and come positive in the next match. (Pant's own body) Doing fine. Getting out there. Enjoying every day but cricket has its own ups and downs."

11.18pm So KKR win their first three games, of which two have been away from home! This 106-run win now also sends them to No. 1 on the points table.

There wasn't much pressure for their bowlers after the batters posted 272, and the seamers Starc and Arora very nearly ended the chase in the powerplay. From there on, the Capitals saved some blushes with Pant and Stubbs hitting two attractive half-centuries, but Varun and Narine closed the deal swiftly thereafter. KKR win comfortably after posing the second-highest score in IPL history, stopped from breaking the record only courtesy a terrific Ishant Sharma 20th over in the first innings.

7pm Shubman Gill and Shikhar Dhawan are out, both in good spirits too. Gill has the coin, tails is the call. It's tails, Punjab will bowl first

Pitch: Square boundaries are 63 metres each. Fine ones are shorter - 55 and 56 metres. Long ones are on the other side - 68 to 70 metres. Simon Katich says it's pitch 6, was used four times last game including the final. Three were won by the chasing team. It has a mix of black and red soil, so it's rock hard. Got 3 millimetres of grass on it, so there'll be a bit of pace and bounce but also runs for batters. GT have won 8 out of 12 games, so Kings will have a tough challenge. From the sounds of it, my guess is that chasing would be the better. Let's see what the captains think at the toss. Scheduled for 7pm local as always.

6:40pm The sky's blue in Ahmedabad but probably not for long. People are peppering in across the stands. The ring-lights on top are on. Practice is going in full flow. The pitch, as the preview mentioned, might be one of red soil. We'll know more about that and the teams soon. If it does have some zip, GT might think of bringing in Spencer Johnson, who looked like a million bucks in the BBL but didn't start as well here. Of course after Mayank Yadav's bursts, raw pace might be worth a try. Kings' spin, actually the home bowlers in general, need to step up. Jitesh Sharma, in his pre-match interview on the IPL website, has in fact all but confirmed Liam Livingstone won't play due to an injury tonight. Shoutout to Matt Roller for digging it out.

Deivarayan Muthu's Match Preview - Gill's Titans look to make it three in three at home

6:30pm: Isn't it nice to be in a routine? It's what the IPL, along many T20 leagues offer. Something to comfort-watch on a weekday that's beyond what an algorithm recommends. (Recommended reading on the topic from three years ago). And today can be about breaking free from set formats for Punjab Kings, who might bring in Sikandar Raza in place of Liam Livingstone if he is unfit. They might, as Mitch McClenaghan mentioned, go with Rile Rossouw to strengthen their batting. For the hosts Gujarat Titans, it's mostly go-with-the-flow stuff. They're in a groove, have a balanced side, may want Rashid to get more consistent but he's easing back in to top-level cricket. So no alarm bells for now.

Should be good if bowlers hit the right areas.

9:14pm Gill, Titans' captain, bats through and has given his side a great chance. It was a buffet, nay, a Thali of strokeplay, powerhitting, placement, everything you want. Arshdeep, Rabada got great bounce and a bit of sideways which Williamson tried to negate. It slowed them down a bit. He fell to Brar while trying to up the ante. Sudharsan joined Gill and did that though, in a 53-run stand. Kings tried to hold their own but conceded big overs every now and again. 11:30pm Time for the presentation

Shikhar Dhawan Kings captain: "It was an amazing game. Very, very close. Boys did the job. Plan was to give a good start, but I got out early. We lost a few wickets early and Shashank came and played a tremendous knock. When you are chasing a big total, you have to keep the momentum going. Shashank showed his class. Magnificent knock. He timed the ball so nicely, it looked effortless. He kept his cool and finished the game. He started from No. 7 and is now showing his positive mindset. Ashutosh also came in and took the game well. The two young boys were keeping their calm and soaking the pressure."

Shashank Singh, Player of the Match: "Still trying to sink in. Visualised all these things, but when it turned into reality, proud of the effort. Coach told me to react to the ball. The wicket is very good, the bounce was good. 200 scored by both teams, so the wicket was fantastic. They are the legends of the game, but when I go to bat I think I am the best. You get experience, couldn't get a lot of matches before. Here the owners and coaching staff backed me. I was very confident."

11:14pm What drama! Kings finally stall their losing run, and it is the second-highest successful chase against Titans in the IPL. Kings steadily lost wickets at the start but what they did not fail to do was keep up with the asking rate. Prabhsimran and Bairstow first, Jitesh a bit, and then Shashank and Ashutosh at the end kept the hits coming and helped the side hunt down the 200-run target. What a platform the IPL is for these unheralded players. Two of them shine and take their team across the line. Did Titans miss a trick but not bringing in the sixth bowler earlier? Should they have promoted Omarzai with the bat, perhaps ahead of Vijay? Lots to dissect for them.

Shubman Gill, Titans captain, gives Mohit Sharma the Purple Cap: "Couple of catches went down. Never easy on a wicket like this when you drop catches. Difficult to defend runs in these conditions. The new ball was doing something. There are always areas to improve. I think 200 was good enough. We were in the game till the 15th over. When you drop catches, you will be in trouble. The way Nalkande bowled in the last match, we went to him for the last over. This is IPL for you - people who you have not seen will come and win games."

Ashutosh Sharma: "I would like to thank Punjab Kings for believing in me. Happy that our team has won. Personal performance happens, but main thing is for the team to win. [Mindset] Shikhar [Dhawan] has told me a lot of things mentally. I was like 'I will do it'. I have won games for my team, so I had the belief. Sanjay Bangar also believed in me, he spoke to me a lot during camps, and that helped. Back home, I had worked with Amay Khurasiya, my coach. He said you will do well when you get the chance."

6.50pm Dhoni has just walked out on to the park and Uppal has gone berserk. Absolute bedlam in the stands. Just what the sighting of one man can do. He's warming up with some light football. while Cummins is doing some batting practice. He'll hope he is not needed today. For all the euphoria, this game is crucial for both sides, who are coming off a loss. SRH went down to Gujarat Titans by seven wickets, and have won just one game out of three. CSK after winning their first two games, lost to Capitals by 20 runs despite Dhoni's whirlwind knock. They will want to get back to winning ways. As far as the head to head is concerned, CSK are firm favourites having won 14 out of 19 games played between the two sides. They, however, will be without their spearhead Mustafizur Rahman for this game.

Here's Travis Head talking to Harsha Bhogle on air: [Any orange around?] Scattered a little bit. I have heard things about Chennai. If Dhoni walks down now, I might lose you. [277 surface] The wicket was nice, we are making sure we start well ,give ourselves the best chance. Hopefully we can get off to a good start. [Going after his shots] It is situational. I am always giving myself a chance. My technique is of a three-format player. I try to use my experience. [Coming to Hyderabad] Have been here a couple of times in the last 12 months, and have done well, so hope to do better. [Surface] I had a look at the surface a couple of days out it looks quite good. Try to come in with plans, assess the conditions, is it swinging, is it not. We tried to do that a couple of days ago and will try to make the right decisions. [Score 277 again?] Tough game to follow. We need to have the same intent, and give ourselves the best chance.

6.40pm Sixes flew, records broke, the balls went out shape the last time an IPL game took place in Hyderabad. SRH amassed 277, the highest-ever score in the history of IPL, while Mumbai Indians were not far off in their chase reaching 246. So, what's in store today? More of the same according to Shashank Kishore in his preview. For SRH, Abhishek Sharma has set the tempo at the top and Travis Head has already shown how dangerous he can be in that game against Mumbai . Then there's Aiden Markram and Heinrich Klaasen in unbelievable six-hitting form. CSK too have a prolific six-hitter in Shivam Dube, who has struck at 177.09 against spin since last year's IPL while they also see Daryl Mitchell warming up to a similar role. And then, of course, there is Thala, who blazed away to an unbeaten 16-ball 37 in his last game against DC. We might be in for an epic clash tonight.

11:05pm Time for the presentation

Pat Cummins, SRH captain: "Different soil, slowed up as the game went on. Stil a fantastic game. We have got plenty of fast bowlers. Shivam was hitting the spinners. So we took a chance with the fast bowlers bowling cutters. [Abhishek Sharma] I would not be wanting to be bowling to him. The crowd is crazy tonight, especially when MS walked out. We love playing here, home conditions."

Abhishek Sharma, Player of the Match: "In the bowling we felt it was a slow wicket. So we wanted to take the powerplay on. We had a chance to prepare well before the IPL. We knew it will be slow but not if we take on the bowler. Because it would be difficult for the bowler as well. Big scores matter, but I went with the flow today. Hopefully I will get out last next time. It is all the hardwork i have put before this. Special thanks to my dad, Yuvi paaji and Brian Lara."

10:49pm One-way traffic in Hyderabad tonight. But CSK did not leave it without a fight. Given the start SRH had, they could have well romped home earlier. Head and Abhishek are turning out to be some pairing. They never let the opposition in, unless they commit a mistake. Tonight was also something similar. Head was offered a life in the first over and then CSK were senton a leather hunt. SRH romped to 78 for 1 in the powerplay in the chase. And you almost knew that was the game.

Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: "It was a slow pitch. At the back end they bowled well. We couldn't capitalise in the last five overs. We were in a good situation halfway but they bowled well at the back. Black soil pitch, so we expected the slowness. As the ball got older, it got slower. They used the conditions well - big boundary one end. We did not bowl well in the powerplay but did well to drag the game. 170-175 is par, if we would have had a good powerplay with the ball, we could have had the game. There was slight dew at the later stage. Moeen was spinning the ball in the 15th-16th over, so not much of a difference."

Aiden Markram: "Not too bad, but not like it was against Mumbai. When we bowled, the first ten overs or so, it was coming on alright but got tougher. So we took on in the first ten and were in a good position later. I don't want to think too much, probably see-ball, hit-ball. That is encouraged by the team management and Patty [Pat Cummins]. When you get in, the batter that is in needs to value the position. The Impact Player has freed batters."

Rajkumar Lingav: "Klassen finishes without hitting a Six!!! "

Nishant: "SRH wasted a great opportunity to improve their NRR. The middle period they went into a shell unnecessarily! No RR pressure, no wickets pressure " Wasn't a very easy surface to hit through and through, and that reflected.

Faf was thinking he'd have bowled but not fully sure. We've got one change to give some impetus to our batting. I feel we haven't played at our best. 6:30pm: It's time for RCB to go pink. Home hasn't been kind to them and Rajasthan Royals are trying to re-establish Jaipur as their fortress but going back on the road could be the welcome change the visitors need, especially their big-name batters Faf du Plessis, Glenn Maxwell, and Cameron Green. They have Karn Sharma and Maxwell in the ranks but aren't strong in the spin department. Alzarri Joseph, their fast-bowling big buy, got pumped. But Reece Topley brings height and the left-armer's angle with him. Can things click together, which seems to be the only mode in which RCB can thrive this season?

9:11pm 183 - It's roughly around par but are they short though? Okay, three minutes and the Kohli chat later, one thing's clear - conditions can't not be factored in. As he said, they had to hit straight and couldn't get under balls. Faf tried pretty much everything but couldn't shake it off. Kohli had a great start to the powerplay. Ashwin coming in slowed things down. He and Chahal were excellent. They used the lack of bounce well and the pace, which wasn't true all the time. The openers then consolidated for a while, put on 125. RCB promoted Maxwell and Chauhan but couldn't get much. Kohli though, was like a motivated bike rider in Bangalore traffic. Knew which gullies to go through and where to accelerate. It might not be enough but he's given them a chance.

Virat Kohli: The wicket looks different from up there when you're not playing the ball yourself. It seems flat. But when you see the ball holding up in the pitch, especially against the spinners you see pace is changing quickly. Big dimensions come into play. Our initial target was 195 but then we decided if one of me or Faf got out one had to bat till the end. We got a boost and got 185, which I feel this is an effective total. If we get the change of pace and lengths right, it will be a tough chase. I'm not coming in with premeditation. I was 12 off 10, I don't want to be over-aggressive, want to keep the bowler guessing. They want me to go hard and get me out. It's just experience and maturity. I play the conditions and have the game ready. Doesn't seem there's dew hope it's the same. Balls didn't come on to bad, felt you couldn't get under bat.

11.32pm Superb performance from Royals who've begun this season with an absolute bang. Four games, four wins, but they know from recent memory that a good beginning is no guarantee of going deep into the IPL. As for RCB, well, lots of problems to dwell on and sort out. Before that, though, we have a tasty double-header coming up tomorrow: MI vs DC first up, and then LSG vs GT. Two potential crackers, so do be there to follow all the action on your favourite website. Until then, good night!

Jos Buttler, Player of the Match: "A little bit of luck to get it over the rope in the end, didn't time it that well, but delighted to get the win. However long you've played the game, you still have those anxieties and stresses. Sometimes you just have to tell yourself it'll be okay. Just keep digging in, working hard, at some point we will be okay. I actually did feel really good in the last game, even though I only scored 13 or something. We've started this season really well. We've been together for three seasons, everyone's comfortable with each other, we just need to keep this momentum going."

Sanju Samson: "I think anything below 190, with a little bit of dew coming in, with the batting order we have, I felt it was a good total to chase. Touchwood, few more games to go, we are bowling well. And we have got a break, which is helping us charge up and come in fresh. [Are RR a batting or bowling side?] I think bowling is 9, and batting is 8.7. It was just a matter of time with Jos. He just needed to get through the powerplay and middle a few balls."

Kumar Sangakkara: "I thought it was a good toss to win, we were pretty decisive in wanting to chase. RCB started well, but Nandre Burger brought us back with the spinners, and Jos and Sanju were clinical. Everyone requires a chat, but the chat doesn't have to be about cricket or technique or anything like that. Jos is the best white-ball opener in the world, and all he needed to do was sit back and ignore some of the noise. [On Jaiswal:] We know the quality that Jaiswal brings to the side, we just want him to relax and bat, and bat long. He just needs to calm down a little bit, rest up."

Faf du Plessis: "I think batting out there with Virat, we found the wicket really tricky and low. We did feel 190 would be a good score. I did feel we could have maximised 10 or 15 more towards the end. It was a good toss to win, you did see that it played much nicer with the dew. Virat was playing really well at the back end. Whether it was Virat or a Greeny or a DK coming in, we could have scored a few more. We tried, but it was quite tricky to hit. With the spinners, a lot of balls were hitting the bottom of the bat. I think the pitch definitely got better. That's what dew does, that's the nature of the wicket. I thought it was a good toss for them to win. We started well in the first four overs, then the one over from our spinners, 20 runs, it shifted the pressure back onto us. Maxwell, all the right-handers batting in the middle, that's why I went to the left-arm spinner, Mayank, who's been bowling well for us this season. And the legspinner [Himanshu], you want to use the attacking option. When we got the wicket of Jaiswal, with the two right-handers in the middle, it didn't feel like the right time to use the offspinner."

11.08pm Terrific win for the Royals. It seems like a long time ago, but RCB began brilliantly with the bat before the Royals spinners began turning things around to restrict them to 183. It didn't feel like enough then, despite what Virat Kohli said about the conditions, particularly with all the doubts over RCB's bowling quality. Royals did it easily in the end, with a brilliant century from a back-among-the-runs Jos Buttler, and a superb 69 from Sanju Samson.

Thanks so much for joining us. Look forward to your company for LSG v Titans that has already begun in Lucknow. For now, this is Shashank Kishore signing off on behalf of Ashish Pant, Thilak Gowda and the rest of our crew.

Time for the presentations

Romario Shepherd is the PoM for 39 off 10 balls along with the wicket of David Warner. "Yeah, it made me proud, my hard work has paid off. Hardik told me to express myself on his way out. In these situations, got to just keep eyes on the ball. Don't need to be tentative. Keep a clear mind."

Hardik Pandya: "I would like to have this feeling [of being winning captain[] more often than not. Lot of hard work, hard to clear our minds, and everything clicked. We will be making some tactical changes here and there but more often than not this will be our XII. Settling of the team is important. There was a lot of love and care going around, everyone knows we lost three games but the belief and backing was there, everyone believes we needed just one win and today was the start. I mean amazing, to start with 77 after six is always wonderful. The way everyone was batting, we needed rhythm to bat, the way everyone is chipping in with the opportunity coming in was fantastic. That was some hitting from Romario, he won us the game. The difference was his innings. I like him, he always has a smile of his face, doesn't run away, very proud of the way he played, proud of the team. All good, will be bowling at the right time. Had it covered, so didn't need to roll my arm over."

Ishan Kishan: "We played to potential, this is what we're known for. Kept the process going, we were in a good headspace and got the result we were looking for. Played enough games here, not easy after six overs, more of a rotation game after that, so power play was important for both of us to take the bowlers on and we executed in a very good way. Romario has been working very hard, wasn't playing but was giving his 100% at the net sessions. That was the kind of over we were looking forward to. We know he's very powerful and it changed the game. I'm feeling very good, lot of meetings going on, talking to the coaches, we knew we had to bowl well."

Hardik Pandya & co doing a lap of honor around the ground to thank the 18,000 kids who turned up to watch them play as part of Reliance's CSR initiatives. All the members of the squad are right there - Hardik., Tendulkar, even the owners.

7.20pm Mumbai Indians were challenged briefly, but the carnage at the end of their batting innings by Romario Shepherd proving to be the difference. Capitals conceded 92 off the last four overs. They'd look back at that as a massive turning point and a momentum changer in the match.

Rishabh Pant: "I feel we didn't have enough runs in the Powerplay. Yes, tried to change it afterwards but when pressure mounts on you with asking rate crossing 15-16, it's very difficult. One over here and there can change the momentum, either we can look to play the blame game or look to improve on that. The wicket was good to bat on, slower ones were sticking on the wicket. Will look to improve power play [batting] and death bowling."

7pm It's time for the toss. Rahul and Gill are out in the middle. Heads is the call by Gill, and it comes down as tails. LSG will bat first. Rahul says it is a good wicket. Batting first has been working for them, and they are confident about it. Adds this is the first time he has realised they have not won against GT and they are not really thinking about it. Same team for LSG. He also talks about Mayank Yadav, and says he is very professional in the way he goes about his cricket and his routine and that it is important for them to manage him.

Gill says he would have bowled first anyway, so he is happy with the toss. Adds that they were on top for 32-33 overs but that happens in T20 cricket. Couple of injuries. Saha misses out with a back spasm, with BR Sharath making his debut. Spencer Johnson comes back in too. Says everyone drops catches but it is about always looking forward to the next game.

Over in Mumbai, the five-time champions are well in control against the Delhi Capitals, with the latter needing 82 off 24, as things stand. You can follow all the live action here.

Let's see what the conditions have in store for us. We have moved on to pitch no. 5. Equidistant square boundaries - 66m to each side. 75m hit down the ground. The shortest and longest pocket are 60m and 79m, respectively. The pitch looks hard and Matthew Hayden proves that by banging his knuckles into the turf. He reckons it might be an innings of two halves. It will not be easy work but it the batting conditions will be great with the ball coming on. As the ball gets softer, though, it could get tougher.

6:30pm The last time these sides met in Lucknow, the Titans huffed and puffed their way to 135-6, led by Hardik Pandya's 50-ball 66. Mohit Sharma then turned up with the ball to stifle the Super Giants, helping the Titans win by seven runs.

6:25pm The Lucknow Super Giants versus the Gujarat Titans. A side that has fallen short at the Eliminator twice in succession, against an outfit that has reached the final in both years of its existence. A team with lofty ambitions, up against a franchise that has already gotten to where LSG would want to be.

In one corner, a power-packed batting unit, studded with stars throughout; in the other, an ensemble cast that continues to do what is asked of them. On one side, there is a young fast bowler, all of 2 IPL games old, terrorizing batters with his raw pace. And in the opposition, a veteran who keeps unfurling his bag of tricks with guile, poise and precision.

Then, there is a captain who is relatively experienced in the IPL (and has led India), and another who has just started out. A team that could barely win at home, against a side that travelled so well in 2023 (winning six out of their seven away league fixtures).

This might seem a contest of contrasts. But what ties these two franchises together, apart from when they first ventured into the IPL arena, is that they are on four points, and would love two more. Two points that will ensure they end the weekend in the top four, and will allow them to continue dreaming big.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the IPL. This is Match 21, and we are back in Lucknow. LSG have only ever won three matches at this venue, and they have never beaten the Titans in the IPL. An 0-4 record usually hints at a lopsided rivalry, but LSG would be out to prove otherwise tonight. Hop on, this should be plenty of fun!

9:14pm And so, LSG stutter and stumble their way to 163. They were rocked early, losing de Kock and Padikkal to Umesh. Rahul and Stoinis then resurrected the innings. The former, though, was probably too cautious, scratching his way to 33 off 31 and perishing when he attempted a big stroke.

Stoinis fared better and registered a fifty, but he too could not carry on and give LSG the finishing kick they were after. Pooran did manage a 22-ball 32, while Badoni scored 20 off 11. But LSG, at this stage, will feel they have left a few runs out there.

As for GT, they will be largely pleased with their bowling effort. Umesh set the tone early and the spinners followed suit. Nalkande was a tad expensive but he did account for Stoinis and Rahul, which meant LSG were never able to generate the head of steam they were after. GT will be confident of chasing down 164, but they will also be mindful of the fact that LSG have never lost when defending 160-plus. Join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Umesh Yadav: (On his animated celebrations) The way the games are coming, and how I am bowling with the new ball, this was the first time I got two wickets back-to-back in the powerplay. What I worked on before the match, it worked out, so I was happy. My plan was to swing the ball. I feel that if the ball swings and if you can stick to your lines and lengths, that is the best way to get dismissals. That was what I was trying - to bowl in the right areas and to get it to swing. The wicket is a little spongy and there was a little bit of dew. I feel this (score) should be chaseable.

postText:
11:40pm That will be all from us, folks. We will be back again tomorrow as the Chennai Super Kings return to Chepauk, hoping to snap their two-game losing streak, against a Kolkata Knight Riders side that is firing on all cylinders. Until then, this is me (Shashwat) signing off on behalf of Sudeep and everyone else at ESPNcrcinfo. Goodnight and take care!

Yash Thakur, Player of the Match: I am very happy with my first five-wicket haul and my first POTM award. (On bowling to Gill) The plan we had for Gill, we had two fielders on the leg side. So, we sort of knew that he (Gill) would try to make room. Rahul bhaiya told me to stick to my plans and that we will get a wicket that way. Unfortunate for us that Mayank picked up an injury. But Rahul bhaiya told me that this is my day and that I will win the game for LSG. In the last two seasons, we had not won against them. We won today so we are very happy. (On which wicket was his favourite) Shubman's wicket.

KL Rahul, Lucknow Super Giants captain: (On LSG making defending totals an art) We will take the win. Not going to make too much out of it. For the young bowing group we have, helps when we bat first and they can assess the conditions. They have been adapting really well, so credit to them. (On not losing a game when defending 160-plus) It is a good record to have. But it is where we have played. We know how the wickets were, very low-scoring wicket and low-scoring ground. Having the home advantage obviously helps a bit. The same guys were playing last season as well, they have adjusted their roles and they are reading the wicket well. That is something I try to speak to them about in the nets and in practice, to help them make the right choices when the pressure is on. Hopefully we can continue. (Thoughts at the half-way stage) We knew very early that it (the pitch) was not as good as the other day. We were not trying to get to a particular score, and were just trying to bat and see how many we would get. We put up a score and then you expect the bowlers to do their job. All three spinners have been key for us. Sid (Siddharth) has done very well, he bowls a crucial part when he bowls with the new ball. He has shown great temperament and he has given us steady bowling in the first 2-3 overs. He has picked up wickets, but his job is to restrict runs. KP (Krunal Pandya) has played for so many years, and he is smart and knows how to bowl. Have played with Bishnoi also for a lot of years. Feels good to get off the mark (against the Titans).

Shubman Gill, Gujarat Titans captain: (On the conditions) I think it was a good wicket to bat on. just a poor batting performance by us. We got off to a decent start but we lost it in the middle overs and were never able to recover from that. (On the bowling) I think our bowlers were exceptional to restrict them to that score. We were looking at 170-180 but to restrict them, it was a tremendous effort. (On Miller) He is a player who can change the game at any time. We had a couple of injuries but irrespective, this total was gettable. (On his dismissal) It was the last over of the powerplay and I just wanted to capitalise. Everyone was up on the off side, I wanted to give himself room. The ball I got out to, I was trying to play it too square and missed it. (On Umesh Yadav) He is definitely someone who is very experienced. Darshan and everyone in the bowling attack did a good job.

Krunal Pandya: When I went in, I just played a couple of balls. I was having a chat with Pooran and the wicket was very good, and we felt we were 10-15 runs short. At the end of the day, what I do is knowing the batter's strengths and weaknesses and bowling according to that. On some days, it works. On others it does not. One of those days where I was able to execute what I wanted. It feels great the way we have been defending in the entire tournament. It gives that extra confidence. But see, at the end of the day, you have to go there every day and execute your plans and we have done well so far. (On Mayank Yadav's injury) I don't know what is happening. I had a brief chat and he seemed okay, which is a positive. Whatever conversation I have had, whatever we see, he has a good head on his shoulder. Really excited to see how his carer pans out.

11:11pm At the half-way stage, it might have seemed the Super Giants were a little par. As it turned out, they weren't, and much of it was down to how well they bowled. They were put under pressure early, with Gill and Sudharsan getting the Titans off to a decent start. Once the latter fell to Thakur on the final ball of the powerplay, though, things went south for the 2022 champions.

None of their middle-order batters got going, and they kept finding ways to get out. Williamson perished to a sensational catch, while some of the other batters' shot selection left a bit to be desired. Tewatia got a few boundaries away towards the end but that only reduced the margin of defeat, rather than acting as a catalyst for a turnaround.

Coming back to LSG, Thakur picked up his career-best IPL figures, finishing with a five-wicket haul. Krunal was also very impressive, giving away only 11 runs in four overs and accounting for three batters. Bishnoi and Naveen also chipped in, ensuring that LSG, once they got the momentum in their bowling innings, never relented.

postText:
Thanks for joining us. This is Shashank Kishore saying goodbye on behalf of Ashish Pant and Chandan Duroah. Cheers, take care.

11.01pm CSK have turned a banana peel of a chase into an absolute cruise at dewy Chepauk. Ravindra Jadeja led their turnaround after KKR set themselves up superbly in the Powerplay, and then with the bat, Gaikwad and Mitchell laid the foundation of a chase that they were always in control of. And that means, KKR have been consigned to their first defeat this season.

Ravindra Jadeja is PoM for his 3/18. "My title hasn't yet been verified, hopefully they'll give me one [laughs]. I always enjoy my bowling on this track. I was hoping the ball grips a little, if you bowl in the right areas with helps you. For visiting teams it takes time to settle in and plan, you hardly get 2-3 days, for a visiting team to come here, play and identify the surface is little difficult. We know our conditions better."

Ruturaj Gaikwad: Bit of nostalgia for me. My first IPL fifty, Mahi bhai was with me to finish the match. With Jinx injured, onus was on me to bat through, didn't want to put the youngsters in a difficult situation. Was a 150-160 wicket. Jaddu always comes in after the power play with momentum in the spin department. With this team, I don't really need to tell things to anyone. Everyone's in a great head space, Mahi bhai and Fleming are still around to take those calls. I wouldn't say mine is a slow start, in T20s there are times you nick off one or two balls, sometimes you need a bit of luck to get going, maybe something for experts to talk about, with my strike rate (laughs)."

Daryl Mitchell: "Always nice to play in front of a special crowd, pretty cool. When you know surface is on the slower side, it's about building a partnership and take it as deep as we could. He's world class, for me it's coming up with plans to put pressure on those guys. The way Rutu got the job out there was amazing to see. There was a bit of turn and bounce, for us it was about building partnerships and allow ourselves into a position to finish it off. I don't mind wherever I bat, here to win games of cricket and get the job done.

Shreyas Iyer, tonight's losing captain: It's deafening out here, will try to express how I'm feeling. We fell short in terms of assessing the wicket. Phenomenal start in the power play but we couldn't capitalize. Couldn't assess conditions, pitch completely changed after power play and to score runs, it wasn't easy. They know conditions pretty well, bowled according to their plan. It was tacky, wasn't easy to go big right from first ball. It changed tremendously after power play and the way we were trying to construct our innings, didn't go to plan. We take those learnings and move forward. We were in a comfortable place, thought 160-170 was a great score. That was our plan but when you lose consecutive wickets it's difficult to carry forward momentum. Have to go back to our drawing board and learn, just a matter of one match and one innings, glad it happened at the start of the tournament. When we go back, we know our home conditions pretty well, important to analyze and assess situations and make the best use of it.

7:27pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, and there is a roar from the crowd as the Punjab Kings fielders emerge. Head and Abhishek will open the batting, so no surprises there. Rabada to take the new ball - the first time he is doing so this season. Head on strike - here we go!

7:20pm Just about ten minutes to go for the first ball. SRH have batted first on two occasions; scoring 277 and following it up with a more sedate 162 against the Titans. What kind of batting innings do they have in store for us tonight?

Shrikant : "Why Rahul Tripathi is not in playing 11 this year?" -- SRH's top order seems stacked, with Abhishek, Head and Markram all in good form, with Klaasen to follow. Plus, Tripathi did look scratchy in their opening game against KKR.

Suresh: "Who will be the Impact Sub for SRH? Markande or Umran?" -- No specific news on that at the toss. Cummins did mention they were going in with the same team, which could mean Markande coming in when SRH bowl. That said, if there is pace and bounce in the surface, they could be tempted to bring in Umran.

Punjab Kings XI: Shikhar Dhawan (c), Jonny Bairstow, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Sam Curran, Sikandar Raza, Shashank Singh, Ashutosh Sharma, Harpreet Brar, Harshal Patel, Kagiso Rabada, Arshdeep Singh

PBKS bench: Prabhsimran Singh, Nathan Ellis, Tanay Thyagarajan, Rahul Chahar, Rishi Dhawan

Sunrisers Hyderabad XI: Travis Head, Abhishek Sharma, Aiden Markram, Heinrich Klaasen (wk), Shahbaz Ahmed, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Abdul Samad, Pat Cummins (c), Bhuvneshwar Kumar, T Natarajan, Jaydev Unadkat

SRH bench: Umran Malik, Mayank Markande, Washington Sundar, Glenn Phillips, Rahul Tripathi

7pm Right. It is time for the toss. Cummins and Dhawan are out in the middle. Dhawan gives the coin a flick. Heads is the call, and tails it is. Punjab Kings will bowl first. Dhawan says the pitch is likely to remain the same and they want to know what they are chasing. Adds they were lucky they won the last game and that there is no dependency on certain players, with everyone standing up. They are looking forward to another win today. Livingstone is still recovering, and hopefully he will be back for the next game.

Cummins says he would have bowled first too but on a new venue, he does not mind batting first. They are happy with how they are playing. It has been fun and exciting to be a part of, he says. Says they have lots of options with the new ball and at the death, and that is the reason he is bowling more in the middle overs.

6:50pm The last time these sides met, Shikhar Dhawan produced a magnificent unbeaten 99, putting together a 55-run final-wicket stand in the process. It was in vain, though, with Markram and Rahul Tripathi ensuring SRH cruised to an eight-wicket win.

The previous three games between these franchises have been won by the chasing team, and in the only IPL game at this venue, PBKS won batting second. Win the toss and bat second then? Toss in 10.

Nick: "You feel if Bairstow doesn't score runs today, he might get replaced" -- He has not gone big so far this IPL but he has looked in decent touch in his last two games. Maybe tonight's the night...

Pitch Report: Slightly skewed square boundaries tonight: 63m to one side, 70m to the other. 72m hit straight down the ground, with the shortest and longest pocket being 56m and 75m, respectively. Simon Katich reckons the pitch might play similar to how it did during the Punjab Kings-Delhi Capitals game. He says it is a very good wicket, calling it a 200-run pitch. It is rock hard and there is an even coverage of grass. He reckons SRH will enjoy batting on this, as will the Kings. There has not been a lot of dew in the past couple of days, and it might be the same tonight as well.

6:40pm Shashank Singh helped the Punjab Kings script a remarkable victory away to the Gujarat Titans just days ago. This, thus, is the perfect time to jump into this piece, tracing his journey every step of the way.

6:30pm There will be plenty of familiar faces across both camps. Jonny Bairstow and Shikhar Dhawan, who will likely open for the Punjab Kings tonight, donned the SRH orange once upon a time. Shashank Singh, PBKS' hero against the Gujarat Titans, and who made headlines at the auction (for no fault of his), like Bairstow, also made his IPL debut for SRH.

Flip it around, and Mayank Agarwal was one of two players PBKS retained ahead of the 2022 mega auction, only to be released a year later. Aiden Markram was not retained at all and found his way to SRH, where he has become a vital cog.

6:25pm ICYMI: Wanindu Hasaranga, who was bought by SRH to bolster their spin-bowling stocks, has been ruled out for the season, with Sri Lankan spinner Vijayakanth Viyaskanth replacing him.

6:20pm Four matches, four points. A win in their last game against the 2023 finalists, a 100% record at home, and a chance to get closer to table-toppers Rajasthan Royals: the circumstances that precede this contest and what is at stake, appear uncannily similar.

Both the Punjab Kings and the Sunrisers Hyderabad have points to prove too. Neither made the playoffs last year. In fact, it has been ten years since PBKS (Kings XI Punjab then) did so, whereas SRH last tasted playoff action in 2020.

These teams have traversed different paths up to this point, even winning their respective last encounters in contrasting fashion. But tonight, they are on a collision course, and only one will be able to emerge from this scuffle unscathed, making their fans rejoice tonight, and perhaps proclaiming to the rest of the IPL that they are the real deal in 2024.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the IPL. It is Match 23, and the Punjab Kings are back at home, where they won their opening game and where they will play their next four matches. Up against them are the Sunrisers Hyderabad, who are yet to win on the road this season but have a 14-7 record against the Kings in the IPL. postText:
9:15pm An innings of two halves, really. In the first half, the ball was doing all sorts and PBKS reduced SRH to 66-4. They could not get rid of Nitish, though, and he stood tall, even as those around him perished. He registered his maiden IPL fifty and finished with 64 off 37. Samad, Shahbaz and Head also played cameos, and those knocks have helped SRH to get to 182, which did not seem llikely at the half-way stage.

Arshdeep was the standout bowler for the hosts. His last over went for 15 but with the new ball, he looked unplayable at times. He broke the back of SRH's top order, with a two-wicket over that included the scalps of Head and Markram. Arshdeep then returned later to rip out Samad and Nitish, ensuring that SRH did not threaten a 200-plus score.

Curran and Harshal picked up two wickets apiece, while Rabada accounted for Cummins. PBKS will be relatively happy with the score they have to chase. SRH, though, will also feel they can make a match out of this, especially if they start well. Join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Arshdeep Singh: There was some movement to start off with. It was a little sticky. Then the dew came in and the wicket settled a little bit. I was very happy till the third over. It was a really good day, was trying to stick to my plans and deliver for my team. Hitting boundaries straight is relatively easy than hitting it square, so trying to make the most of it, and tried to use the wicket. Tried to bowl into the wicket and bowl wide yorkers also.

7:37pm There is plenty of pink in the crowd, and they are thoroughly enjoying themselves, grooving to the music the DJ is playing. The umpires make their way out to the middle now. Buttler and Jaiswal will open, and the latter could do with some runs here. Umesh with the new ball for the Titans. Jaiswal on strike. Slip in place - here we go!

Gujarat Titans XI: Shubman Gill (c), Sai Sudharsan, Vijay Shankar, Abhinav Manohar, Matthew Wade (wk), Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Noor Ahmad, Umesh Yadav, Spencer Johnson, Mohit Sharma

GT bench: BR Sharath, Shahrukh Khan, Darshan Nalkande, Manav Suthar, Sai Kishore

Rajasthan Royals XI: Jos Buttler, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sanju Samson (c & wk), Riyan Parag, Dhruv Jurel, Shimron Hetmyer, R Ashwin, Trent Boult, Avesh Khan, Kuldeep Sen, Yuzvendra Chahal

RR bench: Rovman Powell, Tanush Kotian, Shubham Dubey, Keshav Maharaj, Navdeep Saini

7:25pm It's toss time. Gill and Samson are out in the middle. Samson gives it a twirl. Gill calls heads, and heads it is. Gujarat Titans will bowl first. He says that if rain is around, it is always better to be chasing than batting first. Not ideal to select a playing eleven with main players getting injured. Couple of changes for GT - Matthew Wade comes in for Kane Williamson, and Abhinav Manohar comes in too. Concedes they were in very good positions in the last two matches and they want to finish off games ruthlessly now. Adds that he does not really think about captaincy when he is batting, and when in the field, he is looking to enjoy and giving the players confidence.

Samson says he does not mind batting now, although he wanted to bowl first too. He is thankful for the support he has received as he leads RR out for the 50th time tonight. There have been lots of challenges, despite their winning streak, and adds they want to keep concentrating on the process. Samson, when asked about the changes to his team, is not sure, and smiles sheepishly.

7:20pm Four of the five matches played between these two sides have been won by the chasing team. Last Saturday, RR chased down 184 against RCB rather comfortably. The first two games of the season, though, were won by the team defending. What shall the captain winning the toss do, especially now that rain is around?

Here is the pitch report, although this was done before the rain arrived: Pitch no.4 is being used tonight. Slightly incongruent square boundaries - 62m to one side, 70m to the other. Aaron Finch says it looks like a really good wicket, but there is a hint of green grass, which means there could be some pace in it. Adds he would look to play really straight as an opener as there might be movement early on. But as the game goes on, it could get slower. No dew expected because of the overhead conditions.

7:12pm We have official confirmation. The toss will take place at 7:25pm (local time), with the first ball set to be bowled at 7:40pm (local time). Just a ten-minute delay on the original starting time.

7:07pm The cover on the square is also coming off now. Another sign that the rain might have relented and that we might not be too far away from the toss.

7:03pm Good news, folks. The cover that was covering the run-up area, is now being removed. Only the cover on the square remains now.

7pm Nothing new to report, unfortunately. The covers are still on. There are a few threatening clouds overhead. Fingers crossed that they blow over, and we can have some cricket real soon. The toss, by the way, has officially been delayed.

6:50pm As we wait for the rain to relent, here is what happened between these two sides last season. They played each other twice, with both of those games being won by the away side. RR, riding on Shimron Hetmyer's pyrotechnics, got the job done in Ahmedabad, but the Titans, led by Rashid Khan, demolished the Royals in Jaipur. GT will not mind something of that ilk tonight as well.

Cricfan: "Is it a huge rain? Or will it be a quick start once the drizzle stops? " -- It is not raining cats and dogs, but it is steady rain, and the covers are in full operation.

6:38pm First things first, it is drizzling in Jaipur. No word yet on whether that has affected when the toss takes place, but this is unexpected. The covers are on, and this is a dampener (quite literally) ahead of what promises to be a sizzling contest.

6:30pm And then there was one. Just the one team with a spotless, unblemished record at this year's IPL. The Rajasthan Royals have won batting first. They have won chasing. They have won at home, they have won away. Their batters are scoring runs, their bowlers are taking wickets. And they have cast themselves as the team to beat this season.

RR's run, in many ways, is similar to what the Gujarat Titans achieved in their first two seasons. This campaign has been a little different for GT, though. Injuries have played a part, but a 2-3 record after five games is still short of their standards.

A trip to Jaipur, keeping all that in mind, might not be what the Titans would have wanted. More so because RR are only behind the Chennai Super Kings when it comes to winning at home.

When viewed from another perspective, however, this is perhaps just what the Titans need. An away win, especially against the pace-setters, could reinvigorate their campaign, and tell everyone that they will not give up their playoff status so easily.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of Match 24 of IPL 2024. It is the Rajasthan Royals, hoping to go 5-0 and grow their aura of invincibility, up against the Gujarat Titans, longing to get their teeth stuck into this campaign. Hop on, this should be some game!

preText:
We will start with offspinner Mohammad Nabi.

Rose: "Faf/Kohli selfishness will cost RCB. Jacks is a brilliant attacking opener and both of them can play at 3 (if it were up to me I'd go Jacks, Kohli, Faf as the top 3). RCB management have shot themselves in the foot making Faf captain, they've missed out on Finn Allen and now Will Jacks opening because of him"

Sujatha : "Unlike popular opinions, Cam Green is a batter who needs atleast 10 balls to get set. He is not a basher from the word go. So , he is not like DK / MSD who thrive during those last 12-18 balls of an innings."

7.22pm Solid crowd over here at the Wankhede. General tickets for this game are unavailable due to its popularity. Its been hard to get tickets for any away RCB game to be fair, unless you were an early bird.

Harrish: "Is SKY fit ? is he playing?" -- Here are the XIs. SKY is currently not in the fielding XI but is in the bench.

Shubham: "@Soumya-Why Gopal will be replaced by impact player?Instead MI can replace already out batsmanĺwith impact player so that Gopal can bat if required"

Sowmya : "Shreyas Gopal is a better option than Piyush Chawla (better bowler , better batter and better fielder). Don't see him batting though as he might be replaced with an Impact player."

Faf was quite clear in stating Jacks will bat No. 3. But Jacks has opened in 125 of his 149 T20 innings. At No. 3, his top score in 14 innings is 40, with an average of 16.92.

To summarise, RCB are without Cam Green with Will Jacks at No. 3. Lomror, who was on the bench, is back in the XI. Mumbai have opted to bring Shreyas Gopal as the like-for-like replacement for Piyush Chawla.

Toss: Mumbai Indians win the toss. They will bowl first. "Similar track but in the evening might be better to bat on," Hardik says. "There was dew last couple of days. (Mood after win?) Mood before and after the win has been the same. We play every game with a fresh start. Want to put early pressure with the new ball. (Team effort last time) I heard it was the highest score without anyone scoring fifty, gives confidence to us that even one guy batting long we can score 234. At the same time, bowlers held their nerve in the powerplay well. (Prefer chasing here?) It has been a chasing ground and looking at the tradition. Shreyas comes in for Piyush Chawla.

Du Plessis: "We've tried to change a few things around. Our plan today is to bring a few fresh faces and give them chances. We want to make as few changes as possible but when you reach yourself in this position where you don't play your best cricket, then you have to make a brave decision. The sixth game is the right time to do that. Virat has been excellent with consistency, but that's what is frustrating, we can't look at the opposition and say they've outplayed us. We've not done as well. But with T20 cricket, we are close to turning it around. Mumbai got that in their last game and we are looking to do the same. Three changes: Jacks comes in at No. 3. Mahipal is back. And Vyshak too."

In other news, Injured Mayank Yadav 'unlikely to play' next two games for LSG, says Justin Langer

Debut for Will Jacks (RCB) today. Does that mean Maxwell / Green are not playing?! Maxwell caught up with Neroli Meadows at ESPN Australia yesterday to discuss how one can 'find form' when they are struggling while in our ESPNcricinfo studios in India, Tom Moody and Mitch McClenaghan have said they find Green's role in the RCB 'confusing and unsettling.'

S Sudarshanan is at the venue and says its a humid evening. He can spot Hardik and Madhwal training together, and the trio of Siraj, Vyshak and Akash Deep marking their run-ups.

Sasikanth: "Faf should drop himself for Jacks. Jacks and Green should open with Kohli at No. 3. RCB needs an aggressive start that Kohli can then take forward. A quick 20 from Green can still add a lot more value than 15 of 15 balls down the order."

Tim David: [Playing in Mumbai] Important to get that first win. It is a great feeling for the camp to get that first win. Normally it is a pretty good batting pitch. [Role] I have to finish things off. I have had to bat a bit more long, and I have fired, a couple of big sixes in the end. [Going up against the Aussies] Will be good to get over the other Aussie boys. [Game-plan] We have to take one game and a time, might sound cliched but that's how it is. We have a strong squad, and if we can perform together we can win.

What would've pleased Mumbai so much in their win from Sunday is that they won their first game of the season despite Suryakumar Yadav making 0. SKY will be bubbling to get off the mark with a big score tonight and yesterday he addressed the media where he said that rehab helped him grow both as a player and a person.

6.33pm Since 2016, RCB have never beaten Mumbai in Mumbai. Tonight, too, the focus will be on whether their inexperienced middle order can tackle the Mumbai bowlers. Also they need runs from Maxwell and Green. According to the match preview, Mumbai might look to put more pressure by going with extra spinners because of RCB's poor numbers against them this season.

6.25pm It's the battle between India's financial capital and India's tech capital, but from a cricketing perspective, the stocks are down for both Mumbai Indians and Royal Challengers Bengaluru. Positioned at eighth and ninth respectively and with more than a third of the season over, there's no more place for fun and games. Every game matters for both sides - Mumbai hope to make it two wins in two after winning last Sunday, while RCB want to avoid losing their fourth game in a row.

Jasprit Bumrah is the player of the match: Very happy with the outcome. I will never say I wanted to take a five-for. The wicket was sticky and I am very happy with the contribution. In this format it is very harsh for the bowlers. I try to not be a one-trick pony, I have worked on this early in the career. People start to line you up. I want to have different skills. Bowling is tough, because you will have to take a beating. When things have not worked out for me the next day I have seen the videos and analyzed what did not work. Preparation is always the key. Important to keep pushing yourself before a game. It is not a one-trick pony. You don't always have to bowl a yorker, sometimes you bowl a yorker, sometimes short ball. There is no ego in this format. You can bowl145, but sometimes it is important to bowl slower balls.

2) And the 11th time where Royal Challengers Bengaluru failed to defend a target of 190-plus runs, also joint-most in T20s, alongside Punjab Kings. (edited)

3) Top three fastest successful 190-plus target chases in the IPL in terms of run rate have been by Mumbai Indians.

4) 50th win for MI at Wankhede, the first team to reach 50 wins in the IPL at a venue. (Not including super over wins)

Suryakumar Yadav: It is always good to be back in Wankhede. Joining the squad was great. Mentally I was here, just physically in Bangalore. Great to be back, Coming at Wankhede chasing 200 if there is dew it is important to take a chance. Wanted to finish early for the net run rate. [On his shots over point] I just try to play the field. I practice these shots. It is in my muscle memory. [Favorite shot] I think all the shots. The slice over point was my favourite. [Kishan] That's what we have told him. Just go out and enjoy. His intent has been great. He is enjoying the fruits. [Bumrah] It is always good to have Jasprit by your side. It has been 2to 3 years, have never batted Jasprit in the nets. Either he breaks my bat or my foot.

Faf du Plessis: Very tough pill to follow. It was very wet out there, it will be nice to win a toss somehow. Credit to MI how they came out and made our bowlers make a lot of mistakes. Anyone that came in and found the middle of the bat. We spoke about it. [Dew] We knew the dew would play a big part. We needed 215-220. 190 wasn't enough. It is a big thing at some venues. When the dew settles in, it was very tough. We changed the ball many times. It is the only sport where the changes in conditions make a difference. We need that score board pressure. We fought with the bat. We lost crucial wickets at crucial stages. We had to rebuild a lot of the times. The guys played positively. [On Bumrah] He has been the difference in the two innings. We put them under pressure but the one guy, being out there myself, and you see him with the ball in his hand. You want to put him under pressure, but the variety does everyone in. He has got a really good bouncer, slower ball. Someone like Malinga was the best bowler in T20 cricket, but Bumrah has taken over the reins. You know you can bring him on and take the wickets but also be defensive. [What went wrong] I feel like from a batting perspective, we have to push for that 200. We don't have as many weapons in our bowling. So it comes down to the batting. From a bowling perspective, we have lacked penetration. We have to get them two or three down in the powerplay. Always feels like we are on the back foot after the first four overs.

Kaustubh: "Every aspiring bowler must listen carefully what Bumrah said in the post-match"

Naveen Kumar : "So looks like another typical season of Mumbai losing initial few matches and then stringing together wins to get into playoffs. But the bowling mill is clearly not upto the mark yet, barring boom boom."

Pratik Soholkar: "Not a single go to bowler for RCB..they need to bring Lockie now for sure.."

11.15pm Phew, what a chase this has been from Mumbai. They have come out and knocked the wind out of RCB's sails. It was not an easy pitch to defend, but the way MI have gone about the chase, will just uplift them beyond belief. After the first two overs, there was no swing whatsoever for the RCB bowlers and Kishan cashed in. It was Siraj's second over that went for 23 runs which got MI's motor running. MI raced to 100 in 8.3 overs and even when Kishan and Rohit fell, they kept going. Suryakumar came in and hit five fours and four sixes in his 19-ball 52 lighting up the Wankhede crowd. Pandya and Tilak then came in and took MI over the line with 27 balls to spare. RCB's season has now gone from bad to worse.
