DC: 1 Prithvi Shaw, 2 David Warner, 3 Shai Hope, 4 Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), 5 Tristan Stubbs, 6 Axar Patel, 7 Jake Fraser-McGurk, 8 Kuldeep Yadav, 9 Mukesh Kumar, 10 Ishant Sharma, 11 Khaleel Ahmed. Impact Subs: Richardson, Porel, Kushagra, Sumit and Dubey

LSG: 1 Quinton de Kock, 2 KL Rahul (capt, wk), 3 Devdutt Padikkal, 4 Marcus Stoinis, 5 Nicholas Pooran, 6 Ayush Badoni, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Ravi Bishnoi, 9 Yash Thakur, 10 Naveen-ul-Haq, 11 Arshad Khan. Impact Subs: Gowtham, Hooda, Siddharth, Mishra and Henry

7pm It is cloudy and windy in Lucknow at the moment, as we get closer to the action. LSG win the toss and bat. "This is the first time we are playing on this surface," he says. So presumably, it is a fresh pitch. Arshad Khan replaces Mayank Yadav for LSG. Pant would have batted first too, he says. "We're trying to find our best XI," Pant confesses. Mukesh and Kuldeep are back for DC.

6.50pm There are a few questions to answer for the visiting DC side. One of them is about their fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who has incessantly leaked runs to sit on top of the list of the most expensive bowlers this IPL. But is the problem actually with DC's usage of Nortje? Our experts weigh in. And is DC's poor season already putting their head coach Ricky Ponting under pressure? Ponting's former Australia team-mate Michael Clarke feels the former needs to find a way out.

Akhil: "I don't understand why we are talking about Pant and Rahul being contenders for the World Cup. The leading wicket-keepers have to be Sanju and Karthik based on their performances" --- Karthik's days are all but gone, with him even set to end his IPL career after this season. As for Samson, one of him and Rahul could be part of the squad as a reserve keeper or batter if Pant makes it. But as has been told by the boss, Pant qualifies for the T20 World Cup only if he's able to keep wicket

6.40pm LSG could take the spin route to win again. Krunal Pandya, Ravi Bishnoi and M Siddharth had restricted Gujarat Titans during the hosts' successful defense of 163 a few nights back; so why would LSG want to deviate from producing a spin-friendly pitch again? Here's the preview looking forward to their game against DC, who are yet to beat LSG in three attempts so far. In other news for the day, LSG's special talent Mayank Yadav has all but been ruled out of their next two matches, as coach Justin Langer confirmed last evening.

Kuldeep Yadav: "I got injured in the first match - it was a groin issue - and it got aggravated since I also played in the second match. [I am] getting better. We've played well, other than against KKR, which was a one-sided match. Size of the grounds doesn't matter - all sixes go out of it anyway!"

6.30pm It's between Rahul and Pant's sides tonight at the IPL, and it could entirely come down to which one among those two finds a spot in India's squad for the T20 World Cup that follows. While Rahul has had middling numbers so far this IPL, Pant has been better and more impactful. But leaving aside talk about the future for later, the story of the IPL sides they are leading at present is contrasting to their own performances. LSG are No. 3 on the points table, with three wins on the bounce, while DC are lying at the bottom after four losses in five matches. In Lucknow tonight, the visitors will be hoping that they can start ticking.

postText:
Thanks for joining us. It's the first win on the road for DC. From Himanshu, Thilak and myself, Shashank, it's a very goodnight. Take care and see you soon.

11.11pm A look of relief on Ponting's face. Ganguly can afford a smile. Pant is a little more animated. This has been a comfortable win.

Capitals had LSG in tatters courtesy a magical Kuldeep spell, before their bowling came a cropper in the death against unheralded Ayush Badoni and Arshad Khan. Chasing a lot more than they looked like at one stage, they lost Warner early, but Frazer-McGurk on debut and Pant played superb knocks to take the sting out of LSG.

Kuldeep Yadav is the PoM for 3 for 20. "Wasn't fit for a couple of games, got injured in the first game. Was difficult to see the team struggle in the middle overs. Credit to Patrick for maintaining me. All those were good wickets, when you get three in the middle overs and control the run rate as well as chasing target, it's good. I liked the first wicket, played a lot against Pooran. Execution was right, that was a good ball. I was clear with my plan, length matters a lot as a spinner. Irrespective of format good length is good length."

Rishabh Pant: Relieved. Told boys we need to think like champions, keep fighting hard. There have been phases where we've not been upto the mark with the ball but some individuals have to take responsibility. We have to stick together as a team. Problem we had is so many injuries in the camp. With 10 teams, difficult to get players. We can either make an excuse or learn. Most probably [we've found our No. 3], haven't thought a lot yet. Take it one match at a time.

Jake Frazer-McGurk: Spent five-six games on the sidelines itching to get out there, stoked! Was just more about trying not to swing too hard and lose shape. That's what I've done over the last 12 months. I loved the one over cover, pretty happy with that. Don't usually hit many over the off-side. Batting out of the powerplay is something am contiuing to learn, it'll come with experience. I'm so happy to be here, different world in terms of cricket. Never seen anything like it, to be able to savour eight weeks, hopefully more, is amazing.

KL Rahul: We were 15-20 short, should've capitalised to get 180. There was a bit of help for seamers, odd-ball was keeping low and Kuldeep put the brakes on our batting group. We fought till the end. McGurk, the new guys when they come in, was very unknown. We've watched a lot of videos of him but he hit the ball really well, credit to him. We walked in with the same kind of mindset, assess what the good areas, what pace works on this wicket and execute as well as we can. We got Warner, and a couple after the powerplay. We were in the game till the 10th over, then a drop catch and then Rishabh-McGurk took it away from us. In hindsight, can wonder if we could've done something differently [with Pooran's batting position]. Not much spin for Axar, so I thought Nicky P with the shots he has can put the opposition under pressure. We knew they had to bowl their spinners in that phase. Mayank is not too bad, he looks good, feeling good but we also want to make sure we don't rush him back in too early. He's young, we need to protect his body. He's itching to go, we just have to pull him back a little, maybe a couple of more games, before he comes back.

7:27pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the RR fielders. It will be Taide opening the batting for the Punjab Kings, with Bairstow alongside him. The England batter could do with a few runs here. Boult, as usual, will take the new ball. This could be a key period in the game, especially if the ball moves around as it did on Tuesday. Taide on strike. One slip in place - here we go!

7:20pm Tonight is also a brilliant opportunity for Taide, who managed two fifties in seven innings in the IPL last year. In this season's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he scored 302 runs in seven innings for Vidarbha - at a strike rate of 169.66. It will be interesting to see where he bats, though, with Prabhsimran also capable of opening the batting.

Shivang Madaan: "What are your thoughts on Sikander Raza being left out after not a bad game last time around?" -- Think Raza going out has more to do with Livingstone being fit again. The other option could have been to exclude Bairstow but with Dhawan also missing, PBKS perhaps need a bit of experience at the top of the order.

7:10pm Plenty of changes to keep track of. RR will definitely miss Buttler and Ashwin. Powell, though, adds middle-order muscle while Kotian had an excellent Ranji Trophy campaign just before the IPL. The Kings, rather interestingly, have omitted Ashutosh, who struck the ball cleanly against the Titans and against SRH the other night. They could still bring him in as an Impact Player, but with PBKS batting first, it might require a collapse for that to happen.

Punjab Kings XI: Atharva Taide, Jonny Bairstow, Prabhsimran Singh, Sam Curran (c), Liam Livingstone, Shashank Singh, Jitesh Sharma (wk), Harpreet Brar, Harshal Patel, Kagiso Rabada, Arshdeep Singh

PBKS bench: Rahul Chahar, Ashutosh Sharma, Vidwath Kaverappa, Harpreet Bhatia, Nathan Ellis

Rajasthan Royals XI: Sanju Samson (c & wk), Riyan Parag, Rovman Powell, Shimron Hetmyer, Dhruv Jurel, Tanush Kotian, Trent Boult, Keshav Maharaj, Avesh Khan, Kuldeep Sen, Yuzvendra Chahal

RR bench: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Tom Kohler-Cadmore, Shubham Dubey, Navdeep Saini, Abid Mushtaq

7pm It's toss time. Curran, the home captain, is stood there alongside Samson. Curran gives it a flick. Heads is the call by Samson, and heads it is. Rajasthan Royals will bowl first. Says it looks like a decent wicket to bowl first. Adds that they have, since the season started, focussed on not thinking too much about the goal. Lots of things have been happening, he says, with a few players not being 100% fit for this game. Buttler and Ashwin are having niggles, with Powell and Kotian coming in.

Dhawan has picked up a bit of a niggle, says Curran, and he hopes he can perform well for the team. Reckons they would have bowled first too but now that they are batting, they want to get some nice runs on the board. The middle order has been been finishing well, he says. Livingstone is back, and Taide comes in for Dhawan.

6:56pm The first big news from Mullanpur is that Sam Curran is walking out for the toss, instead of Shikhar Dhawan. We will possibly have more news on why Dhawan is missing at the toss, which is scheduled to take place at 7pm (local time).

Pitch Report: We are back to Pitch No.4, which was used for the Punjab Kings-Delhi Capitals fixture. 75m hit straight down the ground. 67m square boundary to one side, 64m to the other. Shortest and longest pocket are 60m and 73m, respectively. There is a tinge of green on the surface and the pitch is 100% black soil. Water retention could be higher, says Daren Ganga and he expects the pacers to get seam movement and be dominant. Bowling a good length, just in and around off stump could be the key to keeping teams under 50 in the powerplay. Dew could come into play but Ganga says you can also win batting first by getting an above par total. Above 180 could be par on this track.

Matthew: "Wonder whether Boult will bowl his full quota this time? Was a very bizarre choice to leave him with 2 overs left last match, surely? " -- The decision was indeed quite puzzling, especially with RR also going on to lose the game. Mitchell McClenaghan certainly thinks the Royals should trust him more at the death.

6:40pm Jonny Bairstow has not been in great form so far this season, scoring only 81 runs across five innings at an average of 16.20. Our experts weigh in on the amount of pressure he might be under.

6:30pm The last five matches between these two teams have all gone into the last over. Rajasthan have won three of those, with Punjab winning the other two. In their first meeting in 2021, Sanju Samson's sublime hundred went in vain; in the other, Kartik Tyagi conceded just a run off the last over to defend four.

In 2023, Dhruv Jurel, coming on as an Impact Player, almost broke Punjab hearts in Guwahati, before landing the more decisive blow in Dharamsala. And way back in 2015, a Super Over had to be summoned to separate the two sides.

6:20pm The streak is over. For 35 overs on Wednesday, it seemed as if the Rajasthan Royals' winning run would continue, only for the Gujarat Titans to snap it in extraordinary fashion. Not panic stations yet for the Royals. No team has more points than them at this stage, and a solitary loss after five games is hardly a crisis.

But the Royals will be quietly aware of what happened last season. They had four wins in their first five matches, and then stumbled their way to a fifth-place finish. Tonight, thus, is the perfect opportunity for them to illustrate how much they have learnt from 2023.

Like the Royals, the Punjab Kings were denied at the death in a home game. Ashutosh Sharma and Shashank Singh almost mounted a daring heist but fell short by two runs. A defeat of that ilk would have stung. That they came so close, despite seemingly being out of it at one stage, could help fuel their charge for tonight, though.

So, here we are: in Mullanpur for the latest instalment of arguably the most keenly-contested IPL rivalry in the past few years. Both of these sides have been around since it all began in 2008, and have played out some enthralling encounters (more on that in a bit).

Tonight should be no different. An RR win and the defeat to GT might be cast aside as an aberration. A Punjab victory, and there will be renewed belief that this is their year, while making the Royals revisit a past sequence they're longing want to forget.

postText:
9:13pm 72 runs came off the last six overs, and that has given this score some sort of respectability. Livingstone and Jitesh did their bits, but it was all down to Ashutosh, omitted initially but then making his impact as, well, the Impact Player. Prior to that, Bairstow, Curran, Prabhsimran and Shashank all struggled, either picking the wrong options or not showing enough intent to throw the RR bowlers off their plans.

Speaking of RR, the spinners were the pick of the bunch. Maharaj, in particular, was impressive, bagging a two-wicket haul and only conceding 23 across four overs. Chahal accounted for Prabhsimran, moving to within two of the 200-wicket mark in the IPL. Boult, as always, was exceptional at the top and held his own in the final over, with Avesh and Sen also chipping in.

This pitch, compared to the PBKS-SRH game the other day, does seem a little trickier, although 147 does not seem a lot at this stage. PBKS will have to fight for every run in the field to make this total feel bigger, and to prevent the Royals from making it five wins out of six. Join us in a bit for the run-chase!

Keshav Maharaj: (On Chahal) He has been phenomenal. He is someone I can feed information off, and a privilege to bowl alongside him. (On the pitch) It was starting to get better at the end. It was a bit stoppy at the start. Hopefully we have restricted them to enough and we can chase it down. Not a lot of dew. When the ball got older, it looked a bit truer, and it was more reactive when the ball was newer. Huge privilege to be a part of this team. Learning and trying to evolve my game.

postText:
11:45pm And...that brings us to the end of another Punjab Kings-Rajasthan Royals classic. This did not rattle along at breakneck speed throughout, but when push came to shove, it was quite a spectacle. Such finishes in the IPL seem commonplace this season, and tomorrow, we have two possible humdingers in store.

KKR host LSG in the afternoon, before the Mumbai Indians take on the Chennai Super Kings at the Wankhede Stadium. Do join us for both of those matches. Until then, this is goodbye from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo. Goodnight and take care!

Shimron Hetmyer, Player of the Match: (On his mindset) It is just practice really, I try as much as possible to bat properly in the nets first. Then I go back after everyone has finished to try and hit sixes. (On being so effective as a finisher) It is a blessing and a curse. Sometimes it happens, sometimes it doesn't. Happy I could help my team win tonight. (On if thoughts of failure ever come in) They creep in, but afterwards, I just try to keep it as clear as possible. After the first few balls, he (Boult) came up to me and calmed me down. I would have taken it (the single in the final over). I spoke to Boulty and even if I don't get the other one, I will try my best to get the single and at least tie it. I was just tyring to get a single or a double and then I got the full toss, and tried to hit it for six. (On being such an effervescent character) Being away from family, it is the only way you can keep yourself upbeat, by just enjoying every moment and doing every thing you need to. (On dying his hair pink) Waiting for my wife to come, she will do it (laughs).

Sanju Samson, Rajasthan Royals captain: (On two or more fielders going for high catches) We had a few funny instances but I am happy everyone is eager to go and catch it. Gets a bit tough, because the stadium is full of noise. I need to tell my fast bowlers that it is easier to catch with gloves. (On if they were tensed during the chase) We all were. Games against Punjab in the last few overs, I don't know what it is, they are always close. It was a very funny game. (On Hetmyer) He has been doing it for years and years. He has confidence about his skills. Rovman and Hettie, having them, was good. He (Kotian) is a very interesting youngster. He came in as an all-rounder. Had a fabulous Ranji Trophy season. He has been impressing everyone in the nets. We had a proper settled batting order, so we did not want to unsettle it. Jos is almost ready for the next game and we wanted to try him (Kotian) up the order. Happy to see him (Jaiswal) spend time and get 30-40, hopefully he can have a big game next match. (On having five wins in six) You can never take it for granted. Last game, we did some really good things but ended up losing. Tonight, we made more mistakes and won. Cricket is a funny game, so you have to put your head down and just focus on the process.

Sam Curran, Punjab Kings captain: The wicket was slightly slow. We did not start very well with the bat and then finished off well, much like it was with them. It was a really good effort to get to what we did. Any time you get to 150, you are in the game. Unfortunately, another close one for us, but positive signs. We want to improve and get a few more runs. We bowled really well as a unit and fielded well. A little disappointed and we will bounce back in the next game. (On playing in Mullanpur) The conditions are new to everyone and we are adapting really well. Lost this in the final over and the other by two runs. Proud of the boys for staying in the game that long.

Rovman Powell: It is important for us to get two points, especially on the road. The other teams are creeping up (getting points), we just wanted to get a bit of separation. (Chat with Hetmyer) The good thing is we know each other, we are calm. All we needed to do was hit proper cricketing shots, and play along the ground. We are West Indians, we hit boundaries. In the previous games, the lower and middle order have not batted a lot of balls, and I told Hettie that there might be a day soon when they will have that opportunity. When I went out to bat, he just reminded me of that (smiles). (On when Buttler might be back) They are doing some good work with him. I think he is maybe out for a day or two. I think he will be back, the medical team is doing a fantastic job. (On Buttler's return possibly leading to his exclusion) I believe I am a decent player, and if I am not getting a game, the team is doing well. I try to stay patient and when I get my opportunity, I will try to contribute.

11:15pm This game seemed a slow-burn, until about five overs were left in the chase. But then, it exploded and it sparked into life. A flurry of wickets threw RR's chase into turmoil. Their West Indian batting pair, though, held their nerve. Hetmyer was there at the end, but do not discount the cameo Powell played, given PBKS were beginning to turn the screw at that point.

Jaiswal was also among the runs at the top of the order, and his innings sort of offset Kotian's struggles at the other end. The rest could not get going as much as they would have liked, but RR, having almost fallen into a hole they dug for themselves, will pleased that they ultimately emerged from the trenches unscathed.

The Punjab Kings will be gutted, having lost another game. But they will be proud of the effort their bowlers put in. 147 was not a massive score, and the only reason this game stretched into the final over was because of how disciplined most of their bowling attack was.

Rabada was at the forefront and his two-wicket salvo in the middle overs brought Punjab back. Curran and Livingstone were not bad either, and fulfilled their roles to perfection. Arshdeep and Harshal were not quite at the races, though, and the latter's 18th over, which went for 14 runs, definitively turned the game in RR's favour.

Plenty of positives, no doubt. But Punjab, having now lost four out of six, would want to translate these into tangible results soon. We will have the presentation in a bit.

3:27pm LSG coach Justin Langer rings the customary bell that signifies the start of play. The umpires now walk out, followed by the KKR fielders. Rahul and de Kock, in their changed maroon kit, will open the batting, and this powerplay could be crucial. Starc with the new ball. Can he get KKR the early breakthroughs they want? Wide slip in place for de Kock - here we go!

Tanz: "Shreyas said Rinku goes out since they are chasing. Do teams give the first 11 after the toss?" -- Yes, the playing elevens can be finalised after the toss.

3:20pm Just about ten minutes to go for the first ball. LSG have a superb record when defending totals in excess of 160, although in the last game they played, that previously spotless record suffered a blemish.

Sidd: "Cant wait to see how Shamar Joseph bowls in this match. Definitely my favorite bowler modern day"

3:10pm LSG have made a few changes, with Joseph's inclusion perhaps the most high-profile, given what he achieved at the Gabba a few months ago. Padikkal, who was struggling for rhythm, has also made way for Hooda, and Mohsin adding more variety to the attack.

KKR, on the other hand, have decided to have an extra pacer in place of Anukul Roy, which indicates what kind of surface they are expecting. Rinku will most likely come in as their Impact Player when they bat.

Kolkata Knight Riders XI: Phil Salt (wk), Sunil Narine, Venkatesh Iyer, Shreyas Iyer (c), Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Andre Russell, Ramandeep Singh, Mitchell Starc, Vaibhav Arora, Varun Chakravarthy, Harshit Rana

KKR bench: Suyash Sharma, Anukul Roy, Manish Pandey, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Rinku Singh

Lucknow Super Giants XI: KL Rahul (c & wk), Quinton de Kock, Deepak Hooda, Marcus Stoinis, Nicholas Pooran, Ayush Badoni, Krunal Pandya, Ravi Bishnoi, Yash Thakur, Shamar Joseph, Mohsin Khan

LSG bench: Arshad Khan, Prerak Mankad, M Siddharth, Amit Mishra, K Gowtham

3pm KL Rahul, clad in maroon, is out there for the toss, accompanied by Shreyas Iyer. Shreyas gives it a twirl. Heads is the call but it comes down as tails. KKR will bowl first. Shreyas says it feels nostalgic to be back after so long, and adds they were missing the energy of the home crowd. Great feeling to be back. He says he has no idea how the conditions will play, and that they have to take as much advantage of whatever is offer. Rinku goes out because they are bowling first, with Harshit Rana a part of the bowling eleven.

Rahul says he would have bowled first too but is not disappointed batting first. Reckons it is important to recover, and making sure everyone is well-rested. They are looking forward to a good game. Few changes for LSG. Padikkal and Naveen miss out. Hooda and Joseph come in, as does Mohsin Khan.

2:55pm Shamar Joseph has been handed his LSG cap, and looks like he will be making his debut today.

2:50pm All three previous encounters between these sides have been won by the side batting first. KKR, in the only game played at this venue, also won when they were defending. With heat also a factor, will the captains contemplate batting first? Toss in 10.

Pitch Report: It has been 22 days since an IPL game was last played here and it is very hot. 63m and 66m square boundaries, with a 73m hit down the ground. Michael Clarke says the wicket looks good for batting and that it is going to remain consistent. He reckons this is the fastest outfield in India and if batters can get in, they can cash in. Maximising the new ball will be key, both when batting first and when batting second.

Mustafa Moudi : "With 3 Wins already in their kitty, this is a golden opportunity for KKR to boost their Playoff Chances with 5 Continuous Matches at their Home - Eden. With No travelling or change in ground, they must capitalise on this opportunity!!"

2:40pm Gautam Gambhir, now back at KKR as their team mentor, will be plotting LSG's downfall today, the side he was mentoring in the last two seasons. All that and much more in Sreshth's preview.

2:30pm Three matches, three Lucknow Super Giants wins. That is what their head-to-head against the Kolkata Knight Riders looks like. In two of their most recent games, though, they were almost undone by Rinku Singh - once when he brought KKR to within a run, and two years ago, when he was only denied by an Evin Lewis stunner.

Now, though, Rinku has plenty of cavalry around him. Andre Russell is looking as good as he has ever done. Phil Salt and Sunil Narine are tearing teams apart in the powerplay. Shreyas Iyer and Venkatesh Iyer can be match-winners and young Angkrish Raghuvanshi has not missed a beat since debut.

So, can KKR break their rut against LSG? And can they do so on the back of a rather tepid display away to the Chennai Super Kings?

Home comfort might help KKR, but LSG, despite losing to the Delhi Capitals on Friday, are a top-quality side. They have been particularly efficient defending totals, and in their last game, captain KL Rahul showed signs of coming back to form. Oh, and like KKR, LSG will also be smarting after a defeat that brought their three-match winning streak to a grinding halt.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of Match 28 between the Kolkata Knight Riders and the Lucknow Super Giants. I am Shashwat Kumar and will be bringing to you all the action from the Eden Gardens. This is just the second game this season at this venue, but if it is even half as interesting as the last encounter here, we are in for lots of entertainment!

full and angling into off stump. Rahul tips it to mid off and hares across to the other end

shortText: Arora to de Kock, no run
text: length on leg stump. Shapes away from de Kock and opens up him. He prods at it and gets an outside edge that dribbles towards short third
preText: Stays over the wicket to de Kock

wkt_text: Q de Kock c Narine b Arora 10 (12m 8b 2x4 0x6) SR: 125.00
text: taken this time! de Kock perishes early! Fullish and slanted across the batter outside off. de Kock goes after it again, but does so with minimal footwork. Gets a thick outside edge and the ball floats to Narine at short third, who accepts the offering gleefully. Arora did not begin this over well, but he has certainly come back strong since!
sharp, short delivery on leg stump that climbs onto Hooda. He gets into an awkward tangle but manages to fend it into the ground on the leg side. Rahul is alert enough to sneak in a single
preText: Hooda in at 3. Wide slip in place

text: play and miss! Back of a length in the channel. Threatens to shape in before pitching and going on with the angle. Hooda goes feeling for it and is beaten all ends up
preText: Here's Sampath with an amazing stat: KL Rahul has hit a six on the third ball he faced in second game in succession. He had not hit a six inside the first three balls of his innings in the IPL between 2019 and 2023.

text: another play and miss! Hard length outside off, slanting away from the batter. Hooda fishes at it away from his body and is lucky to not nick it
brutish short ball that rears up just outside off. Hooda has to hop around his crease but does well to drop it behind point. Picks up a single for his toil
back of a length just outside off. Rahul dabs it towards backward point and calls Hooda through for the single
fires this down leg. Rahul does not get bat on it and the umpire has no qualms in calling it a wide
full just outside off. Hooda comes onto the front foot and pokes it back past the bowler for one
pulled away with disdain! Banged in short on leg stump, and it sits up for Rahul. He rocks back, swivels and hammers it behind square!
preText: The ball has done just enough so far, either bouncing more or sticking in the surface longer

text: back of a length delivery angled into off stump. Hooda waits in his crease and works it into the mid wicket region
length outside off. Rahul gets a half stride forward and prods it into the off side. That seemed to hit Rahul high on the bat
back of a length on leg stump. Rahul uses the angle and tucks it off his hips towards deep backward square leg
nicely done! Slower bumper on off. Gets up close to his grille but Hooda watches it all the way, taking his bottom hand off the stroke to help it over the keeper!
back of a length just outside off. Hooda presses half forward and defends
length outside off. A bit of hold in the surface and Hooda plonks it back to the bowler
shortish on leg stump. Rahul hops up onto his toes and stabs it towards mid wicket
preText: Starc to bowl his third on the trot

text: shot! Back of a length outside off, and the width allows Rahul to climb into it. Stands up tall and crashes it over cover for four!
length just outside off. Rahul waits for it and pushes it towards deep cover point. Might have been a cutter

wkt_text: DJ Hooda c Ramandeep Singh b Starc 8 (14m 10b 1x4 0x6) SR: 80.00
text: taken superbly at backward point by Ramandeep Singh! Length in the channel just outside off. Nips away a smidgen with the angle too. Hooda tries to drive on the up but cannot keep it down. Skews off the outer half of the bat and arrows towards backward point, where Ramandeep flies to his right and snares it. He was almost parallel to the ground when he took that, and KKR will be chuffed with that wicket!
dug in short outside off. Badoni gets up on his toes and fends it into the off side
preText: Badoni joins his skipper

text: length in the channel again. Badoni lets the ball come to him before meeting it right under his eyes
oh! Hard length just outside off. Nips back in and causes Rahul some trouble. He stabs at it and jams it off the inside edge into his back thigh. Rolls past the stumps for a single
preText: Harshit Rana to round off the powerplay

text: that is some way to get off the mark! Over-pitched outside off and Badoni unfurls a classical cover drive. Gets to the pitch, gets his hands through the ball and finds the gap between cover point and extra cover!
preText: Vismay: "Sticking with Starc worked for KKR"

shortText: Harshit Rana to Badoni, no run
text: back of a length on off. Badoni gets behind the line of the ball and plays it towards the bowler

shortText: Harshit Rana to Badoni, no run
text: shortish outside off. Badoni takes a step down the track before dabbing it towards backward point
off-cutter on a back of a length outside off. Cuts back into Badoni, and he drops it behind point for a single
picks the gap! Shortish outside off again. Rahul rides the bounce and opens the bat face very late to steer it between backward point and short third!
floated up full outside off. Badoni stretches forward and knocks it to long on
preText: Narine into the attack, straight after the powerplay

text: back of a length outside off. Rahul camps on the back foot and taps it towards backward point
shortish outside off. Badoni goes back and punches it to long off
on a length just outside off. Nips back in and cramps Rahul for room. Kept out via a combination of inside edge and thigh pad
length just outside off. Rahul sits deep in his crease and eases it out to long on
angled well down leg. Badoni gets bat to it but cannot get it past Chakravarthy at short fine leg

shortText: Harshit Rana to Badoni, no run
text: banged into the track outside off. Badoni has a swipe at it but only grabs a handful of fresh air. Called one bouncer for the over
preText: Rana to continue. Off-pace deliveries have gripped a little so far

text: off-pace on a full length on middle and leg. Badoni works it towards deep square leg
full and speared into middle and off. Rahul, perhaps expecting the short ball, is caught on the crease and prods it towards mid off
another cutter, on a length on middle and off. Badoni turns it towards deep square leg
slower ball on a back of a length outside off. Rahul plays it very late and dabs it past backward point for a couple of runs
preText: Four fielders on the fence on the leg side

text: slower ball on a full length on off. Rahul pushes it down to long on and settles for a single
back of a length outside off. Rahul stays back and chops it towards backward point
preText: Narine back for his second

text: short on off stump. Rahul waits and punches it towards deep mid wicket
fullish on off. Badoni comes half forward and pokes it towards deep square leg

massive appeal, not given! Fired in very full on off and Rahul, looking for the sweep, is completely beaten by how full it is. Narine was vociferous in his appeal, but it might have just hit Rahul outside off. Replays confirm the impact was probably a touch outside the line
full on middle and leg. Rahul gets down on one knee and sweeps it towards deep backward square leg
back of a length just outside off. Badoni eases it out to deep mid wicket. And that brings us to the first time-out of the day

boundary straight after the time-out! A bit of a freebie really. On a length well down leg. Badoni glances it past short fine leg. Russell comes around from deep backward square leg but his footie skills are not quite up to scratch
preText:
A change of bat for Rahul during the time-out. Chakravarthy to get us underway again

LSG have not quite rattled along as quickly as they would have wanted. This pitch, though, does look a touch slow, with more than a few balls holding in the surface. Rahul is still around, and LSG will hope he can shepherd them to a competitive total. More of the same, with the odd wicket in between, could be KKR's brief

text: back of a length on the stumps. Badoni tucks it off his pads towards deep backward square leg
length just outside off. Rahul presses half forward and knocks it down to long on
full on middle and off. Badoni looks for the flick and squirts it off the inside edge towards short fine leg
back of a length outside off. Rahul hangs back in his crease and jabs it past backward point
preText: Sukanta : "It's time for Varun to have an impact "

text: a polite lbw enquiry but nothing more than that! Given a bit of air on a length just outside off. Spins back into Badoni and hits the front pad as he plays down the wrong line. Okay, looks like there was bat involved too. Off the inside edge into the front pad
KLaasy! Banged in short outside off and Rahul climbs into it. Jumps up onto his toes and scythes it over the deep point fence!
preText: Russell to roll his arm over

wkt_text: KL Rahul c Ramandeep Singh b Russell 39 (52m 27b 3x4 2x6) SR: 144.44
text: holes out to deep mid wicket! Russell gets Rahul! Another shortish ball, although this is on the stumps. Rahul, trying to up the ante, opens up his stance and swipes at it. Gets a decent piece of it but the only problem is that he hits it straight down Ramandeep's throat. Much easier catch, compared to earlier, and LSG lose their skipper!
Stoinis starts off with a boundary! Russell goes short again but Stoinis is waiting for this. Stands up tall and belts it past deep mid wicket!
preText: Stoinis in at 5

text: Russell tests out the middle of the track for the fourth ball running. Seems to balloon over Stoinis' head but not called a wide
thumped! Half-tracker on off stump that is just begging to be hit. Stoinis rises with the bounce and hammers it between deep mid wicket and deep square leg!
the full ball comes now but it is on the pads, allowing Stoinis to work it towards deep mid wicket. Stoinis has to hurry for the second, and makes it in the end
preText: This has been a strange over so far. Everything has been into the track

text: very full just outside off. Badoni digs it out towards extra cover. A bit of hesitation between the batters and they decide against taking the single
watch out in the crowd! Incoming delivery that lands right in the slot on off. Badoni gets down on one knee, picks it up and dumps it over cow corner!
quicker and flatter. Low full toss on off and Badoni knocks it to long on

wkt_text: MP Stoinis c †Salt b Varun 10 (5m 5b 2x4 0x6) SR: 200.00
text: smart work by Salt, and Stoinis has to walk back! Tossed up a touch on a length outside off. Grips in the surface and rips back in. Stoinis does not account for that much turn and jams it off the inside edge into his pads. The ball pops up and Salt keeps his eyes on it all the way. Reacts quick enough and snaffles it sharply to his right, one-handed. KKR keep chipping away, and LSG, in trying to increase the tempo, have lost two in quick succession!
length on leg stump. Pooran lets the ball arrive before meeting it right under his eyes
preText: Pooran is the new batter in. LSG would love if he could get his teeth stuck into this contest

text: just short! Googly given a bit of air on a full length outside off. Pooran has a huge swing at it and slices it on the bounce to short third man. On another day, that would have carried comfortably to Narine
length on off. Badoni stretches forward and pushes it towards long on
slowed up on a length outside off. Pooran tries to hit it too hard and scuffs it into the off side
preText: Slip in place for Pooran

text: short and wide outside off. Pooran hops back and cuts it towards deep cover point
floated up full outside off. Badoni lunges forward and turns it towards deep mid wicket
slow on a back of a length on the stumps. Sticks in the surface too as Pooran defends
back of a length on leg stump. Pooran goes back and works it towards deep mid wicket
That. Is. Massive. Proper buffet ball. Knee-high full toss on leg stump, and Pooran rubs his eyes once before smoking that deep into the crowd over mid wicket!
preText:
Chakravarthy to continue

Pratheek Jain: "Badoni must be in a whole lot of confidence after his previous knock!" -- He needs to summon all of that confidence to haul LSG out of another hole today...

text: very full on middle and leg. Pooran clears his front leg and powers it down the ground to long off
preText: Chakravarthy feeling the pressure now

text: length delivery darted across the batter way outside off. Some more exercise for the umpire
short and wide outside off. Badoni stays back and cuts it towards deep point
length on middle and leg. Pooran reads it off the pitch and plays it towards extra cover
hung up outside off but this, again, is too wide. Pooran swishes and misses, and then sees the umpire call it a wide
preText: Vinod Rajpal: "Early prediction: This pair will take the score to 185!" -- These two are capable, but 185 seems a fair distance away at the moment

text: another away-going delivery on a length outside off. Pooran wafts at it and only connects with fresh air
length just outside off. Pooran pushes it towards extra cover and sets off for the single, only for Badoni to send him back

another lbw appeal, not given by umpire Akshay Totre! Length ball on off, that comes in with the angle. Badoni has a hack across the line and misses it completely. Gets struck on the back leg, and this looks awfully close. KKR think so too, and take it upstairs. If Badoni has not hit this, he could be in trouble. There is a slight spike when the ball is next to the bat, and Badoni survives. Excellent decision, given that scraped the toe-end!
fired in fuller on leg stump. Badoni comes forward and flicks it towards deep mid wicket
back of a length on off. Pooran stays back and punches it towards long off

wkt_text: A Badoni c Raghuvanshi b Narine 29 (44m 27b 2x4 1x6) SR: 107.40
text: goes straight up, and Badoni bites the dust! Slowed up just a shade on a length outside off. Seems to drift away late too. Badoni tries the expansive sweep but cannot get to the pitch of the ball. Skews it off the top edge and the ball swirls towards deep backward square leg. Raghuvanshi circles under it, tracks it all the way and holds on. LSG keep losing wickets!
length on middle and leg. Krunal comes forward and pokes it into the on side for a single
preText:
Krunal joins Pooran. Slip in place, Narine stays over the wicket

This pitch has not been as flat as everyone expected it to be. It is not very sluggish, certainly not like it was in Chennai when KKR were there, but a score in the 170-175 range could be competitive. LSG, if they can get there, will have a fighting chance

text: full on middle and off. Pooran gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it to long off
shortish outside off. Pooran reaches out for it and slaps it towards deep cover point
full on leg stump. Krunal gets onto the front foot and blocks
back of a length outside off. Comes off more sluggishly than Krunal expects and he jabs it to deep cover point
quicker and flatter on a length on leg stump. Pooran is rushed into the stroke and works it into the mid wicket region
short and wide outside off. Krunal goes back and cuts it towards deep cover point
short outside off again. Pooran hops back and punches it towards deep cover point
cutter on a back of a length outside off. Pooran throws his hands at it and scuffs it towards deep cover point
preText: Chakravarthy and Narine have finished their quota, so we might not see any more spin this innings. Pooran would not mind that, although the pacers, when they come back on, might bowl an assortment of slower balls. Here's Rana

text: back of a length just outside off. Krunal advances and chips it on the bounce to deep cover point
right out of the screws! Another off-pace ball but this sits up nicely outside off. Pooran opens up his front hip and whacks it over wide long on!

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: full and angled across the batter well outside off. Pooran swishes at it and misses. That was on-pace too and Pooran was probably not expecting it

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: sharp bumper just outside off. Zips off the surface and whizzes past Pooran's flailing blade as he looks to pull. Pooran feels he missed out there

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: short outside off. Pooran wafts at it away from his body and only connects with fresh air. The last four balls were six or nothing
slower bumper on leg stump. Barely gets to Krunal and he hacks it towards deep square leg
preText: Three overs left. Can LSG get up to 160? Arora to bowl the 18th. LSG will have to target him. In the meantime, Rinku Singh has come on as KKR's Impact Player, replacing Chakravarthy

text: Pooran power! Another slower bouncer on middle and leg. Pooran sizes it up early, gets on top of it and muscles it over deep mid wicket!
the change of angle makes no difference! Goes short again, this time on middle and off. That is right where Pooran wants it and he slugs it over deep backward square leg!
preText: Around the wicket now

text: very full on off stump. Pooran, sitting deep in his crease, swings at it and squirts it off the inside edge towards deep mid wicket for a brace
full outside off. Pooran drills it out towards deep cover point. The bat face opened upon impact and that rid him of the requisite power

low full toss slanted into leg stump. Krunal closes his bat face too early and the ball bobbles off the leading edge towards long off. Pooran wants the second to retain strike and makes it comfortably enough

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: off-pace on a length well outside off. Pooran does well to reach it but can only chalk it off the toe-end towards short third man
preText: Rana to bowl the penultimate over. 160 very much within reach after that last over. Rana to bowl from over the wicket

text: streaky but they all count! Slower ball on a length outside off. Pooran nearly swings himself off his feet, and that amount of effort takes the outside edge over short third man. First four for Pooran today!
bowls this a mile outside off. A wide yorker gone wrong and the umpire has no hesitation in calling this a wide

safe, and it rolls away for four! Pooran well and truly on the charge! Banged into the track on leg stump. Gets up high, perhaps to where Rana wants. Pooran, though, swipes at it so hard that he clears square leg, with the ball then trickling into the ropes, despite Starc's dive!
another wayward delivery outside off that just tests out Phil Salt's skills behind the stumps. More exercise for the umpire

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: full and wide outside off. Pooran gives it the lot but only swishes at thin air. Seemed inside the tramlines but Pooran has reviewed nonetheless. The ball is passing clearly inside the tramlines, and the original decision stands!

shortText: Harshit Rana to Pooran, no run
text: slower ball dug into the track outside off. Pooran tries to smash it into the Bay of Bengal but only swats away a few flies in the process
full and wide outside off. Pooran holds his shape this time and slices it down to deep backward point. Retains strike for the final over

wkt_text: N Pooran c †Salt b Starc 45 (37m 32b 2x4 4x6) SR: 140.62
text: edged and gone! No Pooran pyrotechnics in the final over! Length delivery hung up a long way outside off. In fact, it was beyond the tramlines. Pooran went after it and because it was so far, he could only feather it through to Salt. Subdued celebrations, but this is a huge wicket, and could possibly alter the score by 10-12 runs, at least!
preText: Six balls left in this innings. Can Pooran take LSG to 170? Starc will bowl the final over. Pooran might appreciate the left-arm angle coming into him

text: Arshad begins with a boundary! Banged in short outside off and Arshad has the license to swing for the hills. Gets it nowhere near the middle but the ball flies off the top edge over the keeper!
preText: Arshad Khan walks in to bat. He has come in as LSG's Impact Player, replacing Quinton de Kock

shortText: Starc to Arshad Khan, no run
text: oh! Right in the slot just outside off. Arshad swings his blade like an axe but does not make any contact

excellent yorker just outside off. Tails back in late, and seems to go past Arshad's swing. Krunal is alert enough and sneaks in a bye. Salt wanted to go upstairs, not sure why. Looks like the on-field umpire has brought his colleague into play. The ball has bounced after going past the bat, so everything else is immaterial
back of a length on off. Shapes away a little and squares up Salt as he prods it off the back foot towards backward point
preText: 5:31pm We are back. The sun is setting in Kolkata, but has it set on LSG, as far as this game is concerned? 161 to defend, and KKR will come hard at them in the powerplay. Rahul with some last-minute instructions as Narine and Salt wander out to the middle. Joseph, making his IPL debut, will take the new ball for LSG. He can bowl at a brisk pace. Over the wicket to Salt, slip in place - here we go!

text: hard length, angling into leg stump. Salt is rushed on the pull and cannot lay bat on it. Loops up off the thigh pad towards short fine leg. That was bowled at 140.7kph
Narine is up and running! Too much width and this is short enough too. Narine stands up tall and cracks it through cover point for four!

hard length just outside off. Narine continues swinging because, well, that is what he does. Skews this off the outside edge and it loops over short third. Hooda chases after it, puts in the dive and saves two
preText: Around the wicket now

text: beauty! 146.5kph heat-seeking missile that pitches just outside off and jags back sharply. Cuts Narine in half and Rahul can only get fingertips to it. A bye to KKR
Joseph gets pumped down the ground! 146.4kph but this is right into the slot outside off. Salt swings through the line and bangs it over mid off. And the first over finally comes to an end!
postText: Rahul puts an arm around Joseph and that is a nice touch, especially after a tough initiation to the IPL

text: full and speared down leg. Salt steps across to the off side and then watches it go through to Rahul. And it is another No ball. The wheels are coming off already for Shamar Joseph!

oh dear, this is going from bad to worse! Sprays this well down leg. Salt swings and misses. Rahul cannot get close to it either. Five extras added to KKR's total, and they still have a free hit to tuck into!
full and wide, possibly a slower ball that has gone wrong. Beyond the tramlines too and the free hit continues

dropped, oh dear! 150.7kph delivery, bowled on a hard length and slanting into leg stump. Salt gets inside the line and helps it towards short fine leg. Thakur dives to his right but puts it down. That is not all because...Joseph has overstepped!
preText: Back to over the wicket

shortText: Mohsin Khan to Narine, no run
text: back of a length just outside off. Kisses the surface and zips through, sneaking past the outside edge of Narine's dab
preText: Mohsin to share the new ball

shortText: Mohsin Khan to Narine, no run
text: hard length on middle and leg. Hurries onto Narine quicker than he anticipates and he cloths it to mid on

wkt_text: SP Narine c Stoinis b Mohsin Khan 6 (10m 6b 1x4 0x6) SR: 100.00
text: Narine will not dominate the powerplay tonight! Mohsin sticks to that hard length just outside off, and takes the pace off this time. Narine was always going to go after it, but the lack of pace means that he miscues it. Gets plenty of height, but not enough distance. Stoinis, stood at cover point and on the edge of the ring, does the rest!

shortText: Mohsin Khan to Raghuvanshi, no run
text: back of a length in the channel. Decks away with the angle and that draws Raghuvanshi into a poke away from his body. Beaten all ends up
preText: Raghuvanshi in at 3

shortText: Mohsin Khan to Raghuvanshi, no run
text: shortish outside off. Raghuvanshi stands up on his toes and punches it crisply towards backward point, where Bishnoi sprawls to his right and prevents a certain boundary
preText: Two slips in place

text: goes all the way! Length ball on the pads and it gets the treatment it deserves. Raghuvanshi snaps his wrists into the stroke and lifts it over the long leg fence!
Salt welcomes Krunal with a boundary! Darted into the slot outside off. Salt plants his front foot and thumps it over the bowler's head!
preText: Spin into the attack early. Krunal to bowl the third. LSG have the luxury of doing this because Narine is no longer at the crease. Around the wicket to Salt

text: four more! In the slot again, this time on the pads. Salt bends his back knee and sweeps it well over backward square leg. One bounce and into the fence!
crrunnnchhheeededdd! Marginally short outside off, and that is right up Salt's alley. Stands tall and crunches it to mid off's left!
fuller on middle and off. Salt comes forward and drives it down to long off
preText: Mid off goes back

text: angled in on a length on leg stump. Raghuvanshi plays all over it and gets pinged on the front pad. Was probably going down leg, though
safe! On a length outside off. Holds in the surface and spins away. Raghuvanshi pokes at it and almost pops it to Bishnoi at backward point. Enough to his right to survive

wkt_text: A Raghuvanshi c †Rahul b Mohsin Khan 7 (7m 6b 0x4 1x6) SR: 116.66
text: Mohsin has two, and LSG are fighting back! Back of a length delivery slanted across the batter outside off. Goes on with the angle and forces Raghuvanshi to play at it. He does so without much conviction and nicks it through to Rahul. The easiest of catches for the LSG skipper, and Mohsin is pumped!

shortText: Mohsin Khan to SS Iyer, 1 run
text: back of a length just outside off. Shreyas plays with the angle and runs it down to third man
preText: Skipper Shreyas walks in

text: dug in short on leg stump. Gets a little big on Salt and he splices his pull towards deep square leg

shortText: Mohsin Khan to SS Iyer, no run
text: back of a length outside off again. Shreyas waits for it and defends

shortText: Mohsin Khan to SS Iyer, no run
text: jaffa! Length on middle and leg. Threatens to shape in but nips away off the surface. Shreyas is opened up like a deck chair and beaten comprehensively

shortText: Mohsin Khan to SS Iyer, no run
text: this is slower but on a similar length on off. Shreyas, having walked across his stumps, fends it into the off side. Looks like it was the off-cutter
hard length on middle and leg. Seems to just hold in the surface and hits Salt high on the bat as he defends. Popped up into the air but it was well to Joseph's right
preText: Joseph is back

text: ripper! Back of a length delivery in the channel that curves away late. Salt nibbles at it and is squared up completely. Play and a miss!
back of a length outside off. Salt gets up on his toes and jabs it towards deep cover point
preText: Salt does not like defending usually. Joseph has pace to burn. Something might just give here...

text: Shreyas gets his first boundary! Drifts onto the pads and pays the price. Plenty of pace on this too and Shreyas can just glance it fine for four!

shortText: Joseph to SS Iyer, no run
text: back of a length just outside off. Shreyas hangs back and prods it into the off side

shortText: Joseph to SS Iyer, no run
text: back of a length on off. Shreyas gets behind the line and presents the full face of the bata
Salt continues on his merry way! Slow and short outside off. Salt picks the change of pace, holds his stroke long enough and glides it past backward point!
preText: Thakur to bowl the last over of the powerplay, like he did against the Titans when he dismissed Gill

text: back to back boundaries for Salt again! This is also short, perhaps a little closer to off stump. Salt generates room by jumping up onto his toes and carves it over cover point!
into the blockhole on middle and leg. Salt digs it out into the mid on region and picks up a single

shortText: Yash Thakur to SS Iyer, no run
text: another play and miss! KKR have made 58 so far but there have been quite a few of these too. On a back of a length outside off. A bit of nibble away and it breezes past Shreyas' prod

shortText: Yash Thakur to SS Iyer, no run
text: just short! Hard length just outside off. Shreyas tries to stand tall and go over mid off. The ball sticks a little, though, and Shreyas clinks it on the bounce to mid off

shortText: Yash Thakur to SS Iyer, no run
text: back of a length just outside off. Shreyas stays back and drops it into the off side with soft hands
shortish just outside off. Salt has a swipe across the line but is beaten for pace, and by the inward movement. Not far away from the stumps either
preText: KKR will be fairly happy with their powerplay, despite losing two wickets. The required run-rate is under 7.5 runs per over now, and if Salt sticks around for a few more overs, KKR might do this at a canter. Joseph to bowl his third

text: hard length on leg stump. Skids onto Salt and he, after hopping onto his toes, tugs it towards deep square leg

shortText: Joseph to SS Iyer, no run
text: huge appeal, and given! Shreyas reviews it straightaway! Hard length again, slanting into leg stump and cramping Shreyas for room. He tries to help it fine and seems to miss it, with the ball brushing the thigh pad on its way to the keeper. The quickness of the review suggests exactly that, and the replays confirm it too. Clear spike off the thigh pad, and Shreyas survives!
safe! Shreyas is not looking comfortable when the ball is at his body. This gets up close to his grille and he top-edges it on the bounce to fine leg

parried over the bar! Shortish on middle and leg. Salt stands tall and whips it away towards deep square leg. Arshad settles himself on the fence but palms it over the bar. Not a difficult chance in front of his face, and LSG will be gutted about that!
yorker speared into leg stump. Salt does not get bat on it and the ball trickles off the pads towards fine leg. Thakur dives to his left and saves two
edged and four! Back of a length on leg stump. Nips back into Salt and zips off the surface too. Salt is beaten for pace but luckily for him, the inside edge hurtles away past short fine leg!

shortText: Arshad Khan to SS Iyer, 2 wides
text: sprayed a mile down leg, and Rahul does well to get something behind it. Just the two extras for KKR

postText:
7:37pm And, that is a wrap from this game. But don't go anywhere, the El Clasico is up and running, with CSK batting first. Hop over to that match. Until next time, from me (Shashwat), Thilak, Ranjith and Raghav, this is goodbye. Take care, folks!

Phil Salt, Player of the Match: I said to Swanny (Graeme Swann) before the game that I was melting and I had only been out there for two minutes. Kept going, Shreyas was good in the middle and kept me on task. Good to get another win at home. Before the lights came on, I felt it was a little slower. When they came on, there was a bit more moisture to allow the ball to slide on, so it got a bit better for our innings. In India, this (Eden Gardens pitch) is probably the most similar to home. Ball bounces a bit more and you can aim squarer. Really like the wicket here. I have loved it. we have some great overseas players, some great coaches. Good to have Shreyas back. GG (Gautam Gambhir) is back in the fold as well, and I am really enjoying it.

Interview: Phil Salt spoke to ESPNcricinfo before this game about his attacking ability and life as a T20 globetrotter

Shreyas Iyer, Kolkata Knight Riders captain: (On if he is happy with the performance) Yeah, certainly. The way we played, it was a comprehensive victory. We bowled well under pressure and then finishing off the game, it was the icing on the cake. It was important to bowl as many slower balls as possible. With the heat coming in, the wicket was a little dry and we wanted to minimise the half-volleys and we wanted the batters to use their power and clear the ropes. That is what we were focussing on and I feel we executed phenomenally well. When we got wickets in between, that gave us an advantage. The bowlers were ready whenever I passed on the ball to them. The character and attitude they showed, it was exceptional. (On playing five home games in a row) It is absolutely an advantage but I will keep reiterating that this is a funny tournament and you have to stay in the present. You cannot take the situation lightly. You have to be on top of the game and ensure you do not leave it to someone else. That is what we have been doing sensationally well, and that is what we have to keep doing to build momentum and make sure we are all on the same mindset.

KL Rahul, Lucknow Super Giants captain: A tough day. A proper hammering. Every team in the IPL goes through a game like that. Not going to sit too much and think about it. Will go back, work out where we went wrong and bounce back better. (On if pitch got better under lights) I think it was the other way round. The ball started nipping around a lot more after the lights came on. Can't say we played bad shots but the shots we played, we did not execute well. Kept losing wickets in bunches and we left about 30 runs out there. If we kept wickets in our hand, and had one of our top three-four bat through, we could have got a lot more runs. That is where I think we lost the game. With the ball, it was nipping around. We got a few wickets but leaked too many boundaries. (On Joseph) That was a positive, he was bowling very quick. First game of the IPL, you can get excited, and Shamar was very excited and just wanted to bowl fast, sprayed the ball around a bit but that can happen with anyone. The positive was he was bowling very quick and he got the ball to nip around. He hit some good areas but obviously he has to work on his consistency and the choice of balls he bowls. (On back to back defeats) Not panicking but you can't put your feet up and hope results go your way. We have to figure out where you are going wrong. We will have a few difficult conversations. The last couple of games, we have not been able to get more than 160 and that is something to think about, and see how we can get to the 180-200 run mark.

Sunil Narine: (On his plans) Trying to keep it as tight as possible, some games it happens, some games, it doesn't. Once you are in control of the game, it is easier to bowl as a spinner. We have been doing good. two from two, hopefully we can continue. All the guys are keen and everyone is fully fit and enjoying it. The key thing is enjoying it because then you can go out there and have fun. The figures didn't show it, he (Shamar Joseph) was a bit unlucky. He gave energy in every ball. It was his first game, and it is a learning process. I am sure he will come back strong. (On Salt) Salty looked brilliant today and he is someone who has looked good every game. once someone from the top five bats the majority of the overs, it is good for our batting line-up. (On if he wants to play the T20 World Cup) I will be watching from home, Badree.

7pm Comprehensive with a capital P. That is what this win was. KKR called the shots during the chase. Salt blazed away in the powerplay, like only he can, and then kept adding flavour whenever the innings threatened to turn stale (which was not very often, mind you). At the other end, Shreyas did struggle for his usual rhythm but he stayed there till the end, ensuring there were no hiccups.

As for LSG, well, they were just not at the races. The wicket did get a little better under lights but LSG's bowling plans left plenty to be desired. Joseph did not have an ideal IPL debut, with Thakur and Arshad also conceding runs. Mohsin was the only bright spark, picking up 2-29 in his four overs.

LSG, with this defeat, have now lost two in a row and will need to recover swiftly. KKR, on the other hand, have begun this five-game home stretch with a win, and would want to build on this from here.

It's toss time at Wankhede!

Hardik wins the toss, Mumbai Indians opt to bowl. He cites the dew factor as the major reason for his decision. Expects this surface to play better than the one on which the RCB game was played. Mumbai are unchanged.

Ruturaj Gaikwad says CSK would've bowled first too. One change. Matheesha Pathirana comes in for Mahesh Theekshana.

6.55pm There has been plenty of chatter around Ishan Kishan, ever since he decided to opt out of the Test series in South Africa in December. All along, there has been stoic silence from the man himself. But the other night, after his blitzkrieg against RCB, he spoke for the first time about his long absence and his time away.

Nagraj Gollapudi from the Wankhede: "MI seamers seem unchanged: Bumrah, Coetzee, Shepherd and Madhwal have marked run-ups. Fizz and Deshpande for CSK so far. i suspect Moeen will play alongside Mitchell."

Naga is also closely tracking Hardik, who is undergoing some drills under the physio's supervision. Hardik is now bowling off a short run-up though he has not marked his run-up yet.

6.34pm This may be an away game for CSK alright, but the likes of Shivam Dube, Shardul Thakur, Ajinkya Rahane, Tushar Deshpande will all feel at home. But there's little doubt the cheer will possibly be the biggest for another Mumbaikar. They call him Surya dada, who lit the scene with a magical knock against RCB the other night.

6.25pm It's El Classico time! Welcome to a brand new chapter of this fascinating rivalry between the two most-storied IPL teams with two brand new captains looking to lay the foundation of a new era.

The change of guard at the top for Mumbai Indians has been a touch controversial, whereas it's been a lot more organic for Chennai Super Kings. But now we're almost halfway into the competition and the ringing boos are slowly, but surely beginning to be replaced with applause as Mumbai have begun a climb up the ladder.

Those in and around the Wankhede tell me they're seeing a sea of yellow amid a smattering of blue. As always, CSK continue to have a massive following everywhere. Who knows, maybe this is MS Dhoni's last game at the Wankhede, where he hit that iconic six to bring India World Cup glory.

Sit back, relax and enjoy this fun ride. I'm Shashank Kishore. With me on this journey is Deivarayan Muthu. The scoring duties are manned by P Ranjith, Venkat Raghav and Chandan Duroah. We hope to keep you hooked to the action. Fire away with your comments, inputs, observations and anything else you may want to tell us. We're all ears. Cheers!

9.23pm What a finish! CSK didn't look like getting 200, but for those big hits in the final over from MS Dhoni that has tipped them over what you'd think is "par plus", in the words of the great man. Props to Shivam Dube too for playing a blinder, and giving the innings that momentum in the middle overs alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad.

CSK have made 57 off the last five overs. Amidst the carnage, Bumrah once again finishes with an exceptional economy of 6.75 across his four overs. Nabi was excellent in the three overs but couldn't bowl out because he was held back with Dube around. Wonder how much MI will be concerned around Hardik's bowling form.

11.25pm That is that. CSK halt MI's winning streak at home and seal their first win away from home this IPL. They have defended 206 at the Wankhede, thanks to excellent defensive bowling. Pathirana led the way with 4 for 28 in his four overs. He bows to Bravo, his bowling coach. Bravo would've been proud of his effort from his bowlers. Do stick with us for the post-match presentation.

Gaikwad, CSK captain: Our young wicketkeeper scoring three sixes down the order helped a lot and I think that was the difference. To start off, on this kind of ground, you need 10-15 extra runs. We were looking at 215-220, but Bumrah bowled well. Bowling-wise, we were spot on with our execution. Even in powerplay, I would have taken six overs for 60. These kinds of venues demand both skills: batting and bowling. Our Malinga bowled exceptionally well and nailed those yorkers. Not to forget - even Tushar and Shardul bowled well. We encourage everyone to be in a good headspace. Nothing, Jinks was carrying a bit of a niggle. Thought it was better for him to open and get away quick runs. I'm fine batting anywhere.

Hardik, MI captain: Definitely, gettable. But they bowled pretty well and Pathirana was the difference. They were smart with their plans and used the longer boundary well. They got the hang of it and they have a man behind the stumps telling them what's working. The ball was slightly gripping and they got ahead of the game. Until Pathirana came, we were on course for the total. It was just about what was best at that point (on whether they could have used a spinner to Dube?). To seamers it was more difficult to hit on this wicket. We are now on the road for the next four games. If we are smart, we can get the goal we want.

Pathirana, Player of the Match: When we bowled in powerplay, I was nervous. I then came to do my regular things. I don't think about results and I just think about execution. First of all, I was having a niggle before two weeks and all support staff and players helped me. That's the main thing to have my form.

Thakur: Much-needed  win. Playing against opponents like MI, especially at the Wankhede is not easy. Rohit, Ruturaj and Shivam the way they batted...but at the end of the day, we held our nerve better. We spoke about keeping it simple, meaning we need to have fielders where we bowl. This is a repeated pitch and MI played on it on April 11. We felt we needed to bowl slower ones into the pitch. Pathirana was magical and the way he bowled the yorkers was amazing to see. Not much dew today. When Rohit was going strong, we felt the game was sliding away a little but I wanted to challenge Rohit to hit me on the bigger side. If he can't, it might be the turning point.

Sudhir: "In hindsight, those hits from Dhoni towards the very end (20) have made the difference. Dhoni is in top form this year making an impact just when it's needed. I bet he is going to be back for one more season."

Sampath Bandarupalli, our stats wiz: This is the first time Rohit Sharma remained unbeaten in an unsuccessful run-chase in the IPL. His team won on all 18 previous instances where he remained unbeaten in a run-chase.

7.27pm Out come the players, with Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma leading the line for SRH. Looks like Lockie Ferguson will take the first ball ... no, it'll be the spin of Will Jacks. Right into the action from the outset.

7.15pm Right, what do we have in store tonight? RCB desperately need to get their campaign heading in the right direction, and at least by bowling first, they spare themselves the angst of working out what is a competitive total. That said, SRH haven't been guilty of second-guessing their approach too often this year. And on a small ground like the Chinnaswammy, who knows what heights they could attain...

RCB have the worst economy rate and fewest wickets in powerplays this IPL while Sunrisers are the joint second-quickest batting team in powerplays this season. That could decide what's in store early on.

Karthik: "Am I reading it right? RCB are bowling first but they named only 4 bowlers and left Siraj out yet named as impact sub. Sometimes this impact rules confuses me." Have to admit, it permanently confuses me!

Royal Challengers Bengaluru XI: F. du Plessis(c), V. Kohli, W. Jacks, R. Patidar, S. Chauhan, D. Karthik(w), M. Lomror, R. Topley, L. Ferguson, V. Vyshak, Y. Dayal. Impact options: S Prabhudessai, A Rawat, Swapnil Singh, M Siraj, Karn Sharma

Sunrisers Hyderabad XI: T Head, A Sharma, A Markram, H Klaasen(wk), A Samad, N Reddy, S Ahmed, P Cummins(c), B Kumar, J Unadkat, T Natarajan. Impact options: U Malik, Anmolpreet Singh, M Markande, G Phillips, R Tripathi

Toss: RCB win the toss and opt to bowl.

du Plessis: [The pitch has been] pretty much the same. Playing a little bit two-paced and slower than expected. That's the nature of the game and we need to play what's in front. We haven't played our best cricket, we're not delivering to our skill and some of the guys aren't playing their best. Maxwell is sitting out and so is Siraj. Ferguson is coming in.

Looks like Chauhan has come into the starting XI as the second change.

Cummins: We're going with the same team. 240 feels like par at Chinnaswamy.

Toss coming up in a few minutes and we will have Ian Bishop on our live show. Don't go anywhere!

6.50pm This ground is known as a batters' paradise but somehow this season hasn't quite provided the big scores. Three games so far and the highest score has been KKR's 186. It seems like the Chinnaswamy tracks have been turning and gripping a bit more than usual. RCB can't even boast of a big-name spinner in their ranks to try and stop the SRH fireworks before Klaasen, learning from how Mumbai Indians used Nabi's offspin last night before Shivam Dube came out to bat. Can the RCB line-up step up tonight? They'll be hoping Siraj turns his form around, at least.

Prateek: "Topley and Ferguson both is exactly what RCB needs. Their batting line up looks good enough, but bowlers need to step up. Time for Siraj to find what works for him in T20s as he is a contender for WC squad as well."

Rahim Chagani: "RCB's issue is their middle/lower order, particularly when the top order fails. They can't always rely on DK to bail them out. In comparison, SRH have Klaasen, Samad, Shabhaz and Cummins lower down their order. They can all clear the fence from the first ball. It's relentless. "

Hemant Brar has waded through the Monday traffic and made it to the ground. He says: "Ferguson has marked his run-up and Topley too. I am not able to spot Maxwell, maybe they are going in with Faf, Jacks, Lockie and Topley as their four overseas." Update: Maxwell is also there.

Cricfan: "If indeed they are going with both Topley and Lockie, then it is a good move. Their main problem is bowling. I hope Siraj also gets a break for a few games, and he can come back refreshed. One more thing RCB is losing out on, is the lack of left-right combinations. That is easily costing around 15-20 runs in my opinion. It will be good if the playing XII is -- Faf, Kohli, Jacks, Saurav, Patidar, Lomror, DK, Himanshu, Vyshak, Yash, Topley, Lockie. Impact players swap will be Patidar and Yash. "

What all can we expect in this game? Here's Abhimanyu's preview.

The home team languishing at the bottom against the visitors placed fourth right now. A team with four losses in a row to take on a team with back-to-back wins in two games. Greetings to one and all, this is match 30 and we'll bring you the toss in 30.

7.29pm Salt on strike. A slip and short third in place, let's get this show rolling...

7.27pm The lights are on in full tilt, some seats are still missing some bums but the purple and yellow flags are fluttering in full flourish. Michael Clarke has rung the ball at Eden Gardens and out walk the umpires. Phil Salt runs out soon after and Narine is walking out like he's just woken up. What a pair this has been at the top for KKR this season. How will Narine do against Boult's swing? But hang on, Royals are opening with spin. No, they're not. Samson is standing up just to set the field. Boult has the ball and is setting the field.

"Could some update where is Nitish Rana this season, captained KKR last season" Looks like he's still injured, Gursewak

7.25pm Riyan Parag is having a stellar IPL this time around. And this time he's among the many uncapped Indian players making headlines one after another. Deivarayan Muthu has put a list together for your eyes.

Royals XI: 1 Jaiswal, 2 Powell, 3 Samson (capt), 4 Parag, 5 Hetmyer, 6 Jurel, 7 Ashwin, 8 Boult, 9 Avesh, 10 Kuldeep, Chahal
Impact options: Buttler, Kohler-Cadmore, Dubey, Saini, Burger

So no place for Maharaj after taking 2 for 23 in the last game. And interesting that Royals have five bowling options despite bowling first. Parag is the only other option if they need a sixth bowler.

lakssman: "@Vishal - at least Royals have 5 specialist bowlers.. yesterday RCB just had 4 specialist bowlers when they chose to bowl first."

KKR XI: 1 Salt, 2 Narine, 3 Shreyas (capt), 4 Venkatesh, 5 Raghuvanshi, 6 Rinku, 7 Russell, 8 Ramandeep, 9 Starc, 10 Varun, 11 Harshit
Impact options: Suyash, Anukul, Manish, Vaibhav, Gurbaz

Shrikant : "The batting line up of KKR cannot be contained, the only option is to set up aggressive fielding to take wickets relentlessly "

The captains are out there, here goes the coin:

Toss: Royals have won the toss and will bowl first

Samson: It might be better to bat here, but it's ok, we'll bowl first. To be back at Eden is special, it has a special vibe. Jos and Ash bhai are available for this game.

Shreyas: Yea we wanted to bowl first because of the way it was seaming the other day. We are going with the same team.

Some Yuzi love before the toss..

6.53pm Time for the pitch report: the square boundaries are uneven tonight: 59 metres on one and 71 on the other. It will be interesting to see how the two bouncers an over and the spinners use the longer boundaries. Toss coming up soon...

Kumar: "I agree with Tom Moody. Impact sub rule should be scrapped. Batting dominating all the time is not cricket."

Kalyan: "I get that some people don't like "impact player" rule. But every other popular team sport has multiple substitutes that replace the on field players(not just fielding like in cricket). Impact player rule can also be used to strengthen the bowling too."

Hemant Noval: "@Kalyan : Agreed, cricket needs substitute players, but what is hurting India ias that it is still not allowed at international level, and hence no all rounders are being groomed. You hardly see Parag, Abhishek, Dube bowling due to this."

6.45pm A couple of injury updates: Ashwin and Buttler, two key RR players, missed the last game with niggles. Both are at the ground today; Buttler has his left knee and hamstring taped, and is gingerly warming up with the teams. And Ashwin is bowling on the side nets. We should know soon if they're fit for today.

Mahesh: "RR should continue with Maharaj in place of Ashwin. It does add variety to their bowling attack."

6.40pm Here's a fun fact: Sunil Narine hasn't conceded a single boundary at Eden Gardens yet this IPL in two games. For much such gems and what's in store for today's game, catch up with Karthik Krishnaswamy's preview here.

6.30pm Are you also hungover from the one-of-a-kind run-fest last night? And if you didn't enjoy the domination of the bat much, tonight's game is just for you. This top-of-the-table clash is a proper bat vs ball contest because Royals are the most economical bowling attack of this IPL and KKR the second-most destructive. The action moves from Bengaluru to Kolkata, which has hosted just two games so far: first KKR just defended 208 and then chased down 162 opposite LSG pretty convincingly. Hello and welcome to the 31st match of this edition, I'm Vishal Dikshit and will be joined by Shashank when the chase starts.

7.15pm Will Gill be opening alongside Rohit Sharma for India at the T20 World Cup? Or will Yashasvi Jaiswal pip him for that spot? Watch our Runorder crew discuss that, and more, as the World Cup begins barely six days after the IPL ends.

Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 Wriddhiman Saha (wk), 3 Sai Sudharsan, 4 David Miller, 5 Abhinav Manohar, 6 Rahul Tewatia, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Mohit Sharma, 9 Noor Ahmad, 10 Spencer Johnson, 11 Sandeep Warrier. Impact Subs: Sharath, Suthar, Shahrukh, Sai Kishore and Nalkande
