7:27pm Sourav Ganguly rings the bell at the Eden Gardens and that is the cue for play to start. Shaw and Fraser-McGurk to open the batting for the Capitals and both of them usually throw caution to the wind. Starc will take the new ball for KKR. Shaw on strike - here we go!

Any Mohun Bagan and KKR fans in the house? Mumbai City and FC Goa are going at it to see who'll face Bagan in the Indian Super League final, you can follow that crunch ISL semifinal live, right here.

7:15pm The Capitals have strengthened their top order with the inclusion of Shaw. Starc's return should also bolster KKR's bowling attack, and his battle against Fraser-McGurk will be particularly intriguing to watch.

Jayant Isswani: "Early prediction: Delhi Capitals are going to capitulate to the bowlers of KKR and expecting an early finish tonight." -- Well, that is quite an early prediction, and a bold one too, given how DC have been batting lately...

Delhi Capitals XI: Prithvi Shaw, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Abishek Porel, Shai Hope, Rishabh Pant (c & wk), Tristan Stubbs, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Lizaad Williams, Khaleel Ahmed, Rasikh Dar

DC bench: Mukesh Kumar, Sumit Kumar, Pravin Dubey, Kumar Kushagra, Ricky Bhui

Kolkata Knight Riders XI: Phil Salt (wk), Sunil Narine, Venkatesh Iyer, Shreyas Iyer (c), Rinku Singh, Andre Russell, Ramandeep Singh, Mitchell Starc, Vaibhav Arora, Varun Chakravarthy, Harshit Rana

KKR bench: Suyash Sharma, Anukul Roy, Manish Pandey, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Rahmanullah Gurbaz

7pm It's toss time. Pant and Shreyas, teammates once upon a time, are out in the middle. Shreyas gives the coin a twirl. Pant calls heads, and heads it is. Delhi Capitals will bat first. Pant says the way the team is going, they want to put up runs on the board. He adds the wicket looks on the slower side and that it might slow up further in the second innings. Shaw returns in place of Kushagra, with Rasikh also part of the starting eleven.

Shreyas says he would have bowled first anyway, so both sides happy with the outcome. He adds that they have tried to keep things simple in the break, reckoning that it would otherwise be very easy to go away from what they have doing after a tough loss. Two changes for KKR - Starc comes in, as does Arora.

Poonit: "10 days ago or so, Delhi were 9th . Now tonight if they win, they go 2nd!

6:55pm In five matches this season at Eden Gardens, the team batting first has won thrice. The most recent game, though, saw the Punjab Kings mow down 262 rather comfortably. What will the captain winning the toss want to do? Toss in 5.

6:53pm Rajan Raj says that Starc has now marked his run-up. The left-armer, if that is any indication, looks set to return to the eleven tonight, possibly in place of Dushmantha Chameera.

Pitch Report: This is the same surface that was used for the KKR-RR game. Unequal square boundaries today as well at the Eden Gardens. 59m to one side, 71m to the other, with a 75m hit down the ground. The shortest and longest pocket are 55m and 77m, respectively. Simon Katich says the pitch is rock-hard and that the ball will come onto the bat nicely. Not a lot of dew expected, and he adds that the bowlers will have their work cut out tonight.

Rajan Raj, our man at the ground, says that Vaibhav Arora and Ramandeep Singh have marked their run-ups. Arora was quite influential the last time these sides met. Starc, however, is not practicing at the moment and arrived a little later than the others too.

Yoel: "Predicting birthday boy Andre Russell to have a blast today.... "

6:40pm KKR's win in Vishakhapatnam snapped a three-game losing streak against the Capitals. Throughout the IPL, though, KKR have had the better of the exchanges, winning 17 as compared to the Delhi-based franchise's 15.

6:30pm 438. That is how many runs were scored the last time these sides met. The Kolkata Knight Riders got 272 of those and have since scored 223, 222 and 261 when batting first at the Eden Gardens. The problem, though, is that they have only won one of these home games, and that too was secured by a one-run margin.

The Delhi Capitals, on the other hand, have found a batting gear they were lacking at the start. Jake Fraser-McGurk's inclusion has made their fans drool over what is indeed possible and the Capitals have reeled off two consecutive 200-plus scores when batting first.

This game, thus, already has a high-scoring vibe to it. What is different from last time, though, is that the Capitals are the team now in red-hot form, close on KKR's heels and capable of leapfrogging them in the points table, with KKR now becoming the side in need of a turnaround.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of Match 47 of IPL 2024. The Capitals, hoping to get one over the franchise that chastened them earlier in the season; the Knight Riders, longing to prove that these recent failed defences were an aberration rather than the start of a worrying trend. Grab your choice of food and drink, put your feet up, and savour what promises to be another humdinger!

11:25pm Right, that will be all from us for tonight. A bit of an early finish, given this was done well before the last over. We will be back at it tomorrow as the Lucknow Super Giants take on the Mumbai Indians. Until then, this is goodbye from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo. Goodbye and take care!

Varun Chakravarthy, Player of the Match: It (the pitch) was holding a bit and you could see as the game progressed, it was turning more. (On the Rishabh Pant wicket and his match-up) The first ball, when the catch was dropped, I think that was a better ball. The ball that got him out, might have gone for six on any other ground. Cricket has become a game of fine margins. The Stubbs one (was my favourite). (On what happens in conversations between him and Narine) Silence (laughs). Mostly when something does not go well for me, he is always there. After conceding so many runs in the last game, it was a tough pill. Everyone, including Abhishek Nayar and Shahrukh Khan spoke to me and that was nice. (On him asking to spare a thought for the cheerleaders) Unfortunately that has become the trend and maybe they should dance only for the sixes and not for fours (laughs).

Shreyas Iyer, Kolkata Knight Riders captain: (On if he thought the pitch will play this way) Not at all, considering the last few matches. After the powerplay, the ball started spinning a bit, was helping the spinners and was tacky. Happy that we bowled first, we got an idea on how it was playing. (On having a chat with the openers beforehand) Sunny, not at all. Phil, he coms into the team meetings and he is completely engrossed into the game. Pure bliss to see the way he is performing. He (Narine) does not (attend team meetings), and I would recommend him to not come as well (smiles). He (Chakravarthy) was not at his best in the last few games. But today, coming in and delivering under pressure, that is what we demand. The way he turned up today was simply brilliant. We have been thinking about it (qualification) from match one, that has been our mindset. Just focussing on our work ethics and our performance.

Rishabh Pant, Delhi Capitals captain: (On his decision at the toss) I think that (batting first) was a good option but as a batting unit, we did not bat well enough. 150 was definitely below par. That is part and parcel of cricket. We have a long break ahead, where we can learn from our mistakes. Sometimes, it is just not your day. The way we were going, it was pretty nice. You cannot get away every time in T20 cricket. We were 40-50 runs short. (On the ideal target) I think anything between 180-210 would have been a good target. There was a lot of help for the bowlers but as a batting unit, we did not give them enough.

Phil Salt: Good to be contributing. We have had a good run of home games, nice to have that continuity of conditions. Had to bounce back from a tough last game. Pleased to see the bowlers put in that sort of performance, really pleased for them. (On his attacking approach) It is high-risk but it is also about putting the odds in your favour and not taking the risks you don't want to. You just have to keep backing yourself and keep taking the right options. Very helpful to keep on it first and see what it is doing. So, when you come out, you have a fairly good idea of how the surface is playing. (On his conversations with Narine) Off field, we have a laugh. On the field, not a lot. We usually do the talking a day before. He (Narine) does not talk much but he is a deep thinker of the game. (On them taking turns to attack) That is also part of the communication. If one of us gets going, you feed the strike to the other person. Good that we are on the same page like that.

11pm A fairly one-sided contest in the end. It did feel that way at the innings break, and once Salt tore into the DC bowlers inside the powerplay, it quickly became clear that there would be no twists. In fact, Salt's onslaught was so severe that Narine barely had to hit a shot in anger throughout the powerplay, even as KKR ransacked 79 in the first six overs.

The Iyers, Shreyas and Venkatesh, then drove home that advantage, ensuring there were no further hiccups. The only downside to the run-chase was Rinku not making the most of his opportunity at No.3 but apart from that, everything else went to plan.

Nothing of that sort for the Capitals. They leaked too many boundaries when the field was up and by the time their spinners came into the attack, the game had passed them by. Axar and Kuldeep did show what might have been capable of, had they had more runs in the bank, but that is perhaps the only thing DC can cling on to from today's display. And that sums it up.

Afeef: "Time for a special performance from birthday boy Rohit"

7:28pm Umpires Michael Gough and Ulhas Gandhe make their way out to the middle. The LSG fielders are already there, with the MI openers the last to stride out. Rohit and Kishan will open, and they have a crucial role to play in the powerplay. Stoinis will take the new ball. Kishan on strike, wide slip in place - here we go!

7:25pm The excitement is building. Mumbai are pretty much in must-win territory, and they will have to set the pace with the bat. There is uncertainty over how the pitch will play too and MI will have to assess it quickly and recalibrate, if required.

7:15pm Lots to dissect from the toss. LSG fans will be chuffed Mayank is back in the fold. Turner gets a gig too and he bolsters their middle order, while Kulkarni is an exciting prospect, who should come in when LSG bat. Mumbai, meanwhile, have brought Coetzee back, and his stock length could be useful on a ground with big boundaries.

Lucknow Super Giants XI: KL Rahul (c & wk), Marcus Stoinis, Deepak Hooda, Nicholas Pooran, Ashton Turner, Ayush Badoni, Krunal Pandya, Ravi Bishnoi, Naveen-ul-Haq, Mohsin Khan, Mayank Yadav

LSG bench: Arshin Kulkarni, M Siddharth, K Gowtham, Yudhvir Singh, Prerak Mankad

Mumbai Indians XI: Rohit Sharma, Ishan Kishan (wk), Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (c), Tim David, Nehal Wadhera, Mohammad Nabi, Gerald Coetzee, Piyush Chawla, Jasprit Bumrah

MI bench: Nuwan Thushara, Kumar Kartikeya, Naman Dhir, Shams Mulani, Dewald Brevis

7pm It's toss time. Hardik Pandya and KL Rahul are out in the middle, alongside Ian Bishop. Rahul gives it a flick. Heads calls Hardik but it comes down as tails. LSG will bowl first. Rahul says the wicket looks good and he wants to put the batters under pressure by putting them in. Adds that staying balanced is important, staying excited for the game and wanting to put on a show for the crowd.

Few changes for LSG - Quinton de Kock misses out. Arshin Kulkarni is in the team, as is Ashton Turner. Mayank Yadav is playing too. Says he has been tempted to throw Mayank in and that he has been pushing the medical team and support staff to get Mayank back on the field, and he hopes he can come back and bowl fast.

Hardik says he would have bowled first too, reckoning the pitch looks on the slower side. The thing they can focus on is having the basics covered and giving everything. The boys are up for it, he adds, and they want to focus on one game at a time. One change for MI - Coetzee comes back in for Wood. Signs off by saying that they have backed whoever has been a part of their eleven/twelve, although injuries and other factors have forced changes.

6:58pm All previous LSG-MI matches have been won by the team batting first. On a used pitch, will batting first be the way to go again? Toss in 2.

Azfer: "LSG should really give Arshin a chance, he might be a good asset for them" -- Seems like they heard you!

6:50pm Arshin Kulkarni and Ashton Turner have been handed their LSG caps. Rahul presented it to Kulkarni, while Stoinis did it for Turner. In the Mumbai camp, Tim David is doing the pre-match team talk in the huddle.

Pitch Report: The first thing Graeme Swann says is that the bowlers might be looking forward to bowl on this surface. Equidistant square boundaries - 66m to each side. 76m hit straight down the ground. It is a used pitch and 163 was defended on this strip previously. There is a little bit of grass but Aaron Finch does not reckon it will play much of a part, adding that he expects the pitch to be on the slower side, with a few bare patches also visible. There is some wind around too, and hitting against the wind could also be a consideration for the batters.

6:40pm First things first, there is significant optimism that Mayank Yadav, LSG's tearaway quick, could feature tonight. Morne Morkel said that the pacer had passed all fitness tests and was well in contention. If he plays, that will be a shot in the arm for LSG.

"Really Excited for this match as we are finally going to Witness Both Mayank Yadav and Suryakumar Yadav Playing the same match. I still believe both of them are one and only watching them play this match would prove me wrong !!" -- Looks like lots of hours are being spent on social media, Mustafa...

6:30pm Nine matches, three wins, six points, ninth place. This season has not gone to plan for the Mumbai Indians. The change in captaincy has not yet yielded the desired results and the five-time champions are now in danger of missing the playoffs for the third time in four years.

The Lucknow Super Giants have not had an amazing campaign either. But their fortunes are not as bad as Mumbai. Ten points from nine games is a respectable tally, and if they can string together a few wins from here, a playoff spot is still well within reach.

That is why this encounter promises to be fascinating. LSG, as things stand, are more comfortably placed and can afford a loss or two but they will know a drop-off now could be severely detrimental.

MI do not really have that option. They know this is pretty much last-ditch territory. They will, of course, not be eliminated mathematically, even if they lose tonight but they will be appreciative of the importance of momentum and the need to start winning.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of Match 48 of IPL 2024. We are back in Lucknow, where LSG did lose on Saturday but have a 3-2 record otherwise in 2024. Mumbai, on the other hand, have won on the road just once and are desperate for two points. Hop on, this should be fun!

11:47pm That brings us to the end of our coverage for tonight. Hope you enjoyed it as much as we loved bringing it to you. We will be back again tomorrow, when the Chennai Super Kings host the Punjab Kings at Chepauk. Until then, this is goodbye from all of us. Goodnight and take care!

Marcus Stoinis, Player of the Match: (On a fan poll saying he resembles the Hulk more than Tim David) I have had the nickname for longer. He (David) is a bit more hairy, like Big Foot (laughs). Nice to bowl with the new ball. As someone who is not quick, I can try to shape the ball. Did not expect to bowl three in the powerplay but nice to bowl. I thought the wicket was okay. We knew it was going to be slow. We could have pushed the envelope and scored a bit faster. If those partnerships went for 8-10 more balls, we would have done it more easily. (On his dismissal) It was a drag-down, wasn't it? After doing the hard work and doing the hard stuff, it was just disappointing to get out and leave it to someone else. This is is my third year, fortunate enough to have been here since day one, from before the auction. Have built a few close bonds with people. We are playing good cricket, and everything is good.

KL Rahul, Lucknow Super Giants captain: (On having flashbacks of last year's game against GT) A little bit, but we still had batters in the middle, experienced batters in KP and Pooran. It was a bit dry, but still, if they had put up 160, it would have been a competitive game. A team coming here, it takes time to adjust to the wicket. Our bowlers put pressure on them, and made the job of the batters easier. Always happy when you get those two points. We still need to get a few things right and hoping that we start gaining momentum at the back end. (On Mayank Yadav) I have not really spoken to him. He had slight pain in his side and after the first ball, he said that there was a bit of pain. Thought there was no need to risk it, he is still a young lad. It is not just the pace. This game, he showed he has more skills than bowling 150-plus. The more he plays, the more he will learn when to bowl what. Right now, we have given him a free hand to just enjoy himself and bowl what he wants.

Hardik Pandya, Mumbai Indians captain: (On losing wickets hurting them during their batting powerplay) Definitely, losing early wickets in the powerplay is tough to recover from. Where we needed the most, we could not do well. (On batters being under more pressure batting first because of the high scores everywhere) Not really, you still have to see the ball and hit. The wicket was good. The ball was there to be hit and we just missed, that sort of season for us so far. I have always believed that whenever you take to the field, sometimes you will be down, sometimes you will be up, and you have to fight. It looks difficult but there are a lot of things you can learn from this game. (On Wadhera) He has been fantastic, the way he batted against Rajasthan and tonight. He did fantastic last year as well. It was because of the team combination that he could not play early. Looking at his talent, he will play for a lot of years for Mumbai and for India eventually.

Justin Langer: We were bitterly disappointed with our last game. So to fight against MI and win against them, that brings a smile. Thrilled with that (win). (On the bowling) It was outstanding. I thought we had all bases covered. The first time we have taken early wickets (apart from Bangalore) and it set us up nicely. (On Mayank Yadav's injury) Looks like he is sore in the same spot. His rehab has been perfect. He has bowled pain-free the last week or so and has looked in great condition. We will have a scan and find out tomorrow. (On Stoinis) He has been a real match-winner. He took a good catch earlier as well. He is showing a good presence at the top of the order, which we demanded after the first few games. Match-winners (like him) are key to progressing in such tournaments. I have been blown away by the IPL and how tight it is, almost like a World Cup. Loved how we fought back tonight and that is a sign of a good team.

11:23pm Well, this was a slow burn. For the longest while, it felt as if the Super Giants would cruise to victory, especially when Stoinis was batting. Once he fell, though, a bit of panic crept in. Turner could not get going, and Pooran lacked his usual six-hitting touch too. Badoni's run-out further complicated matters but thankfully for the hosts, Stoinis had done enough of the heavy lifting earlier to give them that cushion.

While LSG could have been more clinical with the run-chase, take nothing away from the Mumbai Indians' bowling attack. They did not have many runs to defend, yet, they fought with all they had. Bumrah was brilliant, like he is on most days. Hardik also chipped in and picked up two crucial wickets. Coetzee, however, was a touch expensive and the spinners were also not very effective, and that let MI down, given they had absolutely no margin for error with the score they had put up.

How much will CSK miss Pathirana today? With PBKS winning the toss too, just wondering if it makes them favourites for today's game. PBKS stick with Rossouw over Livingstone.

No Shikhar Dhawan yet on this "hot and sweaty evening", as described by Ravi Shastri. Punjab Kings opt to bowl first. "Amazing stadium and crowd and excited to get ball in hand for early wickets," Curran says. "The confidence from the last game, we haven't had many wins but it was an important one. I think it is just about that fight and determination. Now that we have the ball, try to get into the Chennai batting. Same team."

Gaikwad: "Would've fielded too but looking at my toss winning percentage, most of my team members were prepared to bat knowing I would loss the toss (smiles). Always tough conditions defending here with dew but margin of win of 60-70 runs was good. We'll be missing Pathirana (niggle) and Tushar Deshpande (not well) as well. Shardul Thakur and Richard Gleeson will play."

A reminder this is Mustafizur Rahman's last game with CSK with national duty calling him. He has been a strong inclusion in the team this season, but with him gone next game onwards, one man who can step up is right-arm seamer Tushar Deshpande. Here's his story on how he has worked on his defensive bowling to try becoming the next 'Bravo'

6.40pm PBKS bowlers have conceded 200+ in IPL 2024 only once but can they do that against a batting unit led by a transformed Ruturaj Gaikwad? After having strike-rates of under 120 in his first four games of the season, Gaikwad has turned his batting around by scoring at over 155+ in his last five matches, including a century and a 98. More on that from Vishal Dikshit in the match preview.

Matthew: "Any team/s confirmed out of the playoffs yet? What's the permutations? " -- Not yet, there is a small chance that five teams could finish on 18 points from here. And remember, no team is completely eliminated yet.

6.30pm Punjab Kings never let us down when it comes to the IPL and thrillers, but somehow, they fall on the wrong side of the result more often. Even this season, that has been the story, with two uncapped Indians in the lower-middle order giving their batters some respectability but find themselves in a familiar position of eighth place.

But last game, they did the impossible, completing the highest successful chase in T20 history. Not just that, but their opening pair fired too, something they have been desperate for.

When they take the field today in Chennai, can they do more of the same against Chennai Super Kings? PBKS have a 4-0 record in their last four matches against CSK, and if they can get another win away, the points table will also open up miraculously. Welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage of match 49.

postText:
A thumping victory for PBKS who are somewhat turning into a bogey team for CSK. Three teams on 10 points in the middle, two on 12 and a few others lurking. The race to the playoffs spot is likely to get very close. It is going to be RR facing SRH tomorrow, and that promises to be another riveting clash. We'll be live nice and early, but till then, this is me Ashish Pant, signing off on behalf of Sreshth, Thilak and Raghav. Good night.

Harpreet Brar is the Player of the Match: It was a good wicket to bowl on. Even Rahul bowled very well. I have been playing for the last six years, and my confidence is also built up. I am playing with a lot of legends. I wanted to bowl on my strengths and the things happened. I don't think about wickets. My aim is to bowl lots of dot balls in my spell and the dot balls create the chances. When there is spin in the wicket, the bowler's confidence goes up

First up, the Punjab Kings captain Sam Curran Very happy. Anytime you come to Chennai and get two points, it is a huge feeling. Last year also we lostall our home games and won the away games. We are getting a hint of the formulas. Any team that can get momentum at the back-end is dangerous. We are quietly confident that we are coming up against them in a couple of days' time. [Toss] Pretty obvious, winning the toss was huge. KG Rabada set the tone wonderfully. We thought today we'll give him the new ball and he stormed in. [19th over to Chahar] Chahar has come back into the team really well. We tried something different in the 19th over. He showed confidence and to bowl to MS was great. The spinners were the pick of the bowlers. I bowled and got hit. The pace bowlers were going all the way, so thankfully it worked. This game is tough for the bowlers, we have got to be creative. [Next game also against CSK] We start 1-0 on them in a way. We had a tough early part. Trevs [Trevor Bayliss] is big on enjoying the win. Taking a lot of confidence. Winning helps with confidence. Jonny, KG, spinners were great

Presentation time

Sachin Garg: "Jam in the middle of the points table! Interesting phase to start now .. from CSK to PBKS ... a win here and there is going to cause a huge difference and yes...don't forget NRR!"

Stat alert: Punjab Kings are the second team to defeat Chennai Super Kings in five consecutive matches in the IPL. Mumbai Indians won five in a row vs CSK between 2018 and 2019.

Rilee Rossouw: We have to give credit to the bowlers. 160 was very gettable on that pitch. Jonny played well tonight, hope he takes that form into the tournament and gives us a good start. [Spin twins] We have that arsenal, the spin twins as well call them. They have been really really good. [Conversation with Bairstow] Pretty simple, just see the ball and hit the ball. Two batsman out there, playing with the freedom. [Reaction after getting out] Full toss wouldn't you be? Just focused in the zone, when the bad ball comes, was gutted to miss out. [Playoffs?] Never over till it's over. We have the belief that we can make the playoffs. Hopefully we can turn things around

Ruturaj Gaikwad: 50-60 runs short to be honest. When we were batting first, the pitch wasn't great, plus the dew as well. [Toss] I have practised a lot. I have tossed it in the match. I am winning in the practice, but not winning in the match. What to do. I am really under pressure at the toss, not at the game. [Dew] Very difficult. Even last game, we were quite surprised that we would win by that much margin. This is something we can't control. We can slightly bat better in the first innings. In the last 2 games, we tried our best to get 200-210. This pitch it was tough to get 180. [No Pathirana, Deshpande] It is a real problem. There are phases you want to get a wicket, and you have only two bowlers, plus the spinners are out of the question because of the dew. Can't do much.

11.27pm That is as comfortable a win for PBKS as any they've had this season. The win was set-up wonderfully well by the bowlers, who restricted CSK to just 162 for 7. In reply, Gleeson got the ball to move around early and snapped up Prabhsimran Singh. But once the dew settled in, bowling became trickier. Jonny Bairtow got into his stride and so did Rilee Rossouw with the duo adding 64 off 37 for the second wicket. Rossouw and Shashank Singh also had a quick stand before Curran and Shashank finished things off in the 18th over.

preText:
7:28pm The umpires make their way out to the middle amidst a cacophony of noise. A rapturous welcome for the SRH openers Abhishek and Head. Samson gives out some last-minute instructions in the RR huddle, and they now take up their respective fielding positions. Boult will take the new ball. Head on strike, wide slip and short extra cover in place - here we go!

Nik: "Boult vs Head and Abhishek should be exciting!!"

7:20pm The crowd is waiting in anticipation. There was a huge cheer when Cummins won the toss and an even greater cheer when he said SRH would bat first. Can the Royals silence this partisan crowd and tie the SRH batters down? First ball in about 10 minutes from now.

Trent Boult, Rajasthan Royals pacer: (On him and a lot of his RR teammates making their respective World Cup squads) Obviously exciting, you never take World Cup selection for granted. I speak on behalf of the guys, we are all very much looking forward to it. (On how he evaluates the season so far) It is a long season, seems to be cricket every day. We have been playing very good cricket. the results have spoken for themselves. It is all in the past now and the boys are now focussed on the next game and what is ahead of us. I count myself lucky to be involved in such a tournament. You see the smile on my face and how much I enjoy going out there to do my thing. (Secret to taking first-over wickets) There is no secret. If I knew it, I would tell you (smiles). It is going to be an interesting battle tonight. A side that is in incredible form, a strong batting unit and it is a challenge me and the bowling attack is looking forward to take on.

Soumya: "Considering the fantastic RR bowling line up, Jansen the batter maybe more important today than Jansen the bowler."

Jayant Isswani: "Graeme Swann forgot to ask for any changes in the team!" -- He did, actually. Similar team for RR. Parag did not field against LSG but is a part of their bowling-first eleven today, with Buttler likely to come in as their Impact Player. SRH, though, have made a big call, dropping Markram and including Jansen in his place.

Rajasthan Royals XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sanju Samson (c & wk), Riyan Parag, Dhruv Jurel, Rovman Powell, Shimron Hetmyer, R Ashwin, Trent Boult, Avesh Khan, Sandeep Sharma, Yuzvendra Chahal

RR bench: Jos Buttler, Tom Kohler-Cadmore, Shubham Dubey, Navdeep Saini, Tanush Kotian

Sunrisers Hyderabad XI: Travis Head, Abhishek Sharma, Anmolpreet Singh, Heinrich Klaasen (wk), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Abdul Samad, Shahbaz Ahmed, Marco Jansen, Pat Cummins (c), Bhuvneshwar Kumar, T Natarajan

SRH bench: Umran Malik, Mayank Markande, Aiden Markram, Sanvir Singh, Jaydev Unadkat

7pm It's toss time. Cummins and Samson are out in the middle. Cummins launches it up into the air. Samson calls heads but it comes down as tails. SRH will bat first. A massive roar goes up and Cummins has to wait before he can hear Swann's question. Says the crowd is pretty excited about them batting first and that their last two games have had a little bit of a bearing on their decision. Reckons it is a good wicket and that it is nice to come back home.

Samson says he would have batted first too but that they will have to be happy with whatever they are doing. Adds they have done both very well and wants to see what happens this game. Momentum is key, he quips and they want to stick to the patterns they have established so far.

Vince: "We've had some nice bowler-friendly games recently for the classic cricket fans... Now give us big hits and runs galore again!"

Pitch Report: It is a fresh pitch, never been used previously this season, says Graeme Swann. The square boundaries are not equidistant - 61m to one side, 64m to the other. 73m hit straight down the ground. Sunil Gavaskar says it is a pitch that birthday boy Brian Lara would have loved to bat on. There is going to be very little help for the spinners. The pacers might get a bit of carry because of how hard it is but not much. Gavaskar expects a "lot of runs". SRH, he says, have been taking the initiative every time they have played and could be on course for a score of 250 if they get going and bat first, unless the Royals "pull out some magic tricks."

6:45pm SRH have already scored 260 or more thrice this season. The Royals, meanwhile, have conceded a 200-plus score just once. This game, as Alagappan Muthu writes in his preview, is a contest between the best batting team in the IPL and the best bowling side.

Jim: "Manifesting SRH finally letting Glenn Phillips have a game today!" -- Looks unlikely, though, unless SRH decide to bring him in for Aiden Markram....

6:40pm The Royals have batted first in each of these sides' past five meetings, winning thrice. SRH, though, did win the last time these teams faced each other, with Abdul Samad and Glenn Phillips engineering a daring heist right at the end.

6:30pm Rajasthan Royals, the immovable object. Eight wins out of nine, 16 points on the board and with a foot and four toes in the playoff door. They have won when having to defend, they have won when having to chase, and they have won every time they have been on the road. The only game they have lost this season, was one they probably should have won too. That is how dominant they have been.

Now, onto the Sunrisers Hyderabad. An irresistible force, especially when they get it right. A powerhouse batting line-up, and a side capable of blowing any opposition out of the water. The last week, though, has not been very fruitful. They have lost twice in succession and have floundered while chasing, thus, raising a question mark over their chasing ability.

So, here we are, back in Hyderabad. The irresistible force versus the immovable object. A team that has a couple of questions to answer, against the side that has had no asterisks attached to it this season.

SRH will come hard at the Royals, of that there is no doubt and they will give it a proper rattle, despite what has happened in the last week. The Royals, like they have done all season, will stand there, undaunted by the challenge, and hoping to grow their aura of invincibility.

7.30pm Here come Sunil Narine and Phil Salt walking out with the Mumbai Indians' song "Aala Re" blaring out from the speakers. Their first task will be to negotiate Nuwan Thushara. There's a slip in place and four men up on the off side.

"If I am RCB, who should I be rooting for today?" Vikas, asking all the tough questions...

Aryaman d: "To answer Vikas's question KKR winning today should favour RCB . (yes i have prepared a scenario with all the outcomes of the rest of the matches so that RCB qualify) :) "

Sidat: "I know it sounds stupid to say but there have been downsides to Narine batting at the top. Yes he's been batting great, he's also been consistent with his runs, but him batting at the top means everyone else is pushed down the order by 1. And the likes of Shreyas and Venkatesh have struggled. Rinku hasn't faced many ball this IPL due to that and that has arguably cost him a place in the WC squad. But KKR have been winning games and Narine's confidence is flying high, so it's great for the team!"

Akshay: "If Rohit will be coming in as an impact sub it means MI is playing with 3 Overseas players only. Interesting."

Kamesh: "There could only be one reason why Rohit is probably coming in as an Impact Sub. Maybe he is carrying a slight niggle."

Apoorv: "Not sure if MI have the right balance here, they replaced Nabi, further weakening an already weak and one-dimensional bowling."

Ronny: "What happened to Sakariya? Had a great season for the Royals not too long ago. Broke into the Indian team. Don't see him playing much for KKR now."

Arun Prakash: "The impact player move from MI have been below par this season. They could've started with Rohit, that would've given a chance to use Nabi(if they need additional bowler), Naman Dhir (if early wickets fall in power play) or Romario Shepherd (if they needed a hitter to bail them out during the chase)"

7pm Hardik wins the toss and MI opt to bowl first. Rohit could come in as an Impact Player when they chase. Sakariya or Anukul could slot in as KKR's Impact Player in the second innings.

MI XI: 1 Ishan Kishan (wk), 2 Naman Dhir, 3 SKY, 4 Tilak Varma, 5 Hardik Pandya (capt), 6 Tim David, 7 Nehal Wadhera, 8 Gerald Coetzee, 9 Piyush Chawla, 10 Jasprit Bumrah, 11 Nuwan Thushara

Subs bench: Rohit Sharma, Shams Mulani, Shivalik Sharma, Dewald Brevis, Romario Shepherd.

KKR XI: 1 Phil Salt (wk), 2 Sunil Narine, 3 Angkrish Raghuvanshi, 4 Shreyas Iyer (capt), 5 Venkatesh Iyer, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Andre Russell, 8 Ramandeep Singh, 9 Mitchell Starc, 10 Vaibhav Arora, 11 Varun Chakaravarthy

Subs bench: Chetan Sakariya, Anukul Roy, Sherfane Rutherford, KS Bharat, Manish Pandey

Hardik: It looks quite tough for us but at the same time, we want to play good cricket. Good to be back home. Looks like a good track and it's a fresh wicket. We have not played on this surface. One change: Naman Dhir comes in place of Mohammad Nabi.

Shreyas: It's all about doing the small things right. The message is crystal clear: each individual knows his role and responsibility. Batting first, we're going with the same team.

6.50pm Wankhede. Short boundaries. Easy-paced bash-through-the-line pitch. Even a total of 190 will be below par, says Michael Clarke in the pitch report. Toss in ten minutes. Do stay locked in. For more analysis, stats, colour and insights follow Andrew Fidel Fernando's Live report.

Jeevan: "As a KKR fan, it has almost become frightening to watch matches against MI. We always just easily get blown away by them. I hope GG tries to bring in some confidence and we set the record straight."

6.45pm Shreyas Iyer has been on a rollercoaster ride. But KKR assistant coach Abhishek Nayar says the captain has been positive despite all the challenges and disappointments he's faced in recent months.

Mustafa Moudi : "Humble request to BCCI, please conduct a Tri-Series of RR, KKR and SRH. All the 3 matches among these sides were great thrillers !!"

Fabian Ananth: "MI can look at replacing Nabi with Shepherd, as Nabi's full bowling potential is not being utilised "

aariz: "Maybe Chetan Sakariya gets a chance today to replace Harshit Rana. He was pretty good last season for DC."

Hemant Noval: "Mark my words ! Surya is going to win this for MI single handedly."

6.40pm ICYMI: Harshit Rana has been suspended for one game after breaching code of conduct. KKR will also be without the other Rana - Nitish - who is working his way back from injury. How can KKR make up for Harshit's absence? ESPNcricinfo expert Wasim Jaffer reckons Chetan Sakariya can fill that void. Sudarshanan has also spotted Sakariya marking his run-up along with Mitch Starc

Samir Dave: "You got to give it to Guatam Gambhir for bringing the best out of thier team. But you got to also hail impact of Coach Chandrakant Pandit. His pedigree will be realised in time to come and what better day than today to show it. He is the local guy and has the know-how of every inch of this ground. It will come handy with all his insights. Match/Game/Ground Awareness is the key ! Game ON"

6.35pm Sudarshanan from the Wankhede: "Not much buzz that was there in earlier games. People are only trickling in whereas in earlier MI home games, people used to form queues from around 5:15-5:30pm. The word is that this game is also sold out, so we could still see a packed house by the time the game starts.

"On the field, Rohit Sharma is the only one having a net facing Shams Mulani and a throwdown specialist. The other MI and KKR players are yet to arrive as I type this. He's practising a fair few inside-out shots and the sweeps and reverse-sweeps."

Azfer: "My honest opinion about what Mumbai should do is that they should drop David as he is not having his best season and instead they should bring in Shepherd as he also gives bowling help as well" --- I don't see that happening, though. David is MI's designated finisher and has played a few cameos this season so far.

6.30pm Good evening, everyone. After 50 games this season, all ten teams are still in the race for the playoffs, including Mumbai Indians. Hardik Pandya's men are second from bottom, just above Royal Challengers Bengaluru on net run-rate. But they're still in the mix, and they will mathematically remain in the mix even if they lose to Kolkata Knight Riders this evening at the Wankhede.

KKR, meanwhile, are better placed than MI to reach the playoffs and a win against MI today will help them narrow the gap between them and table-toppers Rajasthan Royals. KKR, however, have struggled against MI at the Wankhede: just one win in ten games at this venue, as Vishal Dikshit lays out in the preview. Can KKR buck the trend and conquer Mumbai? I'm Deivarayan Muthu and I'll be joined by Himanshu Agrawal to bring you all the ball-by-ball action.

postText:
So this is how the points table looks at the moment: KKR are second, while MI are at the second-last spot. MI are mathematically alive, and just about; but realistically, they know they are all but done for this season. Many results have to go their way if they are to dream off a top-four finish. But anyway, this was KKR's (k)night, as Venkatesh bailed them out with help from Pandey. The IPL action moves to Bengaluru tomorrow, as two lowly-placed sides battle it out. Until then, see you, and goodnight!

Venkatesh Iyer is the Player of the Match for his 70: "Like a professional cricketer, I have to be flexible in how I can my pace my innings. This is the fourth or fifth time that Manish has padded up, but this time he got to bat! It was very important at that time [to rebuild]. Initially, I told him it will take time to adjust to the wicket. The ball was holding up, and it was a two-paced wicket. He was guiding me. I try to be a smarter cricketer... I thought at that situation, the team needed me. I'm a huge fan of Dada [Sourav Ganguly]. Went to ask him about my stance. It was a very fruitful conversation."

Shreyas Iyer: "We are [knocking at the door] at the moment. Lot of thinking would have gone behind that [had we lost today]. Just got to know about the stat [of KKR not winning at Wankhede for 12 years]... This Impact Player rule specifically helped us in this game. Manish has being eyeing an opportunity from the first game. We got to a commendable total. I told the boys that if we have got here, we can defend it. Spinners were unreal, absolutely spot on in executing their lines and lengths. Kudos to them! [Venkatesh] has been eagerly waiting to go out there and express himself. Happy for him!"

Time for the presentations

Varun Chakravarthy: "Extremely good feeling, because we haven't won at Wankhede for 12 years. It was a just a matter of one wicket [when David was batting]. There was dew, but somehow we controlled our emotions. Second innings there was not much help [for the spinners] because of the dew. The batters did tell that the ball is stopping and turning. But when I came on to bowl, I realised it wasn't stopping. Sunny [Narine] is a legend. This is a very special win because we were down and out in the first innings. The way Venkatesh and Manish pulled it back was great."

Prabir: "Too bad Bumrah didn't get to show his batting skills! I was looking forward to see him bat" --- With his form, you'd think he can swing the bat as much as the ball

Hardik Pandya: "Obviously we couldn't form partnerships and kept losing wickets. There are a lot of questions that will take time to answer. But for now, not much to say. Bowlers did a fantastic job on this track. The wicket got better if I'm not wrong. Dew came in the second innings. Will go through the game and see what we can do better. You keep fighting, that's what I keep telling myself. It's challenging, but you take the challenges."

James: "20 wickets fall in an IPL match. Not every day you see that" --- Only the fourth time in IPL history

11.14pm A comfortable win for KKR after it seemed a bit tricky when Suryakumar was depositing a few in the stands. MI needed another 50 from 28 balls when a set Suryakumar and David were at the crease. But the game turned thereafter; and David brought it down to 26 from 11, but Starc was helped by two full tosses resulting in wickets. Hang around with hopes of MI making the playoffs for the presentations.

Ashish Pant says hello from the Chinnaswamy: "Both teams had a slight taste of the Bengaluru traffic with the team busses stuck in traffic close to the venue. It rained for a couple of hours in Bengaluru last evening. No such threats today, though it does feel unusually humid. Virat Kohli had a long net session on the eve of the game, with a specific focus on spinners. He did get out a number of times but also hit a few into the stands much to the delight of few spectators in. Coming to today, it is expected to be another packed crowd. Most of the stands are already full, and there is a huge queue outside waiting to get in. Spencer and Vyshak marked their run-ups."

Tushar Verma: "Hello Srinidhi, whatever mathematical chanced you mentioned of RCB qualifying for playoffs, if anyhow they do qualify this from this position, it will be like a getting the trophy for us RCB fans. Yes, we live on such low expectations. It's an enduring task to be an RCB fan, but we live on as always. And as always, we will come back the next year carrying the same endurance. "

That apart, it's going to be Kohli vs Titans' spinners the subplot (again) in Bengaluru. Spin has been Kohli's nemesis in T20s for a few years now, but he scored an unbeaten 70 against one of the IPL's best spin attacks in their last match to keep RCB's hopes alive in the season. Abhimanyu Bose in his preview says with GT being a bowling-heavy team, they will need to revise their plans to end their losing streak.

6.30pm: Namaskara, everyone! Welcome to our live coverage of game 52 of the IPL, between Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium. Today's big question is, are RCB still in the mix? Yes, they are on a two-match winning streak and have six points from 10 games. They are at the bottom of the points table. But 14 points could keep them in the mix but at this stage, even 12 gives them a mathematical chance.

On the other hand, Titans have lost two of their last three games and need to pull up their socks sooner than later if they are to go up the ladder. They have eight points from 10 games and occupy the eighth position. Titans are the only side in IPL 2024 to not win two games in a row and that has kept them in the second half of the table. Can they find a way to stop RCB from making it three wins in a row? I am Srinidhi Ramanujam and will be joined by Alan Gardner to bring you all the live action. Oh, and it's good to be back on commentary.

postText:
11.10pm: That's a wrap from Bengaluru, but you know where to come tomorrow for Sunday's double-header. Thanks for all your comments. From myself, Srinidhi and Vairavan, it's goodnight and good luck. Byeeeeee!

11pm: Time for the presentations. RCB captain Faf du Plessis: "Been really good last few games, the way we've played with bat and ball. Aggressive with the bat, unbelievable in the field. [Assessment of conditions] There was more bounce in the wicket, we got that information and the bowlers were consistently really good. We dropped a catch but have been really consistent. Something around 180-90 would have been a good score, but we've seen the way the game has changed. Don't look at the scoreboard and play the way that we want to play. It was a bit nerve-racking, another wicket, another wicket. Probably not the best but you're trying to be positive, get your NRR up. It makes sense from that point of view but it gets to the point when you need to show a bit of calmness and composure - probably around four down, so some lessons to be learned from that."

Mohammed Siraj is Player of the Match for his powerplay burst and figures of 2 for 29: "I was actually sick since last night and wasn't going to play at all today, so this is great. When I got up this morning I thought it was better to rest but the almighty made me play. I kind of manifested it this morning because I envisioned it in a way that I would get Saha out like that, caught behind. I had been playing red-ball cricket for long and hadn't played with the white ball since the ODI World Cup. So my rhythm was missing a little bit when I came here. But it came back gradually as I worked and practised more and more."

10.50pm: Third win in a row for RCB, and they are up to seventh on NRR after completing their chase with more than six overs to spare. Titans lose again, and sink down into the lower reaches of the table. It was messy in the end, despite a record-breaking opening stand from Virat Kohli and Faf du Plessis, but the home side eventually gave their fans something to cheer - there haven't been too many opportunities at the Chinnaswamy this season - as well as keeping the top-four in view

Shubman Gill: [Setting target] "It depends on the wicket. First couple of overs you get a good idea and play according to that. I think 170-80 on this wicket would have been a good total. How we batted in the powerplay, and how they bowled, decided the game. We would have had one extra bowler but losing three wickets in the powerplay [changed planning]. Very important to start from zero in our next match and move on from this game. Learn from mistakes and not repeat them. All about winning from here on."

Dinesh Karthik: "Started with a cup of tea, then after four overs I had a cappuccino and thought I wouldn't be batting. Things happened and then I had to have a bat. [Approach] How to hit boundaries, basic cricketing skills come through. I backed myself to get the job done. The pitch was good to bowl on, having been under the covers there was a bit of moisture. Good toss to win but they bowlers did the job beautifully. The way Faf and Virat batted, I don't think they would have played the same shots batting first! [Swapnil advice] Play for the one that comes in. Said the sweep is a good option, but commit to it."

3:27pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the players. No surprises with respect to CSK's opening combination. It will be Rahane and Gaikwad. Rahane could do with a few runs here. Rabada has the new ball for the hosts. Rahane on strike, slip in place - here we go!

3:22pm The sun is shining, the mountains are visible in the distance, the ground looks pristine and the stage is set. CSK, remember, have lost five on the bounce against the Punjab Kings, and that means CSK now hold just a 15-14 head-to-head advantage in the IPL over the Kings.

Sarthak: "Sorry for not knowing, but where are Fizz and Pathirana? They seemed to be doing pretty good for CSK..." -- Mustafizur has gone back for international duty. As for Pathirana, Gaikwad, at the last game, mentioned he had a niggle.

Samarth: "CSK might not need Rizvi with this line up. So they can play yet another bowler in the second innings. " -- That looks like the plan. Perhaps it will be a toss-up between Mukesh and Simarjeet, given they already have three spinners in Jadeja, Moeen and Santner.

krish: "No comment on deepak chahar? Is he already fit to play?" -- Chahar is not part of the eleven and he is not a part of the subs bench either. And Stephen Fleming, a few days ago, said that Chahar's injury was not looking good. Chahar has also stayed back in Chennai and is waiting on scan reports.

Vismay: "Good to see Santner get a game. He's too good a player to be on the bench."

Chennai Super Kings XI: Ruturaj Gaikwad (c), Ajinkya Rahane, Daryl Mitchell, Shivam Dube, Ravindra Jadeja, Moeen Ali, MS Dhoni (wk), Mitchell Santner, Shardul Thakur, Tushar Deshpande, Richard Gleeson

CSK bench: Sameer Rizvi, Mukesh Choudhary, Simarjeet Singh, Shaik Rasheed, Prashant Solanki

Punjab Kings XI: Jonny Bairstow, Rilee Rossouw, Shashank Singh, Sam Curran (c), Jitesh Sharma (wk), Ashutosh Sharma, Harpreet Brar, Kagiso Rabada, Rahul Chahar, Harshal Patel, Arshdeep Singh

PBKS bench: Prabhsimran Singh, Harpreet Bhatia, Tanay Thyagarajan, Vidwath Kaverappa, Rishi Dhawan

3pm Gaikwad and Curran, two former CSK teammates, are out in the middle for the toss. Danny Morrison says it is great to be back in Dharamsala. Curran gives the coin a twirl. Gaikwad calls tails, and heads it is. Gaikwad has lost another toss. Punjab Kings will field first. Says they fancy their chances of chasing here. Same team for them. Adds they have had two good wins and he expects the conditions to be pretty even, so it is about batting, bowling and catching well.

Gaikwad says it is important to focus on the process and do the little things right. They do not look at the opposition and the track record, and want to rectify what went wrong in the last game. There have been lots of forced changes this season and that is why they have had to tinker almost every game. Losing five matches despite losing ten tosses is a positive. Santner has come into the team in place of Mustafizur, who has gone back for international duty.

2:55pm CSK captain Ruturaj Gaikwad has lost nine out of ten tosses so far. If he were to win it today, though, what will he want to do? Last year, there were two games played at this venue, with the team batting first winning one and losing the other. Toss in 5.

Afeef: "Livingstone's knock of 94 against DC last season on this ground is one of my favourites of the IPL. Rossouw was playing for DC against PBKS in that match and made 82, now he is playing for PBKS."

2:50pm These two sides have met twice previously at this venue. One was, of course, that special night in 2010 (for those of a CSK persuasion). The other was a lower-scoring game in 2012, wherein the Punjab Kings (Kings XI Punjab then) triumphed by six wickets. Of those who played in 2012, only two (MS Dhoni and Ravindra Jadeja) are still with CSK in a playing capacity.

Pitch Report: The square boundaries are not huge - 62m to one side, 64m to the other side. It is a 75m hit straight down the ground. It has a layer of grass and that is "good", says Brian Lara. He adds that whenever there is grass in India, the fast bowlers do get a bit of help. A few cracks here and there but he does not expect it to play a part, and reckons the spinners might struggle. A "wonderful ground" for the batters, and he feels plenty of runs will be scored.

2:40pm The HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala is one of the most picturesque venues in the world. However, it will be a bit of a step into the unknown for both teams, given this ground has hosted just two T20s in the last seven years. All that and much more, including the Punjab Kings' ongoing five-match winning streak against CSK, in Hemant Brar's preview.

2:30pm Dharamsala. Punjab Kings versus Chennai Super Kings. Sunday afternoon game. CSK, in the midst of an indifferent run, desperately needing a win; Punjab riding a recent wave of success and confidence. This is IPL 2010 IPL 2024.

14 years ago, CSK arrived in the foothills of the Himalayas, knowing nothing but a victory would suffice. With about two overs left, they seemed to have missed the semi-final bus. But then, MS Dhoni turned up, and that evening in Dharamsala changed CSK forever.

In 2024, there is a different man in charge. He, like Dhoni, is waiting for that real breakthrough as CSK captain, and in surroundings very familiar to CSK, he will have a chance to reach out for it and grab it.

Punjab, at this stage, are two points worse off than CSK. But a win, and they will go level, having played the same number of games. While a case can be made that CSK can probably afford to lose another, the Kings do not have that luxury. They have to, realistically, win all four remaining games and then see where it takes them (although there is a slight mathematical thread they can still cling on to).

So, this is it. The kind of high-stakes, high-jeopardy game the IPL usually throws up in its final league quarter. Margins will be fine, the room for error perhaps finer. Neither side, unlike CSK in 2010, will definitively qualify today nor be eliminated, but if these teams want to make the top four, neither can really lose this either.

postText:
5:16pm That innings didn't really go anywhere. Gaikwad and Mitchell bossed the powerplay and at that stage, it seemed CSK were on course for a 200-plus score. Gaikwad, though, fell in the eighth over, with Dube being dismissed off the very next ball. That set CSK back and they just could not recover.

Jadeja played a handy knock to get CSK past 160 but a lot of their batting, both in terms of execution and their planning, left a bit to be desired. The decision to hold Dhoni back for so long was also perplexing.

As for Punjab, everything they tried post the first time-out came off. Chahar set the ball rolling, with Harshal then coming into his own through the middle overs and at the death. Arshdeep and Rabada were expensive but given the power CSK had, the hosts will be thrilled to have restricted them to 167.

That said, there is just a little in it for the bowlers. The odd ball was holding, while a few skidded on. If CSK have enough on the board is another matter altogether, but we could be in for a tricky run-chase, especially if there are early wickets. Join us in a bit for the second innings.

Harshal Patel: I definitely misjudged the wicket (earlier when I said it was a good track), it was a bit on the drier side. The ball that we hit on the hard length, it was not going off fast. It is not stopping but it is definitely a slow wicket. (On the celebration after getting Dhoni out) I have too much respect for him to celebrate when I get him out. One of the advantages of playing a day game is that the square is rough. If you hit the square hard, then the ball reverses. It was starting to reverse and that makes it difficult for the batters to hit it. (On the slower yorker) I was not really confident with those initially. I have been working on them consistently. It is all about feel, no real technique. More you bowl it, the better you get. I have been practicing it in the nets and it usually gives you great results (in matches if you get it right).

postText:
7:30pm That will be all from us for this game. The IPL action does not stop, with the Kolkata Knight Riders and the Lucknow Super Giants going at it in Lucknow. Join Sreshth for all the action from what promises to be a thriller. Until next time, from me (Shashwat), Ranjith and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, this is goodbye. Take care, folks!

Ravindra Jadeja, Player of the Match: (On the pitch) It was a day game, so the wicket was slow. As usual, it was expected because it was so hot. (On the batting innings) We had a good powerplay but did not get partnerships in the middle overs. I was trying to build a good partnership to then tee off at the end. (On their bowling performance) The fast bowlers bowled well in the powerplay. Tushar got two important wickets and then Mitch and me did the job in the middle overs. It (the pitch) always seems flat in the powerplay. But when the ball gets old, the ball does not always come on. When playing at a new venue, you don't know how much it will turn or stop. We thought we were 15-20 runs short but we did not bowl loose balls in the powerplay and the middle overs. My role as a batter is to build partnerships and then play the big shots towards the end. Sometimes, when we lose wickets in the powerplay, we do not get momentum. In the matches we win, we play all phases well.

Ruturaj Gaikwad, Chennai Super Kings captain: (On losing the toss again) After you win the game, everyone says good you lost the toss but it does matter to me (smiles). Everyone believed that the wicket was slow and that it was coming off slow. There was low bounce too. Just the start we got, we could have pushed to 180-200. We lost wickets in consecutive balls and then felt 160-170 was probably ten odd runs short. But the way it played in the second innings, it was par. (On Simarjeet's pace) I don't know what he is doing but in the pre-season we had, he was bowling at around 150s. We had Deepak, Shardul, Tushar plus Pathirana and Fizz, so he did not get too many changes. Nothing is late, he got a game today. We were thinking of sending an impact batter but we thought the impact batter would score 10-15 runs but the bowler might get us 2-3 wickets. (On the win) A sigh of relief with the injuries we had. Not even sure about who was going to play on the morning of the match, so really happy with that (the win).

Sam Curran, Punjab Kings captain: I thought we bowled really well as a group. Rahul Chahar bowled really well, and the way Harshal Patel finished off. We were happy as a group at the half-way stage but unfortunately, it was not meant to be. We thought it (the pitch) was going to be slightly quicker, have more bounce. It was a bit slower but it was similar throughout the game. We have a couple of days off and then we play against RCB. We have to move on and keep fighting hard.

Tushar Deshpande: Very happy today because it was a low-scoring game. This was the game we wanted to win badly. (On how he felt coming back from illness) I tried my best to play the last game but couldn't. It was in my mind that I wanted to give my best. It was a crunch game. At high altitude, the ball does something and my job was to take wickets. (On the pitch) It was a bit slow if we bowled into the pitch. We knew if we hit those lengths, it was tough to play horizontal shots.

7:06pm A clinical performance with the ball, and 167, which did not seem many at the half-way mark, was plenty in the end. Credit for that has to go to CSK's new-ball pairing of Deshpande and Santner. The latter kept things tight, while the former got the ball to jag around, picking up Bairstow and Rossouw in the same over.

Jadeja then spun a yarn in the middle overs, bagging three wickets, with Simarjeet blasting batters out at the other end. The pair combined for five wickets and those scalps firmly derailed the Punjab Kings' run-chase.

Speaking of Punjab, they will not want to see this batting display a lot of times. The intent to counter-attack after two early wickets was refreshing but that soon reached alarming and needless proportions, especially in the middle overs. Prabhsimran was their top scorer and while he was at the crease alongside Shashank, the Kings seemed in control. Once that partnership was broken, though, things fell apart.

7.29pm We're ready to begin. Phil Salt is in terrific form but averages only 13 away from home this season. He'll face Marcus Stoinis. Stoinis bowled three powerplay overs last game.

Deo: "Not sure why LSG spent so much money on Joseph as a net bowler. One game doesn't do justice to his talent."

7.25pm The last set of groundstaff members make their way out. We're just five minutes from the start now. This is the last home game for LSG too, so they'll hope to give the home fans a farewell gift.

Harsh: "Where is Nitish Rana? without a doubt he will be a bigger match winner than Ramandeep." -- He was injured at the start of the season and KKR don't want to make changes right now. Ramandeep has also impressed parallelly with 83 runs in 48 balls in his limited chances lower down. I think if Nitish returns, it'll be in Raghuvanshi's place.

7.15pm Salt and Narine have helped KKR keep the best powerplay run-rate (11.2) of all teams this season. But Thakur and Mohsin have a knack of striking in the powerplay with five wickets apiece in that period. Lucknow surfaces are always a bit tricky, not as true as a Kolkata or a Mumbai, so the powerplay will be important. Remember it wasn't long back that KKR were 57 for 5 batting first against MI.

Mustafa: "Since LSG have got a chance to meet Gambhir (again), they must personally tell him thanks for scouting Mayank Yadav for them. He might not play more matches this season but can be the X Factor from next season and might be retained for a very small price since he might remain UNCAPPED until the next season !!"

Vismay: "Pitches and players are getting tired. Seems like those days of 250 runs are gone."

Ammad: "looking forward for some fireworks from both teams as this is a red soil surface"

KKR: P Salt, S Narine, V Iyer, S Iyer, Rinku Singh, A Raghuvanshi, A Russell, Ramandeep Singh, M Starc, H Rana, V Chakravarthy.
Impact: Anukul, Pandey, Vaibhav, Bharat, Rutherford

LSG: KL Rahul, M Stoinis, D Hooda, N Pooran, A Turner, A Badoni, K Pandya, R Bishnoi, N Ul Haq, Mohsin Khan, Y Thakur.
Impact: Kulkarni, M Siddharth, Gowtham, Yudhvir, Padikkal.

7pm toss Rahul and Iyer in the middle with Nick Knight. Lucknow Super Giants opt to bowl.

KL Rahul: I'm not the best reader of the wicket, we just like chasing. (Challenges) Different every game. We've adapted well on the two pitches here and travelled well too. Individual performances too in a competition like this. Everyone's put their hands up. (His highest strike-rates in IPL 2024) There's been a lot of talk about strike-rates and the format is changing. Even 220 is now safe. It is evolving. (Team plans) Quinton was injured in the last game, but we are staying with the same team. Yash Thakur will play."

Shreyas Iyer: "We would've bowled too but this is six in a row [losing toss]. Last game gave us tremendous confidence defending 170 with just five bowlers. There's a lot of self belief and that is important at this stage. (Today's plans) Depends how the wicket plays. We are batting first so we start with the same XI. After that, we'll see, hopefully we don't have to get our impact player too early this time. (Starc's performance) Big confidence for us. He just wasn't able to execute before but he executed in the scenario in the last game. He has a big character and I was happy for him. (One more game to qualify?) It is important to stay in the moment and seize the present."

The way the CSK vs PBKS game is going, LSG will slip to fourth by the time this game starts. If they lose by a big margin to KKR, they could even slip to fifth.

Pitch and dimensions report: Bit of an imbalance in the ground dimensions. One side is 61m square, the other is 68m. This is the third time this red-soil strip is being used, and there's a hint of green grass, but also some bare patches. Expectations are that the pitch will slow down at some point. Aaron Finch reckons 190-200 is the score to aim."

LSG suffered a blow after the Mumbai game when they learnt that Mayank Yadav's abdominal injury has resurfaced. He's been all but ruled out of IPL 2024.

Can the Lucknow surface cause problems for high-flying KKR? Batting first, KKR have been explosive, and in the three games they've chased, all chases were completed inside 17 overs. Sruthi Ravindranath explores more in the match preview.

6.30pm After ten games apiece, both Lucknow Super Giants and Kolkata Knight Riders are on the right side of the points table and are in contention for top-two finishes. But with top-four qualification not yet secured for any IPL 2024 team, neither side can really breathe easy even if they've had strong campaigns. Just one defeat can trigger a slide in this competition, and that's something they cannot afford. They both come into the game with wins over Mumbai Indians, so let's see which side can continue their winning run.

postText:
That's it from us today. Hope you all enjoyed our coverage. This is Srinidhi signing off on behalf of Sreshth, Ranjit and Chandan. Stay hydrated and good night!

Shreyas, KKR captain: "The last six matches in the dressing room there has been havoc, team-mates are coming in and asking what's happening, we are losing tosses, but we are winning games that's what matters. To be honest, we don't assess the total from the first few overs. Anything close to 200 is a great score, whatever we got after that was extra. Great start by both openers, they have been phenomenal. We have to be flexible with left-right combination, bowlers have to change their approach with this, as this plays into bowlers' mind. [on uncapped players] It's all about freedom, to go out and express. Their mindset is positive. Majority of the time, they have been good. [on Narine] He was splendid. The start from openers have been great. Pure bliss. We just want to keep continuing the momentum so that we get to the great total and be optimistic."

Narine, player of the match: "I think the most important thing is starting well. Support staff have been backing me. It's been working for me, hope it works for the rest of he tournament. It's about picking what you are gonna do on that particular day with your strengths, you have to be smarter. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. [on bowling with Chakravarthy] It's going very well with Varun, he is picking wickets, making my job easier. He is a hard worker."

Rana: "The only thing was we didn't want to leave anything behind; we just wanted to qualify [for the playoffs]. Our coaches asked us to bowl the suitable lengths on this surface - hit the hard length, and don't try too much. That is where I my focus was, and that is what benefitted me. I have concentrated a lot on bowling, as to whether I can do something else. I've talked to a few people, and have myself tried to know what I can do better. Russell taking wickets is extremely helpful - when he takes wickets, it helps tilt the momentum on our side."

Rahul, LSG captain: "Lot of runs. Poor performance overall. It was a big total. Like I said, It's a poor performance with both bat and ball. Narine in powerplay puts a lot of pressure. Our bowlers couldn't handle this pressure. That's how the IPL is. You will come against good players and that's when you will be tested. Wicket is very good. There is a bit of bounce if you bowl hard length. It wasn't a bad pitch. 235 was 20-30 runs were above par. Our batting was poor. We prepare in advance, we talk about the opposition batters, trying to see what kind of plans we need to come up with. We need to execute it when we come here, but we didn't, we made a couple of mistakes against Sunil and anyone who strikes well. Once we go back to dressing room, we move on from this game and see where we went wrong. Last home game, we are on the road for the next few games, we need to be little bit more fearless."

11.17pm What an all-round performance from KKR! They win by 98 runs in Ekana and move to the top of the table. Narine's onslaught and a few handy cameos took the visitors to 235 for 6, the highest score at this venue. Barring Stoinis, LSG couldn't find a batter who could get going. Russell's two wickets to dismiss Pooran and Stoinis were crucial to turn the game around. Varun, Narine, Rana all chipped in to event.

MI still not likely to progress but their win has opened up the tournament. DC will hope to further that by beating RR tomorrow while the visitors, sitting pretty at No. 2, will look to seal their playoffs berth. See you then. Thanks for joining us tonight. From my fellow commentator, Hemant Brar, and our scorers, Thilak Rama and M Venkat Raghav, it's goodnight.

Abdul Nasir: "SRH whole team 18 boumdaries. SKY alone 18 boundaries. The major difference."

Suryakumar Yadav, POTM: I've been doing this after very long time. After 14th December this is the first time I fielded for 20 overs and batted for 18. But I'm alright. I feel it was the need of the hour for me to win. Three wickets were down and I needed to play till the end. Knew that dew was heavy and I had to bat till the seam came off. Traditional shots came from the Mumbai school of arts. I knew what to do when the ball was seaming and then brought out all the shots which I practice. I feel the intent would've been the same. As overs would've passed it'd been easier and I'd have gone big but like how I did today.

Hardik Pandya, MI captain: I don't know the mathematical situation we need to go through but happy with how we went today. Gave 15-20 runs extra but batting was excellent. My bowling - I do the stuff I do. I like bowling good areas and see how it goes. Today it was nipping around and that worked. The wickets Piyush took are guys who can take the game away. He asked to long from the shorter side but had to adjust. In T20s, more than change-ups consistency is important, which PC was today, and found success with. SKY was unbelievable. More than him getting runs, him putting so much pressure on bowlers that even other batters get loose balls. He breaks you. He's evolved. Lucky to have him in my team. Hope to have many more such innings.

Mustafa Moudi : "After SRH's defeat tonight, KKR's chances of ending in Top 2 has very high. All they need now is to win a game out of them next 3 and their high NRR will take them to Top 2 with at least 18 Points and a Healthy NRR!!"

Tilak Varma: Initially it was really tough. We were struggling and decided to play with the straight bat. Play it like Tests or ODI knowing we have a 360-degree batter. I was really shocked when SKY took on Marco Jansen. From there it was just going on. It's a long season, so we'll be getting slow and seaming wickets, gotta prepare for everything. Mentally we were challenging each other and playing it with the discipline of Tests. I wanted to just play the situation. I kept my intent, walking in and playing with a straight bat, but while keeping my scoring options open. Then you saw what happened - the Surya bhai show. At that moment, he was batting well. I thought he deserved 100 and gave him the strike. There was no talk about him limping or anything.

Pat Cummins, SRH captain: (Total) Probably a couple short. Defending here at Wankhede you want as much as possible. We felt a little bit unders but still felt we were in the game. There was a bit there in the wicket early. You saw in our batting innings that the wicket had a bit in it till the 10-12 over mark, so felt we were in the game in the chase. (On the sub) Having Sanvir out there got us to 170 rather than 150, which would've had us lose no matter who's in the side. Ideally we'd have had a pacer but wouldn't have made too much of a difference. We obviously wanted to win. It's T20 cricket, doesn't always work out that way. Came against a good side, particularly SKY. We like playing at homem done well there so far. Looking forward to what's ahead of us. Hopefully a few more fireworks. (Harsha says think you gave us an insight on how the pitch will be) I'll have no say in the surface, we'll see how it goes.

11:12pm It might be too late to reignite the campaign but that's a great win for the hosts. Far from ideal for SRH who now sit on fourth as many points (12) in as many games as CSK and LSG. The chase started with a lot of promise for them. The ball was hooping and seaming everywhere but they didn't find the control, gave away too many wides. The wickets came by but MI got away. Bhuvi and Cummins struck. But then SKY and Tilak came together, soaked in the pressure, then let dew and the softening ball mitigate conditions. SKY taking on Jansen helped. They coasted through the middle overs. The repertoire of shots from SKY was out there. He limped a bit and experienced a bit of pain but managed to keep at it and, with Tilak for support, got the century and took his team home.

6.45pm Who has the highest strike rate in the death overs in IPL 2024? If you're guessing Andre Russell, Heinrich Klaasen or Dinesh Karthik, you'd be wrong. The most destructive batter at the finish this season is DC's Tristan Stubbs. More on him via former South Africa left-arm spinner Robin Peterson, who is now Stubbs' coach in domestic cricket.

RR dropped to No. 2 after five weeks at the top of the points table, but it has still taken a lot to beat them this season: Gujarat Titans managed it by hitting a last-ball boundary, and Sunrisers Hyderabad denied RR two runs off the final ball in their previous game. All this and more in Sreshth Shah's preview for the day. But can RR stop Jake Fraser-McGurk?

We are into the 56th match of the season, and yet neither has any team officially qualified for the playoffs nor is any side ruled out yet. But that could finally change today - after 80% of the round-robin games - if Rajasthan Royals beat Delhi Capitals, as RR would make it through to the last four. However, if DC manage to pip RR and thus remain afloat, it could just tighten the mid-table traffic further. And who is to say that (Royal Challengers) Bengaluru aren't part of it when it comes to traffic?! This is Himanshu saying hello for the evening, with Ekanth set to join me soon.

Suraj: "Who is Vijayakanth Viyaskanth?" He is a rookie Sri Lankan leg-spinner and was signed as replacement for Wanindu Hasaranga. From 33 T20 games, he has 42 wickets at 18.78 and an economy of 6.76 an over. Viyaskanth did well for MI Emirates at ILT20 earlier in the year

Here's Krunal Pandya speaking ahead of the game: A tough loss [vs KKR]. Not much in terms of preparation, yesterday the practice session got washed. A more of a mental switch on [for this game]. It's been close to two months in the tournament. We want to rectify our mistakes and keep doing what we have been doing in the tournament. [On SRH] They are very good batting side, they come very hard. We have to be on top of the game and can't take it lightly. We just have to win those small battles, that's every ball, every over. My role it to contain the batters. My role has been simple as a bowler. 6.50pm Pitch report from Mathew Hayden and Sanjay Manjrekar: Pitch no 2 being used, the same one where there was a record-breaking score [by SRH against MI]. This pitch has its own stardom. There is no mini boundary, just a difference of three metres here and there. Boundaries are a little supportive of the spinners. It is the height of the Indian summer. It's like walking into a clay oven. Rock hard pitch, really dry, still feels warm when you touch it. The head has opened up the tiny cracks. Hayden says he will be surprised to see a record-breaking score. The bowlers will use their cutters and Hayden reckons 200 will be par. 6.45pm The other thing to keep a close eye is the weather. The practice session on the eve of the game was cancelled due to rain and thunderstorms, and while it is clear at the moment, there could be a disruption later in the evening. Will that change the way how the two teams shape up? We'll know in a bit.

6.40pmIt's no secret that runs have flowed in Hyderabad this season. This was the venue which made IPL 2024 as big in terms of runs with SRH slamming a record-breaking 277 in their first match here. In eight innings in Hyderabad this season, teams have scored 200 or more five times, and hit 92 sixes. That's where SRH will hope to have the edge over LSG. SRH have hit the most sixes in the powerplay this season, 41 to LSG's 20, while going at a run rate of 11.04 as compared to LSG's 8.48. In the death overs, they have hit 36 sixes, again the most, while LSG's 16 sixes are the fewest in that phase. This and a lot more in the preview.

6.30pm IPL S17E57. Hello and good evening. Today we have Sunrisers Hyderabad taking on Lucknow Super Giants in Hyderabad. Two teams, with the same number of points, trying to get out of the mid-table scrum and give their playoffs chances a boost. It's a high-stakes clash. There are four sides on 12 points at the moment: CSK, SRH, DC and LSG. The team that wins goes to third position on the points table, ahead of CSK, but the one that loses will have another dent on their NRR, which is not ideal in the business end of the tournament. I am Ashish Pant, and will soon have Andrew Miller joining me as we bring to you all the info from what's shaping up to be a riveting clash.
